Suite unchanged at 22 of 22 green.

WALDELFE_DARK RE-TAKEN ON ITS OWN BBOX (38x99+752+359, cropped 120x170+712+330 at 500%), and the verdict row 766 declined to give is now available: THE ELF IS NOT AN INSTANCE OF THE POSE COLLAPSE. It renders as a thin vertical stick -- no torso width, no arms, a small blob for a head -- WITH ANIMATION OFF. Under animation the same stick bends to a diagonal, which for DRF1_ATTACK_SPECIAL01 (a lunge) is plausible motion of an already-broken mesh. A defect visible in the --creatures-noanim control cannot be caused by the variable the control removes, which is the same reasoning that cleared the wolf in row 768. Row 766s fix is not implicated and is not re-opened. UNLIKE THE WOLF, THE FRAMING WAS NEVER AT FAULT HERE: the elfs diff bbox sits inside the old 160x200+690+310 window, so row 766s capture was valid, just too small to read at 300%. The correction row 768 raised about WALDELFE_DARK is therefore itself narrowed -- the earlier image was honest, only under-magnified. CORROBORATED BY A NUMBER ALREADY IN HAND AND MISREAD AT THE TIME: row 766s probe measured this rigs REST bone bounding box as 9.89 x 18.91 x 107.17. That is 107 units tall and under 10 wide -- a stick at BIND, before any clip is applied. Compare BEAR at 109.53 x 196.57 x 127.19, which renders correctly. The reading was on screen during row 766 and I treated it only as a scale reference for the animated comparison instead of noticing the aspect ratio was already impossible for a humanoid. NEXT QUESTION, and it is NOT animation: why does this mesh bind to a degenerate skeleton. Candidates are the bone rest chain for this entry, the mesh_weights bone_map pairing (WALDELFE_DARK is a 90-bone rig, and row 763 already found it is the model whose clip leaves 5 ponytail bones undriven), or the skin bind array. The instrument to use is the rest bbox itself, swept across the corpus: any mesh whose bind-pose bone bbox has an implausible aspect ratio is a candidate, and that sweep costs one pass and needs no rendering. Suite unchanged at 22 of 22 green; no code changed for this row.

THE REST-BBOX SWEEP REFUTES ROW 769. Swept all 124 creature meshes the spawn tables name, using bind_poses() bone origins -- no clip, no render. WALDELFE_DARK is NOT degenerate: at slenderness 0.092 (smallest extent over largest) it sits in the middle of the humanoid pack -- NOBLE_FEM 0.092, PRIESTESS 0.093, dryadin_01 0.097, PRIEST 0.103, SOLDIER 0.105, NOBLE_MAL 0.114. A thin bind bbox is simply what a humanoid with arms at its sides measures, and row 769s "a stick at BIND, before any clip is applied" was an inference from ONE rigs numbers with no population to compare against. Withdrawn. WHAT THE SWEEP DOES SHOW IS AN AXIS DIFFERENCE. Every humanoid peer measures (X 16-30, Y 6-8, Z 63-73): narrow axis Y. WALDELFE_DARK measures (X 9.9, Y 18.9, Z 107.2): narrow axis X, with the broad horizontal extent on Y. That is a 90-degree rotation about the vertical relative to every other humanoid in the set, so this mesh is presented EDGE-ON to the isometric camera while its peers present their broad side -- which is exactly what produces the stick-thin silhouette photographed in rows 765/766/769, and it is present with animation OFF, consistent with row 769s one surviving conclusion (not an animation defect). It is also 107.2 tall against a peer range of 63-73, i.e. ~1.5x, which is a separate scale question this row does not settle. THE METHOD LESSON, third framing-class error in a row: row 769 read one rigs aspect ratio as impossible without measuring what possible looks like. The sweep cost one pass and no rendering, and it was the instrument row 769 itself named -- running it BEFORE writing the conclusion would have prevented the claim. An outlier needs a distribution, not an intuition. NEXT: whether the 90-degree difference is authored (a per-model facing the world must apply, like the 90-Z alignment bone row 609 found between __Root and Bip01 on model 589) or a decode error in this entrys root chain. Row 609s finding makes the authored explanation the stronger prior and it is checkable from the bone names alone. No code changed for this row; suite unchanged at 22 of 22 green.

CONFIRMED AND ATTRIBUTED. The 90-degree difference row 770 measured in WALDELFE_DARKs bind bbox is AUTHORED, and it is row 609s alignment bone. Root chains above Bip01, local rest as XYZ euler degrees: Waldelfe_dark = __Root[0,0,0] > Root[0,0,+90] > Bip01[0,0,-90], net 0. PRIEST, SOLDIER, NOBLE_FEM and PRIESTESS all = __Root[0,0,0] > Bip01[0,0,-90], net -90. So the elf carries an EXTRA bone named Root, +90 about Z, sitting between __Root and Bip01 and cancelling Bip01s -90 -- leaving this rig facing 90 degrees off every humanoid peer. That is exactly the extent difference row 770 measured (narrow axis on X where peers are narrow on Y) and it is the same bone row 609 identified on model 589 as the coordinate-alignment bone that CLIPS HAVE NO NODE FOR. Row 609s prior was correct and this is a second independent sighting of it, now tied to a visible symptom. NOT A DECODE ERROR: the rotation is in the file, so under canonical-first the port must REPRODUCE it, not correct it. The open question is therefore not "why is our elf rotated" but "what does retail apply on top" -- either retail composes something above __Root that we do not, or retail draws this creature facing 90 degrees off too and the silhouette is faithful. That is answerable only against retail, not from the file, and is the right place for the next measurement. CONSEQUENCE FOR ANIMATION, and it is the load-bearing one: because no clip has a Root node, ModelView.build_animation binds no track to it and it keeps its rest -- so the alignment survives animation and the elfs facing is stable, which matches every capture taken. Nothing here reopens rows 766 or 767. The chain of retractions that led here is worth reading as one unit: row 763 (ponytail, refuted as the streak by row 765), row 767 (wolf render, retracted by row 768 as a crop artefact), row 769 (elf degenerate at bind, refuted by row 770s population sweep), and now row 770s open question, closed from the files own bone names in a single pass. Every one of those was resolved by widening the comparison -- a control capture, a population, a peer group -- and never by looking harder at the single case. No code changed for this row; suite unchanged at 22 of 22 green.

THE QUATERNION GATE IS FIXED, BY REMOVING IT RATHER THAN RETUNING IT. ANIM_QUAT_EPS=0.07 refused any clip whose track rotations deviated from unit length by more than that. It was doing TWO jobs: validating the record LAYOUT and gating each ENTRY. It was good at the first -- 05-02 ranked every rival header/field-offset candidate by the epsilon it would need and found the documented layout isolated at 0.0611 against 0.4142 for the next. It was bad at the second, and that cost 643 clips. MEASURED FIRST, and the measurement is why this is a removal and not a new number. A fine histogram of worst-case deviation across all 671 refused entries decays SMOOTHLY from 0.06 to 0.66 with NO gap anywhere: 82 entries at 0.06-0.08, 142 at 0.08-0.10, 102, 74, 39, 28, 24, 12, 27, 12, 18, 14, 12, then a thin tail. That is ONE population of quantization drift, not two separable groups, so there is no threshold to pick and any value chosen would be arbitrary. 0.07 itself came from a three-clip sample whose worst was 0.0611, and 491 entries sat just above it. Raising it to fit would have been the same error this session has now made and retracted three times (rows 763, 767, 769). WHY THE LAYOUT JOB IS NO LONGER NEEDED HERE: row 767 established that a record reconciles EXACTLY, 52 + 16nt + 20nq + 40nu == span, zero slack, every record. A wrong header or field offset leaves slack, so size reconciliation is a STRICTLY STRONGER layout discriminator than the quaternion norm ever was, and it already runs first. The tolerance was relieved of a duty something better now performs. WHAT REPLACED IT: ANIM_QUAT_MIN=0.5, a degeneracy floor. A quaternion is unusable only when it cannot be normalized -- NaN or length near zero, where the direction is noise -- and that still refuses the entry. Everything else is normalized on read, which ModelView was already doing per key before handing them to Godot. RESULT: decodable motion entries 2750 -> 3387, refusals 671 -> 34, of which 28 are the size-mismatch shape and ~6 remain unexplained. NO REGRESSION: BEAR re-captured after the change still renders as a correct quadruped, diff bbox 61x98. Full suite 22 of 22 green; clip_layout_check WANT_DECODABLE re-pinned 2750 -> 3387. TAKEN TOGETHER WITH ROWS 764 and 767, the clip decoder went from 2069 decodable entries at the start of this session to 3387 of 3421 -- and every one of the three fixes came from a case the previous model had DISCARDED as malformed: nu=3 entries called a second constant, varying-nu entries called internally inconsistent, and drifting-quaternion entries called non-unit. The rejects were the signal each time.

CATEGORISED, and most are CORRECT refusals rather than defects. Of the 34 motion entries clip() still rejects after row 772: 26 count-over-max (a declared nt/nq/nu above MAX_KEYFRAMES) -- HORS_DYING_A, HORS_FUN_IDLE_1H, HORS_FUN_IDLE_BH, WOLF_DYING_A and 22 more; 4 no-records -- GLADIATOR.GRN, WIZARD.GRN, SD01_ACTIVATE.GRN, WILB_DYING_C.GRN; 2 size-mismatch on exactly half their records -- FX_E_IDLE_BH.GRN and FX_G_IDLE_BH.GRN, 12 of 24; 1 degenerate quaternion -- ANDD_ATTACK_SPECIAL01.GRN; 1 not-walkable -- INVALID_MOTION. SEVEN SHOULD STAY REFUSED AND NEED NO WORK. INVALID_MOTION is named for what it is. GLADIATOR.GRN and WIZARD.GRN are MESHES sitting in the motion kind, and clip() already documents that decoding a non-clip is a caller error, not a partial success -- is_animation() is the predicate for that question. FX_E/FX_G are the pair clip_track_bone.s own doc comment already records as declaring 12 bones against 24 records with duplicated ids, where a positional bind would be a guess. ANDD_ATTACK_SPECIAL01 carries a quaternion that cannot be normalized, which is exactly what ANIM_QUAT_MIN is for. THE ONE OPEN SHAPE IS THE 26. They are the same entries row 764 measured as SINGLE-RECORD with implied trailers of 1728 to 13560 -- and that is the tell: a clip carries one AnimationTransformTrackKeys record PER BONE, so an entry yielding exactly one record and then garbage counts is one where the walk is landing on the wrong node, not one whose data is bad. Row 764 guarded against them by holding single-record entries to attested trailer widths, which kept them refused for the right reason under a model that has since been replaced. HYPOTHESIS FOR THE NEXT SESSION, untested: these entries nest their track keys differently (an extra level, or a second AnimationTransformTrackSection), so _direct_children of the first matching section finds one node that is not a record at all. Cheap to check -- dump the tag tree under AnimationSection for HORS_DYING_A and compare it against a decoding HORS clip from the same character. The character prefix is shared, so a structural difference between two files of the same creature is the whole answer. No code changed for this row; suite unchanged at 22 of 22 green, decodable 3387 of 3421.

ROW 773S HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED AND THE REAL SHAPE IS FOUND. The tag trees of HORS_DYING_A.GRN (refused) and HORS_IDLE_BH.GRN (decodes) are IDENTICAL: same census, same AnimationSection > Animation > AnimationTransformTrackSection chain, and one AnimationTransformTrackKeys per bone in both (48 records / 48 bones, and 46 / 46). So the walk is NOT landing on the wrong node and there is no extra nesting -- row 773 guessed both and both are wrong. TWO CORRECTIONS TO EARLIER ROWS. (1) HORS_DYING_A is NOT a single-record entry. Rows 764 and 773 both described it that way; that was an artefact of MY probe, which skipped records whose counts exceeded MAX_KEYFRAMES before counting them, leaving one survivor. It has 48. (2) Its "trailer of 1728..13560" in row 764 was the same artefact measured on that one survivor. WHAT IT ACTUALLY IS: a SECOND, FIXED-STRIDE record format. Every one of HORS_DYING_A.s 48 records spans exactly 2324 bytes at a uniform stride -- rel 16104, 18428, 20752, 23076, 25400, 27724, 30048, 32372, each +2324 -- where HORS_IDLE_BH.s records are variable-length and driven by their counts (240, 240, 576, 368). THE ROW 784 TRAP IS NOW GUARDED IN CODE. ModelView gained freeze_anim(t), which sets speed_scale to 0 and seeks -- the ONLY sanctioned setup for reading a posed skeleton -- plus an anim_frozen property that is true only while the player is genuinely parked (flag set AND speed_scale still 0, so a caller that resumes playback cannot leave a stale claim behind). seek_anim() explicitly CLEARS the flag and is documented as not a freeze, because --creatures relies on it to desynchronise loops and must keep animating; conflating the two is what would reintroduce the bug. sample_bone_pose() now REFUSES with push_error and returns IDENTITY when the player is advancing and not frozen. GUARDED BY anim_freeze_check.gd, which pins all four transitions: a rig with no clip is not frozen, play_clip leaves it RUNNING, freeze_anim parks it, seek_anim un-parks it. THE LOAD-BEARING ASSERTION IS THE GUARD IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: while the player advances sample_bone_pose must return IDENTITY (refusal is observable, since that is what refusing looks like), and once parked it must return something else. Asserting only the frozen half would pass against a reader with no guard at all -- the first version of this check did exactly that and also carried a no-op assertion (x or true), both of which were removed rather than left in as decoration. WHAT THIS CHECK DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO: measure a pose. That needs frames, and check.gd.s failsafe (correctly) treats an _init that returns without finish() as a failed assert. A check that needed frames is precisely the check that could not exist while this bug was live, which is why the contract is pinned as an API state machine instead. The complementary design point stands: anim_check reads the ANIMATION rather than the skeleton, which is why it never caught row 784 and why that was the right choice -- pure-data checks have held up all session, scene-based ones have not. MY CONCERN WAS MISDIRECTED AND THE MEASUREMENT SAYS SO. The worry was that mirrored bones (rest basis with det<0) break the row 766 retarget, because it composes rotation QUATERNIONS extracted from rest bases and a reflection is not a rotation. Tested directly across every creature mesh by decomposing each rest basis the way a Skeleton3D pose does -- get_rotation_quaternion() plus get_scale() -- and recomposing Basis(q).scaled(scale), then comparing column by column against the original. MIRRORED BONES ARE FINE: 479 of 489 recompose within 0.001. Godot pushes the reflection into a NEGATIVE SCALE (worst sample M_Spider_02.grn / R_Leg_03_01, det -1.000, scale -0.96,-1.06,-1.00), and since a bone pose carries position + rotation quaternion + scale, the mirror survives in the scale slot. The retarget is sound for them. THE FAILURES ARE 15x MORE COMMON AMONG NON-MIRRORED BONES: 151 lost at det>0 against 10 at det<0, out of ~8800 bones. So the sign of the determinant is not the discriminator at all. What those 161 bones have is SHEAR -- a rest basis that is not a pure rotation times a scale, which quaternion+scale cannot express and which Godot.s pose model has no slot for. The information is dropped silently at set_bone_rest time, before any animation is involved. SCOPE AND WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: 161 of ~8800 is about 1.8%, worst recomposition error 0.191 on the mirrored side (the non-mirrored worst was not recorded and should be, since that is now the larger population). XSHIM_NOTRACK=1 DOES NOT SURVIVE, exactly as xshim.c.s own comment predicted ("Expect the 2005 double-free to abort somewhere; that is the point of the tracking"). The run reaches SDL_SetVideoMode 1024x768 bpp=32 and schedules its screenshots, then dies with glibc "double free or corruption (out)" before gameplay. Zero frames captured. So the malloc tracking is LOAD-BEARING, not instrumentation overhead: the hash table and its global spinlock exist to absorb a real double-free in the retail binary, and removing them reproduces the bug in under 45 seconds. The speed idea is dead in this form. OPERATIONAL NOTE: the abort leaves the process WEDGED with its window up -- glibc aborts, the game does not exit, and `timeout 75` could not reap it. It needed pkill -9. Any future A/B against the tracker must expect that and kill hard rather than wait. WHAT THIS CLOSES, and it is a chain of three wrong guesses of mine in a row, each cheaper to check than the last: Xvfb was not the bottleneck (row 818 -- the runs were already on DISPLAY=:0); llvmpipe was not the bottleneck (no Mesa DRI driver is mapped at all; xshim.c states rendering goes through SDL3.s EGL/Wayland path); and now the malloc tracker cannot simply be switched off. The 1fps remains UNEXPLAINED and the three cheapest explanations are eliminated. WHERE TO LOOK NEXT, if speed is still wanted: the tracker can be made cheap WITHOUT being removed -- the global spinlock is the suspicious part, since a single-threaded 2005 game contends with nothing and the lock is pure overhead on every malloc and free. Making lock()/unlock() no-ops (leaving the hash table intact) preserves the double-free protection while deleting the atomic traffic, and is a two-line experiment with the same A/B shape. If that does not move the framerate, the cost is the hash table itself and the next step is measuring it rather than guessing again -- XSHIM_STATS already exists and dumps allocation counts. XSHIM_NOLOCK=1 ADDED AND IT SURVIVES. xshim.c.s lock()/unlock() become no-ops when set, leaving the hash table -- and therefore the double-free protection -- fully intact. Ran the load-a-save script with it: both scheduled screenshots captured, no abort, clean shutdown. That is the predicted outcome and the reason this experiment is safe where XSHIM_NOTRACK=1 was not (row 819 reproduced the 2005 double-free in under 45s by removing the live-set itself). The rationale: this engine is single-threaded on this stack, so every malloc and free pays an atomic read-modify-write that nothing ever contends. SPEED IS NOT MEASURED AND MUST NOT BE ASSUMED. The script used only loads a save; nothing in it measures throughput, so all that is established is SAFETY. Saying "it survives, therefore it is faster" would be exactly the inference this session has spent nineteen rows retracting -- a plausible mechanism reported as a result without the measurement that separates them. THE MEASUREMENT IS SMALL AND SHOULD COME NEXT: autopilot already hooks SDL_GL_SwapBuffers, so a frame counter is a one-line static incremented there and printed at each SACRED_SHOT time. That gives frames-per-interval directly, and the A/B is one run with XSHIM_NOLOCK and one without, same script, comparing counts. Until that runs, XSHIM_NOLOCK is an available switch of unknown benefit, not a speedup. If it shows no gain, the cost is the hash table rather than the lock, and XSHIM_STATS already dumps allocation counts to size it. PROFILED AND FOUND, AFTER FOUR WRONG GUESSES. SACRED_PROF=1 sampled through load and gameplay (frame counter confirms the split in the same log: 15.20fps to t=45s, then 1.19fps). eiphist.py resolves 2638 late-slice samples as: libz.so.1.3.2 2067 (78.4%), sacred 235 (8.9%), libc 153 (5.8%), libgallium 90 (3.4%), vdso 77 (2.9%), xshim 8 (0.3%). Hottest single address is libz+0x26a7 at 6.1% on its own. Early slice is the same shape at 69.9% libz. THE ENGINE SPENDS ~78% OF ITS CPU IN ZLIB. Not rendering (libgallium is 3.4%), not the GL path, not malloc, not the spinlock (row 821 A/B showed zero difference), not Xvfb and not llvmpipe (row 818). Decompression outweighs everything else by a factor of nine, and xshim -- the thing I spent two rows suspecting -- is 0.3%. IT ALSO EXPLAINS ROW 821.S SHAPE. Menus run at 15-17fps because little is being decompressed; the moment the world appears the engine streams assets out of the paks continuously and collapses to 1.19fps. A constant overhead could not produce that step change; a workload that only starts when the world loads can, and does. WHAT IS ACTIONABLE, in order of cheapness: (1) LD_PRELOAD zlib-ng, which is API/ABI drop-in for zlib and typically 2-4x on inflate -- pure win if it works, nothing in this repo depends on zlib.s internals, and it is one env var to test with the frame counter already built. (2) Find out WHY decompression is continuous rather than cached: 78% steady-state suggests the same data is being inflated repeatedly, which would mean a cache that is absent, too small, or defeated -- and that is a question the port can help answer, since godot-port reads the same paks and knows their structure. (3) Accept it: 1.19fps is survivable for scripted measurement runs, and every retail task this session actually needed (rows 789, 803, 810, 815) completed at that speed. METHOD NOTE: five explanations were proposed and eliminated before anyone profiled -- Xvfb, llvmpipe, the malloc tracker, the spinlock, and the hash table. The profiler was available the whole time (AGENTS.md documents SACRED_PROF and eiphist.py) and would have answered it in one run. Reach for the instrument before the hypothesis. there-is-no-decompression-cache-99-7-percent-of-inflate-calls-are-repeats | ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS THAT NOTHING IS CACHED. Built ztrace.so, a 32-bit shim interposing inflate() that fingerprints each call.s INPUT (length plus first 32 bytes) and counts fingerprint recurrence. Gameplay measurement: 220000 inflate calls in 80s, 219443 of them REPEATS -- 99.7% -- against only 557 distinct streams. That is roughly 400 re-inflations of every stream, at ~2750 inflate calls per second, and the bytes_in counter wrapping past 4GB (32-bit unsigned long) puts the redundant volume in the many gigabytes. The engine decompresses the same small working set over and over, every frame, forever. IT EXPLAINS ROW 823 EXACTLY. zlib-ng is 2-4x on inflate yet bought only 29%, which did not fit a throughput-bound model. It fits this one perfectly: the cost is not how fast a stream inflates, it is that ~550 streams are inflated 400 times each. No library swap can fix a missing cache, and the 29% is simply the fraction of the work that WAS throughput. THE FINGERPRINT IS DELIBERATELY CONSERVATIVE: 32 bytes plus length, not a full hash, so a collision would make two DIFFERENT streams look identical and thereby OVERSTATE repeats. But the direction of that bias is the point -- to be wrong here the fingerprint would have to be colliding at 99.7%, which 32 bytes of real compressed data does not do. A false "no cache" reading cannot come from the instrument. SCOPE, and it matters: this is a property of the RETAIL ENGINE, measured in the retail binary. It is not a finding about godot-port, and the port must NOT replicate it -- Sacred.Pak/Models already decode on demand, and anything built on them should keep decoded results rather than inheriting a 2005 pathology by imitation. Under canonical-first the port reproduces retail.s VISIBLE behaviour and its flaws, not its performance bugs. PRACTICAL CEILING: at 99.7% redundancy the theoretical headroom is enormous -- a working cache of ~550 streams would remove almost all of the 78% CPU row 822 measured -- but implementing one means interposing at the engine.s asset layer, not at inflate(), since inflate() cannot know what the caller will do with the output. That is a much larger piece of work than a shim and is not obviously worth it: 1.5fps already completes every scripted run this session needed. Suite 23 of 23 green, decodable 3413 of 3421.

THE WIDE TAG PAYLOADS ARE DECODED: A 12-BYTE TAG IS THREE SIGNED i32, AND THE 'HUGE' DECIMAL VALUES IN EVERY EARLIER DUMP WERE THAT STRUCT PRINTED AS ONE INTEGER. Control arm, run over all 16 files and 1.35M records: read the same 12 bytes as i32 at byte offsets 0..4 and score in-range. Aligned reads score 100.0%, misaligned 0.0-0.4% (offsets 5-8 were DISCARDED as a bad control -- the third field is near-zero so any read landing in it passes trivially, and the agent said so rather than banking it). Six-u16 is refuted for the coordinate tags: the odd u16 slots are constant 0 or 0xFFFF, i.e. sign-extension high halves. SIGNED, not unsigned -- 4294967073 is -223. The two examples that motivated the question reproduce byte-exactly: 27127013446221 = tag04{4685, 6316, 0}, a chest at cell (4685,6316); 75557863725931503288324 = tag35{4, 4, 4096}; 4294967359 = tag34(63, 1) as 2xi32. COORDINATE TAGS: 0x04 (129,477 occurrences, cell_x, cell_y, enum), 0x0d (7,060, field2 always 0), 0x2a (43,491), 0x4d (393 of 415). Corroboration is independent of range-fitting: op23's known plain-int coordinates and tag 0x04's literals are DISJOINT populations that hit the same ceiling near 6328, and tag-0x04 points fall in op23-occupied spatial bins at 4.0x (bin 128), 9.5x (64), 14x (32) and 23x (16) over a uniform-random control on the same bounding box. TAG 0x20 IS A SECOND COORDINATE SYSTEM AT SUB-CELL PRECISION, and it was decoded by regression rather than assertion: 0x20 never co-occurs with op23 but always co-occurs with 0x04 (85,227 records carry both), slopes are 53.669 (x) and 53.667 (y), a divisor grid-search over 53.0..54.5 in steps of 0.002 peaks sharply at 53.666 (88.6% floor-match, against 71.8% at 53.670 and 66.9% at 53.660), and the exact rational form t04 == t20*3//161 holds for 84.7% x / 89.1% y while //54 gives 0.6% and //53 gives 0.06%. The residual sits between 0.04 and 0.91 from p10 to p90 -- exactly a fractional position inside the cell. So 161 fine units per 3 cells, 53 and 2/3 per cell. A REAL PARSER DEFECT, AND THE FIRST DIAGNOSIS OF IT WAS WRONG. A subagent reported that tag 0x4d 'needs VARIANT/string handling it does not have', on the evidence of 22 records whose 0x4d payload is the ASCII text axVerstecke_. TESTED THAT DIRECTLY: adding 0x4d to the VARIANT table is INERT -- the 0xfffffffe sentinel branch never fires for it, 330 occurrences and 0 string-form, and the all-files sweep is 1,123,758 records / 0 unparsed both before and after. So the change was not made. THE ACTUAL MECHANISM, from the raw record body (elve/funkcode.bin op 58, offset 0xee8e): 48 ff ff ff ff 'AnzahlVerstecke\0' 'MaxVerstecke_r+Var(RNr)\0'. Tag 0x48 is NUMSTR, so it consumes the u32 and the FIRST string and stops. The parser then reads the next byte -- 'M', which is 0x4d -- as a TAG, and 0x4d's 12-byte width swallows the front of the second string. axVerstecke_ is simply MaxVerstecke_ with its M eaten. So 0x48 takes TWO strings after its u32, which is exactly the shape row 721 proved for tag 0x3a (two strcpy calls in one handler), and 0x4d is an innocent bystander whose byte value happens to be the letter M. SCOPE: 16 occurrences across all 16 files, all with the identical 12 bytes, in opcodes 58 and 66. They do not fail the parse -- ok stays True because trailing garbage is absorbed -- which is precisely the hollow-metric failure the parser's own docstring warns about, and is why this survived rows 711-726. THE TEST THAT SETTLES IT, not run here: disassemble handler 0x0826cb0e (the NUMSTR handler serving 0x48/0x49/0x4a/0x5d/0x5e/0x6d/0x6e) and count strcpy calls, as row 721 did for 0x3a. TWO strcpys confirms; one refutes and forces a different reading. NOT CHANGING THE PARSER ON THE INFERENCE ALONE -- 0x48 is 70,000+ occurrences and a wrong width there would silently reshape far more than the 16 records it fixes. The correct arm is the handler, and it is cheap.

THE CHECK'S FIRST NEGATIVE CONTROL WAS VACUOUS AND I REPLACED IT. It fed the join the position tag's LAYER field, which scored 0.9% -- but only because that field is a 0..4 enum sitting near zero, so it could not have failed. So the check now asserts the control is INSIDE 0.30..0.80 -- too high means the join cannot discriminate, too low means the control has gone vacuous again. A control that cannot fail is not a control, and that is now enforced rather than remembered. MUTATION-TESTED, not assumed: changing _ids() to take the first 4-byte numeric argument instead of the first tag-0x02 one -- exactly the positional reading that produced row 831's bad evidence -- makes the check FAIL. Note WHICH assertion caught it: 'every body id resolves to a .grn' still passed at 1.000 under the mutation, and the DISJOINT body/main-hand name sets is what fired, printing SOLDIER.GRN, HORSE.GRN, SERAPHIM.GRN, ORC_CHAMA.GRN and DARKELVE.GRN as overlapping. SWEPT THE REMAINING GATES BY MUTATION AND FOUND A HARNESS HOLE UNDER THEM, WORSE THAN ANY OF THE WEAK ASSERTIONS IT WAS LOOKING FOR. Eleven gates that had never been mutation-tested got one falsifying change each: armour WANT_GROUPS 85->84, defpos REC 100->96, factions TIER 6->5, spawn CREATURE_REC 86->85, spawn_factions TIER 6->5, trigger REC 16->15 and static_chain HEADS 777->778 are all CAUGHT. Four survived, and sorting them apart mattered more than the count. TWO WERE FALSE ALARMS: goaltick's GOAL_AT_OFFSET cancels by design -- the check sets pending_goal_tick from the same constant it then expects, so any value should hold, and the claim is 'the sim fires on the tick it was ASKED to'; desyncing the request from the expectation is CAUGHT. interior_swap's and door_transition's SECT are coordinate helpers, not claims; falsifying their real verdicts -- a FLOOR cell expected EXTERIOR, and entering a door expected NOT to open the interior -- is CAUGHT in both. THE FOURTH WAS REAL AND GENERAL. Changing footprint_bind_check's expected REGION_KEY from 50039000 to 50039001 makes TWO assertions fail, printing SCRIPT ERROR with full backtraces, and the check STILL PRINTS OK AND EXITS 0. GDScript reports a failed assert() inside a FUNCTION and then returns; _init carries on to its OK line and calls finish(0). check.gd's failsafe only detects '_init never reached finish()', so it is structurally blind to this -- and this is worse than the hang that file was written to fix, because a hang is at least visible while this reports success. EIGHT ASSERTIONS ACROSS FOUR CHECKS sat behind the hole: armour_check 2, footprint_bind_check 2, rig_check 2, rigs_check 2 -- and the rigs_check pair are the BEAR/WOLF spot checks whose own comment says they exist so that a human reading the line knows something is wrong, which no aggregate fraction conveys. They could never fail. Note the timing: row 846 documented those spot checks as the human-readable half of that gate one hour before this measured that they were inert. THE FIX is expect() on check.gd -- records the failure, prints CHECK FAILED, and makes finish() exit 1 no matter what code it is handed, returning the condition so a caller can still bail early and collecting every failure in a run rather than stopping at the first. All eight converted. The three mutations that previously survived are now CAUGHT: wrong region key, BEAR animated as WOLF, wrong armour group count. Regression 23 of 24, the exception pax_check refusing without SACRED_CHARS. GENERAL LESSON, and the reason this was invisible for as long as it was: every one of these gates was GREEN, and greenness is what a mutation test measures against. A suite that has never been mutated is a suite whose failure mode has never been observed.

THE SWEEP IS NOW COMPLETE: every one of the 24 gates has had at least one falsifying mutation applied and caught. The eight never previously swept -- anim, anim_freeze, bindagree, clickmove, equip, items_sprite, pax, rig -- all hold. anim_check catches a broken retarget in all three forms tried (inverted clip_rest*model_rest^-1, identity, and the inverse dropped entirely); anim_freeze catches the freeze flag being set the wrong way round at either of its two sites; bindagree catches LOCAL_WITHIN 0.01 -> 100; rig_check catches WANT_LOCAL_WITHIN 47 -> 40 and WANT_MATCHED 60 -> 55; items_sprite catches a one-off in either the sprite id or the item name; clickmove catches the simulation being skipped entirely; pax catches its corpus variable being renamed. THE FALSE ALARM, AND IT WAS MINE. A first pass reported that disabling retargeting was caught by NOTHING -- three gates green with `retarget := Quaternion()`. That was wrong: the sed pattern contained an unescaped `*`, so `model_rest * clip_rest` was read as a regex meaning 't' followed by zero-or-more spaces and MATCHED NOTHING. The mutation was never applied and I was reading a pristine tree three times over. Proved rather than assumed: the unescaped pattern substitutes 0 occurrences, the escaped one substitutes 1. balance-bin-is-one-struct-at-0x08b8d29c-and-that-address-opens-the-combat-code | THE BRIDGE BETWEEN THE BALANCE TABLE AND THE CODE THAT USES IT, WHICH IS WHAT THE COMBAT SYSTEM WAS WAITING ON. The check is a coincidence that cannot survive being wrong: thirteen case bodies push their own skill's resource id as a literal and every one equals 9399 + that case's index, 13/13 with zero mismatches; shifting the base by one or the table pointer by one entry breaks 12-13 of them. The method-to-file association is not inferred -- the linker emits a translation unit's string literals together, so walking the string table in FILE OFFSET order and attributing each cClass::method() to the nearest preceding path recovers it, an ordering property of the object file. tools/binary/armasource.py does this and reports 76 source files, 259 methods and 80 classes; it exits non-zero if the ordering trick binds fewer than 40 files or 60 methods. The cross-build check is retail's own RTTI: 25 of the 80 classes are still there -- cCreature, cWeapon3D, cArmor3D, cArrow3D, cObject3D, cObjectFX, cSector, cWorld, cWorldView, cEngine, cResourceMgr, cParticleSystem, cFsFont, cFile_cached, cFile_memoryMapped, cEvent_idle, six cUI_* and two cCommand_* -- spanning every module, so the tree is retail's tree at module and class granularity. The same assert strings give the script VM's own vocabulary and its invariants, from armaSource/scripts/: cScriptCompiler (parseStatement, parseArmaStatement, parseResource, loadScriptedSequenceR, save, saveResources, load), cScriptVM::load, cScriptInterpreter (load, interpreter, findScriptFunction), cScriptLoader::getResource. `fp->code[ip]<256` states that an opcode is a BYTE indexing a byte array with a frame pointer and an instruction pointer; `serialID<exportFunctions.size()` that the script API dispatches by INDEX INTO A VECTOR rather than a fixed switch; `chunk.type==CHUNK_TYPE_ACS` and `hdr.ver==2` name the compiled-script container and its version. cScriptCompiler shipping inside the game explains why cScriptLoader::getResource reaches RESOURCE.PAK, the Armalion-era container retail dropped. Also ruled out this iteration: harvesting NAMED callees from the 141 retail opcode handlers (tools/binary/ghidra/Callees.java, written for it) returns zero at depth 3 with the caller cap raised to 400, because the handlers reach C++ objects only through vtable dispatch, which leaves no static call reference.
