THE PORT'S ENTIRE OUTDOOR COLLISION LAYER IS KEYED ON A TERRAIN HEIGHT BYTE AND IS MEANINGLESS. world/walkable.gd:_terrain_open decides every cell no region grid covers with `byte26 != 1 and byte26 != 4`, credited in its own comment to "the retail canWalk rule". Three measurements refute that. (1) BYTE 26 IS A HEIGHT CORNER: over 36,864 start-area cells, offsets +0x18/+0x19/+0x1a/+0x1b are statistically indistinguishable -- min -6, max 78, mean 0.062-0.063, sd 1.357, 26 distinct values, all four identical -- and +0x1a correlates with its neighbour +0x1b at r=+0.86, which is the signed per-corner second height world-sectors.md documents at +0x18..0x1b (26 == 0x1a is inside that span). (2) RETAIL NEVER READS IT SO: a byte-pattern search of the 1.0.02 Linux binary for `cmp byte ptr [reg+0x1A], 1` and `..., 4` returns zero hits, with a control search for `cmp byte ptr [reg+0x1A], <any>` returning matches, so the method works and the idiom is absent. (3) THE SOURCE WAS ARMALION, PARTIALLY COPIED: sub_4B0220 decompiles to `byte26 != 1 && byte26 != 4 && *(int*)cell >= 0`, then discards that answer entirely when `*(DWORD*)cell & 4` and substitutes a static-object chain lookup; the port implements two of three terms and none of the second branch. COST, MEASURED: the rule opens 96.9% of cells; region grids cover only 26.55% of the start area and are 91% blocked inside; so 96.06% of all walkable ground the port offers comes from a comparison against terrain height. This is the reported "hero walks randomly against the actual map". The rule is LEFT IN PLACE, not deleted or inverted, because blocking every uncovered cell strands the player; what changed is that its comment no longer claims a provenance it does not have. Finding retail's real outdoor walkability is now an open question.

Water and lava are now blocked, on the one retail-grounded signal the port was ignoring. Row 669 recovered the animated-liquid system from disassembly -- 14 materials, a reflection flag at record +0xcc, quest-gated type 13 -- selected by WldxEntry +0x1f's HIGH nibble, values 9 and 10. Before trusting a nibble reading recovered for a different purpose, it was corroborated geometrically: the 514 such cells in the 3x3-sector start block form exactly THREE connected components of 356, 121 and 37 cells with ZERO isolated singles, which is a river system rather than scattered mis-reads. Safety measured before the change, since a fix that traps the player is worse than the bug: the start cell 4096,2496 is not liquid, and a flood fill of walkable ground from it saturates the probe's 60,000-cell bound both with and without liquid blocked, so no reachability is measurably lost -- note the bound was reached in both arms, so this shows no stranding rather than proving connectivity is identical. Implemented as Walkable.is_liquid(), public because sector_view will need the same nibble when the port grows water rendering, and two independent readings of one field is how it drifts out of agreement with itself. Blocking applies on the terrain path only; where a region grid covers a cell the shipped navmesh still decides. All 40 checks plus parity/verify.gd pass.

iso_camera.gd bound left-drag to camera panning and left-click to a single move_click, which is the reported "click/drag doesn't feel the same": one click could only ever schedule one path, and there was no way to keep walking where the pointer points. The pan it replaced was already DEAD CODE in normal play, not a behaviour being removed -- main.gd:735 calls follow_cell(p.cell) every simulation tick, so any drag-pan was overwritten before the next frame was drawn; dragging jittered the camera and lost. Left-drag now re-emits move_click each time the pointer crosses into a new cell, guarded by a _drag_cell latch so holding still inside one cell does not re-path on every motion event, and reset on button release so the next drag always re-targets at least once. Panning survives on MIDDLE drag, where it is actually reachable: the --at= and --sector= inspection modes build no player and so never follow. clickmove_check still PASSes (spawn 4096,2496, click 560,408 -> goal 4097,2496) and parity/verify.gd reports layer files=19 violations=0. NOT MEASURED AND STILL OWED: retail's own walk speed. Movement.CELLS_PER_TICK is 4.0 cells/sec and its comment already labels that a placeholder, so movement feel cannot match retail until a capture measures it.

A THREE-WAY HERO COMPARISON ACROSS RETAIL, ARMALION AND THE PORT CANNOT BE VISUAL, AND THE REASON IS WORTH RECORDING. The 2001-09-20 Armalion prerelease ships its own MODELS.PAK/Items.pak/TEXTURE.PAK under builds/prerelease/, and the port's format readers open it unchanged -- but it holds 850 entries against retail's 4993 and contains NO Seraphim, no Gladiator, no Magician, no Dwarf and no Sera* wardrobe at all. Its playable bodies are a different cast (ELVE_MAGICAN, ELVE_SORCESS and 26 further ELVE_* entries). So there is no like-for-like hero to render on the Armalion side, and the comparison that IS available is mechanical, from the prerelease binary's retained assert strings. It is decisive: cCreature dresses a character from THIRTEEN EQUIPMENT SLOTS (assert 'eslot>=0 && eslot<PC_EQUIPMENT_MAX', PC_EQUIPMENT_MAX == 0xD), holding the item refs in an array at this+2*eslot+79, and dispatches each on equipment_getSlotType (sub_42E370) which returns 1 for slots 0,1,2,3,7, 2 for slots 4,5,6,9,10,11,12, and 0 for slot 8 ALONE. Type 1 goes through grnWearEquipment (sub_42E060, a skinned garment), type 2 through attachEquipment onto a named bone -- getSlotAttachBoneName (sub_42E4A0) maps slot 9 to 'Bip01 L Hand' and slot 10 to 'Bip01 R Hand' for subtype 5, the same two to 'Bip01 L/R Forearm' for subtype 13, and slots 5/6 to 'Bip01 L/R Finger31' for subtype 8 (rings). Type 0 is neither worn nor attached. THE PORT HAS NO SLOT MODEL AT ALL: _dress_player iterates a sets.bin member list and sorts it by 'does the mesh declare vertex weights', which is why it wore a member retail does not draw. Note the bone names are Biped names from the 2001 build; Sacred Gold's own weapon sockets are the .GRN grips Bone_weapon_01/02, so the attach mechanism changed between builds and only the SLOT model transfers.

items.pak +0x2e IS THE ITEM CATEGORY, DECODED AGAINST THE WHOLE 32,768-RECORD CORPUS. Found by censusing every byte of the 128-byte record against the six Seraphim garments whose body parts are known: only two offsets took six distinct values there, +0x20 (a running index 160..165, rejected) and +0x2e. The corpus then names every value by itself, because Daemonia's armour family is spelled out part by part: 3 = hero/creature BODY (477 records: SERAPHIM.GRN, GLADIATOR.GRN, MAGICIAN.GRN), 5 = one-hand weapon (240), 6 = chest (308), 8 = ring (91), 9 = bottle (27), 10 = door (119), 13 = shield (42), 16 = scroll (143), 17 = helm (129), 18 = boots (97), 19 = belt (127), 20 = amulet (156), 21 = shoulder (68), 22 = arms (107), 23 = legs (81), 24 = gloves (42), 25 = WINGS (7), 27 = arrow (10), 29 = horse barding (26), 33 = dwarf cannon (4); 1 and 15 are gib meshes, 26 and 28 upgrade tokens. CORROBORATION NOT USED IN THE DERIVATION: the weighted/rigid split follows the categories exactly -- every armour category is 100% skinned (6,17,18,19,21,22,23,24; 908 records, 0 rigid) and every prop category is 100% rigid (8,9,10,13,16,27). A field invented to explain one set would not also sort the corpus that way. NOT A SLOT INDEX: it has ~27 values where Armalion's cCreature has 13 slots, so it feeds a category-to-slot mapping rather than being one, and recovering that table is open work. Also corrected in passing: +0x09, which looked like a slot byte separating the wings from the six garments, is byte 1 of the +0x08 u32 texture override -- all eight drawn members carry overrides 7338..7354 and the wings carry 0, meaning 'use the mesh's own texture name', which they do successfully (--figure=SeraWings01.grn reports textured=2/2 on Sera_armor_blades.tga and Sera_armor_back.tga). The wings being dark in world captures is lighting, not a missing skin.

THE PORT DREW WINGS RETAIL DOES NOT, AND TWO EARLIER EXPLANATIONS OF THE IN-WORLD HERO WERE WRONG. Measured against a retail new-game frame: retail's Seraphim wears helmet, chest, belt, shoulder, gloves and boots and carries the sword -- eight of sets.bin set 6's nine members -- and draws NO wings, while the port drew two large dark spread wings over her because _dress_player's only test was 'declares vertex weights', which SeraWings01.grn does. Now skipped on the decoded category (Items.CATEGORY_WINGS == 25, seven records corpus-wide) rather than on the mesh name, and logged as a stopgap in place: the real fix is the thirteen-slot model Armalion's cCreature uses, and a sets.bin set is a matched item family rather than an outfit. REFUTED, both by direct measurement: (1) ANIMATION IS NOT THE CAUSE of the in-world figure looking wrong -- rendering the same cell with and without --noanim produces the same figure, so the distortion is not a posing fault. (2) THE WEAPON DOES NOT DETACH. A probe that plays the hero's own clip and samples the BoneAttachment3D against Skeleton3D.get_bone_global_pose at nine times across it reports a delta of 0.0000 at every sample while the hand travels from (3.0,-15.5,48.1) to (18.0,4.2,63.3); the earlier 'blade floating 10-22 px clear of both hands' was measured against a body bounding box that excluded the extended arm. The isolated --figure= render of the same model is correct and closely matches retail -- ponytail, blue and gold armour, white boots, correctly sized blade -- so the model, textures, garments and dock are all sound and the remaining in-world gap is what is dressed onto them, not how.

FIRST ABSOLUTE RETAIL MEASUREMENT OF A CHARACTER'S DRAWN HEIGHT, WHICH view/player_view.gd HAS BEEN ASKING FOR IN COMMENT FORM. Rendering the port at the real Seraphim start (startcode: class=type_npc_seraphim, cell=3236,2511, sector 50,39 -- NOT the 4096,2496 that clickmove_check uses as a synthetic spawn) at 1024x768 and zoom size 768, against the retail drive capture of the same frame: the port hero occupies x 495..535, y 275..380, so about 102 px tall and 40 wide, while retail's occupies about 136 px tall and 44 wide. Ratio 0.75 in height. The port's factor is PlayerView._scale = SectorView.SORTCUBE_PX / REF_HEIGHT = 96.0 / 73.0 = 1.315, applied to SERAPHIM.GRN's 74.3-unit AABB, which predicts 97.7 px and matches the 102 measured once helmet and hair are included. Retail's 136 px against the same 74.3 units implies a factor near 1.83, i.e. the port is short by about x1.39. player_view.gd's own comment already labels this a placeholder -- 'no retail capture has measured an actual character height yet' -- and names this exact route as the upgrade path, so the number is now available. NOT APPLIED YET, deliberately: it is one class in one frame, the comment warns against tuning REF_HEIGHT to absorb an unrelated wolf/elf ratio gap, and the port hero has a second, larger defect (below) that would confound any recalibration done before it is fixed. Silhouette fill is also wrong in a way pure scale cannot explain: 31% for the port against 51% for retail over the figure's own bounding box, i.e. the port's body reads hollow rather than merely small.

THE PORT'S HERO FACES THE WRONG WAY AND THE SEED IS NOT THE CAUSE. Reported from a side-by-side: retail's Seraphim faces the viewer at the campaign start, the port's does not. world/actor_state.gd seeds facing at PI/4 = cell (1,1) with a derivation in place (px=(x-y)*HW forces x=y; py=-(x+y)*HH puts the near side at x+y>0). CONTROLLED TEST: re-render the same frame with the seed flipped 180 degrees to PI/4+PI, everything else identical. The hero does NOT turn around -- she very nearly DISAPPEARS, leaving a few scattered pixels around x 490..520, y 290..330 where a whole figure stood. A yaw that deletes a rig is not a rotation, so the seed value is the wrong thing to argue about and view/rig_placement.gd owns the defect. The suspect line is its own: apply() writes set_bone_pose_position(i, spin * (root_rest_origins[k] * rig_scale) + local_offset), rotating each parentless bone's REST ORIGIN by the yaw. That is a pure turn-in-place only when those origins lie on the spin axis; otherwise a yaw is a spin PLUS a translation, which is exactly a figure leaving frame in pieces. The comment above it asserts the opposite ('The rig spins about its own origin, so the rest offset turns with it'). UNVERIFIED: the parentless-bone origins themselves were not read -- a probe keyed on a 'parent' field returned 0 parentless bones for both SERAPHIM.GRN and SeraBoots01.grn, so the key is wrong (model_view.gd uses 'parent_effective') and the probe proved nothing. That measurement is the next step and it is cheap. RELATED AND STILL OPEN: the same rig renders correctly through --figure=, which builds no RigPlacement, so every in-world hero defect now points at this one modifier.

RETRACTION OF ROW 997'S MECHANISM. That row suspected view/rig_placement.gd of turning a yaw into a spin PLUS a translation, because apply() writes set_bone_pose_position(i, spin * (root_rest_origins[k] * rig_scale) + local_offset), which rotates each parentless bone's rest origin. MEASURED, and it is false. Driving the production PlayerView and its own apply() over SERAPHIM.GRN: the rig has EXACTLY ONE parentless bone, __Root, and its rest origin is (0.000, 0.000, 0.000), so spin * (0 * scale) is 0 at every angle and the rotation cannot translate anything. The yaw is also demonstrably a clean turn about the rig vertical: the posed-bone extent at yaw 0 is (10.40, 29.82, 95.63) and at yaw PI/2 it is (29.82, 10.40, 95.63) -- the two horizontal axes exchange while the 95.63 vertical is untouched -- and the posed-bone centre drifts at most 1.72 units across four quarter turns of a 95-unit rig, which is the body's own asymmetry rather than displacement. The row-997 render in which a 180-degree seed flip 'nearly deleted' the hero is real but was misread: at the contrast that frame is rendered at (see the lighting row below) the figure is barely separable from the floor at any angle, and a control at all four cardinal facings shows the same thin figure each time. rig_placement.gd needs no change and its comment 'The rig spins about its own origin, so the rest offset turns with it' is correct as written.

THE PORT'S IN-WORLD HERO IS NOT HOLLOW, NOT FLATTENED AND NOT MIS-FACED -- SHE IS UNDER-LIT ON AN OVER-LIT FLOOR, AND THAT ONE FACT RETIRES FOUR SEPARATE THEORIES. Controls run at the real Seraphim start (cell 3236,2511) at 1024x768 against the retail drive capture of the same frame. (1) MATERIAL: rendering with TRANSPARENCY_DISABLED + DEPTH_DRAW_ALWAYS, and again with TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA_SCISSOR at 0.5, is just as sparse as the shipped TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA -- so the alpha pass player_view.gd sets for depth sorting is not the cause. (2) FACING: all four cardinal facings (1,1), (-1,-1), (1,-1), (-1,1) render the same thin figure, so no yaw makes her read solid. (3) GARMENTS: with _dress_player disabled entirely, the BARE body draws as a recognisable Seraphim at essentially retail's height, so the body mesh is present and correctly posed and is not being hidden by what is worn over it. (4) TRANSPARENCY, measured rather than eyeballed: sampling the torso column x 505..530 at six heights, ZERO of 26 pixels per row match the ground colour at any height, so the torso is opaque -- the 'see-through' reading was wrong. WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG IS EXPOSURE. The port's floor in this interior reads [188.8, 179.1, 166.3] where retail's reads [108.4, 101.3, 92.5] -- the port is 1.75x too bright on the ground. Meanwhile the port's torso means about [98, 89, 78], i.e. the hero is far DARKER than her own floor, while retail's torso at about [112, 91, 76] sits at roughly the same brightness as hers. A correctly shaped, under-lit character on an over-lit floor reads exactly as the 'thin hollow wire figure' every previous investigation described, and it also explains the earlier saturation-and-brightness silhouette measurements (39% vs 63% fill, p90 146 vs 202) which all thresholded on exactly the quantity that is wrong. NOT THE PER-CORNER LIGHT BYTES: sector_view.gd already reads +0x14..0x17 (line 419) and those bytes run 195..255, far too narrow to darken an interior floor to 108. Retail must apply a further sector or global ambient term -- cSectorEnvironment's climate/region (row 960) is the obvious place to look and is now the highest-value open lead for hero parity.

RETRACTION OF ROW 999'S CENTRAL CLAIM. That row reported the port's interior floor at [188.8, 179.1, 166.3] against retail's [108.4, 101.3, 92.5] and concluded the port renders terrain 1.75x too bright, making the hero read hollow by contrast. THE REFERENCE PATCH WAS NOT FLOOR. It was y300-320 x560-585, which lands on a bright table the two frames render differently; the two images differ there by a mean 232 per pixel, which is precisely why it looked like a global exposure error. Measured properly over ten 16x16 patches chosen clear of the hero and the furniture, port and retail agree almost exactly: SIX of the ten are byte-identical (ratio 1.000 in all three channels) and the whole frame agrees within 12/255 on 71.35% of pixels. Terrain lighting is therefore NOT globally wrong, and the per-corner light bytes the port already applies (sector_view.gd:419, value 255 at the start cell, so full brightness) are being applied correctly. The residual frame difference is concentrated at x 640..1000, which is where retail additionally draws an NPC, a chest, a quest marker, a minimap and a different taskbar -- content the port does not have -- not a lighting term. WHAT SURVIVES FROM ROW 999, because it was measured separately and independently: the torso is opaque (0 of 26 pixels per row match ground at six heights), the bare body draws correctly when _dress_player is disabled, no material transparency mode changes the result, and no facing makes the figure read solid. WHAT IS RETRACTED: the 1.75x figure, the 'over-lit floor' framing, and the inference that cSectorEnvironment's climate/region is the highest-value lead for hero parity. PROCESS NOTE, the same one row 669 recorded: a single reference patch chosen by eye is not a control. Ten patches cost nothing and would have caught this before it was logged.

SACRED DOES NOT LIGHT CHARACTERS WITH LIGHTS, AND THE PORT NOW DOES NOT EITHER. Recovered from the Windows retail build, sub_41B5B0: character lighting starts from a BASE AMBIENT OF 32/255, adds a contribution per nearby light source attenuated by squared distance (via an inverse-sqrt approximation using the classic 0x5F3759DF magic constant, visible as the literal 1597463007), clamps the running total to 255, and uses that ONE SCALAR to index three 256-entry per-channel colour ramps at object offsets +65048/+66072/+67096, whose output then modulates the mesh; an optional caller colour multiplies on top. NO SURFACE NORMAL APPEARS ANYWHERE IN IT -- there is no diffuse term, no specular and no light direction. The port was instead lighting the hero with two DirectionalLight3Ds from main.gd:_ensure_rig_light, a different model, which drew a harshly directional figure that four separate investigations today read as hollow, flattened, mis-faced or wrongly skinned. view/player_view.gd now sets SHADING_MODE_UNSHADED on every hero surface. CONSISTENCY ARGUMENT, not a fresh guess: the terrain path already works retail's way -- unshaded, multiplied by the cell's own +0x14 light byte -- and already matches, with six of ten floor patches byte-identical to retail and 71.35% of the whole frame inside 12/255. MEASURED: skin, hair, the white boots and the gold all move onto retail's values, and the hero-pixel highlight deficit closes, V p90 going 119.0 to 181.3 against retail's 139.7. IT NOW OVERSHOOTS BY 41.7 AND THAT IS LEFT IN PLACE. No scalar was fitted to hide it, because the two masks are different sizes (3995 port pixels against 5504 retail, the port's figure being separately known too small at 102 px against 136) so percentile-to-percentile ratios do not compare the same pixels -- exactly the fallacy behind rows 979 and 999. The honest remedy is the missing half of the mechanism: retail's ramp, plus the per-cell light value feeding it. At this start cell that byte is 255, so full albedo is the correct INPUT and the ramp is what would bring the top end down. STILL OPEN and unaffected: the hero draws at 0.75 of retail's height (row 996), and _ensure_rig_light still serves creature and NPC rigs, which have not been moved to this model or measured against retail. All 40 checks and parity/verify.gd pass.

CHARACTER SCALE IS NOW A RETAIL MEASUREMENT INSTEAD OF A BORROWED PROXY. PlayerView sized every rig with SectorView.SORTCUBE_PX / REF_HEIGHT = 96.0/73.0 = 1.3151, and its own comment admitted the numerator was the DEPTH-SORT PROXY BOX borrowed for want of a measurement ('no retail capture has measured an actual character height yet'). Replaced by a new PlayerView.RETAIL_HUMANOID_PX = 133.0, giving 133.0/73.0 = 1.8219. SORTCUBE_PX is deliberately untouched -- sector_view still builds its sort cube from it and that sorting is verified, so repurposing it would have moved two things at once. THE PROJECTION WAS PINNED FIRST, so scale was the only free variable: ortho size 768 over a 768-px viewport is one world unit to one pixel, confirmed rather than assumed, because at 1.3151 a 74.3-unit SERAPHIM.GRN predicts 97.7 px drawn and the render measured 97. MEASURED AGAINST RETAIL, same cell 3236,2511, same 1024x768 frame: shoulder-to-sole 77 px port against 110 retail (implied scale 1.879), belt-to-sole 62 against 83 (implied 1.761); mean 1.82, so 133 = 1.82 * 73. Two interior landmarks rather than overall height because retail's hair rises into the stone wall behind her, so that silhouette cannot be segmented from the floor, and her drop shadow -- which the port does not draw at all -- contaminates the bottom. VERIFIED BY RE-RENDER, which is the point of choosing a predictive landmark: the rebuilt figure measures shoulder-to-sole 112 px against retail's 110, within 2% of the 106.7 predicted. CAVEATS STATED IN THE CODE: one class, one frame, and the two landmarks disagree by 6%, so this is +/-4% rather than exact, and row 797's warning still applies -- the factor is global and preserves each model's own units, so it must not be re-tuned to close the separate wolf/elf ratio gap. WHAT THE LARGER FIGURE MAKES OBVIOUS: the hero's TORSO IS NOT DRAWN. Head, hair, both arms, both legs and the boots all render, and the chest, abdomen and hips are seen straight through to the floor. This is the 'sparse silhouette' every earlier pass reported, now unmistakable at the corrected size, and it survives with garments disabled entirely, so it belongs to SERAPHIM.GRN's own torso surface rather than to anything worn. All 40 checks and parity/verify.gd pass.

CORRECTION TO ROW 1002, WHICH CLAIMED THE HERO'S TORSO IS NOT DRAWN. It is drawn. Sampling the chest and abdomen band (x 505..532) on the corrected-scale render, rows y268 through y300 return 0 or 1 pixel in 28 matching the floor colour at any height; floor only appears from y308 downward, which is the gap between her legs and is correct. The geometry was never in doubt either: the world and --figure paths build the identical mesh, 1421 verts and 2054 tris over six surfaces, with Sera_body.tga present as surface 1 at 358 triangles in both. WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG IS CONTRAST, and it is why five separate passes today read this as hollow, flattened, see-through or missing. The port's torso lands at about [106, 94, 81] against a floor of [102, 85, 85] -- within a few counts on every channel, so it is very nearly floor-coloured and the eye separates it only at the silhouette edges. Retail's torso in the same band sits at about [150, 135, 118], well clear of the same floor. So the port's character is not too dark globally -- after the unshaded change its bright regions OVERSHOOT retail (V p90 181 against 140) while its torso UNDERSHOOTS badly. That is a distribution mismatch rather than a level mismatch, and a single scalar cannot fix it, which is the second time today that conclusion has been reached from the other direction. The likely remainder is the half of retail's model still unimplemented: the 256-entry per-channel colour ramps sub_41B5B0 indexes with its accumulated scalar (row 1001), which is exactly the mechanism that would redistribute rather than rescale. PROCESS NOTE: row 1002's torso claim was made from a rendered image and not from pixel values, one turn after row 1000 retracted a claim made the same way. Sample before asserting.

RETAIL'S CHARACTER LIGHT RAMP IS RECOVERED, BUILDER AND CONSTANTS. Row 1001 established that sub_41B5B0 indexes three 256-entry per-channel tables with an accumulated light scalar but left the tables unread. Their writer is sub_417FA0 at 0x4188C0-0x4189ED, found by byte-searching the Windows retail image for the table displacements: 0xFE18 (65048) appears only at 0x41b9ad and 0x41b9c4, both reads inside sub_41B5B0, while 0x10218 (66072) appears once more at 0x418966 -- the writer. It is ONE loop, i from 0 to 255, filling all six tables (two sets of three) from four float constants read out of .rdata: flt_88F7C4 = 0.25, flt_88F914 = 64.0, flt_88F910 = 1/3, flt_88F90C = 0.75. The recovered rule is base = clamp(sub_81C9E0(), 0, 1) * 64, then per entry R = G = floor(i*0.25 + base + 64) into the tables at +0xFE18 and +0x10218, and B = floor(i/3 + base + 64) into +0x10618; the second set at +0x12E18 onward is a separate neutral ramp floor(i*0.75 + 64) on all three channels, selected by the flag at +40460 and not the path the world draws through. BLUE CLIMBS FASTER THAN RED AND GREEN, so the ramp COOLS the image as it brightens rather than scaling it -- which is why neither a scalar nor a gamma could reproduce the mismatch, a conclusion reached twice today from opposite directions before the table was read. APPLIED at full light only: i = 255 with the brightness setting at maximum gives R = G = 191 and B = 213, hence PlayerView.RETAIL_LIGHT_FULL = (191, 191, 213)/255. That is correct for this frame and no other -- the Seraphim's start cell carries terrain light byte 255 with no dynamic light near her; a rig in shadow needs i taken from the cell and the ramp evaluated per rig, which is NOT done. MEASURED on the hero mask with both figures finally at matching size: mean absolute error against retail across p10/p25/p50/p75/p90 falls from 0.362 to 0.230, with p90 landing at 0.980 of retail (was 1.241) and p75 at 1.188 (was 1.500). ALSO FIXED, and found by that same measurement: p10 through p50 did not move at all on the first attempt, because PlayerView's material loop ran once in setup() over the BODY mesh while attach_skinned builds every worn garment as its own ModelView with its own MeshInstance3D, and _dress_player runs after construction. The treatment is now a _style/_style_tree pair called from wear() and equip() as well. All 40 checks and parity/verify.gd pass.

WITH EXPOSURE, SIZE, WINGS AND CONTRAST ALL SETTLED, THE REMAINING IN-WORLD HERO GAP IS LOCALISED AND MEASURED. Row-by-row silhouette occupancy over a fixed window (y268..392, x490..552, figure = differs from the local floor by >55) with both figures now at matching size and matching mean brightness: port fills 30.7% of the window against retail's 48.9%, and the deficit is NOT spread evenly. Chest y268..300 is close (port 58/36/20/18/20 against retail 60/41/26/30/21) and legs and boots y340..364 actually match or exceed retail (31/33/22/27 against 34/31/19/19), but the HIPS AND WAIST COLLAPSE: at y308, y316, y324 and y332 the port is 10, 17, 4 and 3 pixels wide against retail's 24, 27, 23 and 20. The port's legs are visibly splayed with an empty gap between them where retail's stand together. The bottom rows y372..388 diverge too (port 27/16/3 against retail 41/57/61) but that is retail's DROP SHADOW, which the port does not draw at all, and is not a body difference. HYPOTHESIS, STATED AS ONE: this is a POSE difference rather than missing geometry -- a bind pose stands legs apart and arms out, an idle clip brings them together, and the port's figure has exactly the bind-pose look. It is NOT yet established. AND A CORRECTION THAT BEARS ON IT: row 999 recorded that rendering with and without --noanim produced 'the same figure'. That was an eyeball judgement and it was wrong -- the two frames differ in 3776 pixels over a bounding box of x529..625, y100..325, so the clip IS reaching the render. Whether it reaches the LEGS specifically is the open question, and the cheap test is to measure leg separation with the clip on and off rather than to look at it. That is the third eye-based claim to fail a measurement today (rows 1000 and 1003 being the others), and the standing lesson is the same: sample before asserting.

ROW 1005'S POSE HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED, AND THE MEASUREMENT REPLACES IT WITH A NARROWER ONE. Rendering the current build with and without --noanim at the campaign start: the clip DOES pose the rig -- 640 of 7688 window pixels differ (8.3%) across rows y268..385, so animation reaches the skeleton and the figure is not frozen in its bind pose. But the hips barely move between the two, 10.2 pixels mean width with the clip and 9.0 without, against retail's 24.4. A pose difference cannot be the explanation when both poses miss by the same 2.4x. SECOND CONTROL, dressing disabled entirely at current settings: the six worn garments add 531 pixels in total (6.9% of the window), and almost none of it lands where the deficit is -- 87 px in the head/chest band y268..299, only 41 px in the waist/hips band y300..331, against 258 px at the thighs and 145 px at the shins and boots. Bare and dressed measure 10.0 and 10.2 at the hips and 16.6 and 16.6 at the chest, i.e. the garments contribute ZERO chest width. Retail is 24.4 and 25.1. So within the sampled window the port's body is markedly narrower than retail's through the whole trunk, and what is worn does not close it. STATED LIMIT, because the obvious next inference cannot yet be drawn: this is measured in a 62-px window (x490..552) that contains both figures' cores, and widening it to 110 px does NOT settle whether the port's arms splay outside it -- at the wider bound port and retail return IDENTICAL spans at y268, y276, y284 and y292 (468..577, 468..565, 468..557), which is shared scene content being segmented, not either figure. So 'the trunk geometry is missing' and 'the arms are held wide and carry the width outside the window' are both still live, and separating them needs a segmentation anchored on the figure rather than on a fixed box. NOT ASSERTED EITHER WAY. Three eye-based claims already failed measurement today (rows 1000, 1003, 1005); this one stops at what the pixels support.

PlayerView.face read world -Z as the direction towards the camera when it is +Z, turning every character a clean 180 degrees so the hero spawned with her back to the player. IsoCamera sits at Vector3(p.x, p.y, 1000.0) unrotated and so looks down world -Z, and SectorView independently lays nearer cells at larger z via pz = (x + y) * DEPTH_STEP; both make +Z the direction towards the viewer. Measured through the production face() on all seven class bodies with the axis taken both ways: the posed forward, mean (Toe0 - Foot) over both feet mapped into world space, keeps an identical horizontal part under both signs and only flips z, from -0.511 to +0.511 on SERAPHIM and likewise on GLADIATOR, MAGICIAN and DWARF. facing_check passed throughout because every assertion it made was relative - four distinct headings, opposites 180 apart, equal 90 degree steps - and all of those survive rotating the whole set by 180; it is now anchored by asserting the posed forward has z > 0 when facing cell (1,1), which fails on the old sign and passes on the new. Separately the class bodies resolve every draw batch to a real image (0 untextured surfaces on all that build), so the missing textures are not hero skins; DUNKELELVE entry 402 fails to build at all on an ambiguous mesh-to-FormMeshBone pairing, and no liquid rendering exists anywhere in view/ or world/.

The port never drew Sacred's animated liquid at all: Walkable.is_liquid already marked the cells from WldxEntry +0x1f's high nibble (9 or 10) but SectorView drew their ordinary ground tile, and on the open sea that tile is ISO00 alone -- one flat 256x256 image, mean colour (0.52,0.51,0.43), repeated over all 4096 cells of a sector, which is why the sea read as grey-tan ground. RECOVERED THE 14-MATERIAL TABLE BY READING THE LINUX BINARY THIS INSTALL PAIRS WITH: sub_83A6572 builds it as 14 unrolled blocks 0x63 bytes apart, each sprintf-ing a "%s%.2d.TGA" format string and storing frames to [edi+esi*4+0x9118+k*0xD8]; block 0 stores at 0x9118 and block 13 at 0x9C10, and 0x9C10-0x9118 = 0xAF8 = 13*0xD8 exactly, so block order is record order. The table is 0 B_WATER, 1 C_WATER, 2 D_WATER, 3 A_LAVA, 4 B_LAVA, 5 C_LAVA, 6 A_SCHWEFEL, 7 D_LAVA, 8 E_WATER, 9 F_WATER, 10 G_WATER, 11 E_LAVA, 12 B_WATER, 13 B_WATER -- B_WATER at three indices, matching its three xrefs where every other string has one, and 12 distinct stems for 14 records. Each block also writes flags at record +0xCC and +0xD4; +0xCC is 1 for exactly idx 0,1,2,3,10,11, the same six indices row 669 recovered from the WINDOWS build, so two separately-compiled binaries agree on the order. Row 669's NAMES are shifted one slot against this and should not be used; its flag indices are correct. Every one of the 14 stems resolves in texture.pak with 50 frames except C_LAVA and A_SCHWEFEL at 20, which validates the table against shipped data independently of the disassembly. THE PER-SECTOR MATERIAL ID IS STILL UNSOURCED: the consumer at sub_80E3EB2 reads it as mov eax,[edi+17Ch] then mov cl,[eax+0F7h] for nibble 0x90 and mov bl,[eax+0F8h] for nibble 0xA0, so it is per sector with two ids, but the file that block loads from is unfound -- sectors.keyx +0xF7/+0xF8 are 0 in all 6050 records, and the wldx tail past the entry grid is the region table and yields values up to 209 against a 0..13 range. Both were refused against a condition stated before looking. Shipped with the id pinned to 0 (B_WATER, which holds three of fourteen slots and is what a zero-initialised field reads), isolated in Liquid.material_id so it is one line when the source turns up; it will be wrong on lava maps. Added shaders/liquid.gdshader (frame-indexed sampler2DArray, screen-space tiling UV over 128 px, per-corner light in gamma space like terrain) and a third sector surface at DEPTH_STEP*0.9, above every floor.pak overlay and under the next cell's ground. checks/liquid_check.gd gates the table against the pak, the marker against Walkable.is_liquid cell for cell, the quad count, and the depth ordering. Animation rate is NOT measured -- 12 fps is a placeholder.

The FormMeshBone pairing was never a matching problem: the FILE states it. Each FormMesh node (0xCA5E0C03) -- the parent its FormMeshBoneSection (0xCA5E0C09) actually hangs under -- carries one payload int32, the 1-BASED index of the Mesh node its bone list belongs to, counted over ALL Mesh nodes in directory order including non-drawable ones. Found on DUNKELELVE.GRN entry 402, the body whose tie no other rule could break: needs [1,9,5,2,11,10,39] against list sizes [39,5,2,10,10,11,1] admits two matchings differing in which size-10 list serves the meshes needing 9 and 10, the shipped min-over-list geometry scores them 26.26 vs 25.58 (ratio 1.026 against the 1.15 margin), and a sharper dominant-bone scorer not only stays under margin but prefers the OPPOSITE matching -- the payloads [7 3 4 6 2 5 1] answer it outright, and the answer is the one the weaker scorer favoured. Validated over the corpus before being trusted: on all 971 weight-declaring entries the payloads are unique, in range, and hand every drawable mesh a list satisfying size >= highest+1 (six entries carry non-drawable meshes, which is what fixed the index space as all-mesh rather than drawable-only); via pairing_verdicts the reference decides all 1567 entries with pair inputs and agrees by content with the strict size rule on every one of the 1349 it decides alone, zero disagreements. Landed as Models._pair_by_reference, primary over the strict rule and the geometric tiebreaker which both survive as fallbacks; the 79 entries both fallbacks refused now decode, decode count 920 -> 955 of 971 declaring (the 16 left are weight-stream defects, not pairing ones), and all seven class bodies build for the first time -- DUNKELELVE renders as a coherent figure, hair and torso distinct, the exact pair the tie was about. bonepair_check pins reference coverage at TOTAL and reference-vs-strict agreement; weights_check and compose_check pins raised deliberately per their own instructions. The earlier findings kept their truth but not their framing: positional pairing is still refuted, containment under MESH nodes is still false -- the sections were never children of the Mesh, they are children of the FormMesh, and the FormMesh names the Mesh.

FOUND the per-sector liquid material id source that row 1008 shipped without: it is IN THE KEYX RECORD ITSELF. The retail binary has two sector-index loaders behind the same SECTORS.PAK banner -- sub_80EF028 reads 512-byte records and seeks a separate 0x100 environment block by a stored file offset, malloc'ing per sector, while sub_80EF4EE reads the 768-byte records the shipped sectors.keyx actually has and finds the environment block EMBEDDED: it memcpy's record bytes 0x1E9..0x2E8 (489..744) into a preallocated count*0x100 arena and hangs each slice off the runtime sector at +0x17C -- the exact pointer the liquid draw consumes at +0xF7/+0xF8. So the two per-sector liquid material ids are keyx record bytes 736 and 737. Validated against the discrimination stated in row 1008 before wiring: over all 1360 liquid sectors every value is in 0..13, the open sea reads 0 = B_WATER (1012 sectors), rivers read C_WATER, the underworld reads the lavas and A_SCHWEFEL, non-liquid sectors carry ids too (never consulted), and 22 sectors carry two DIFFERENT ids at once -- e.g. (0,11) water+E_LAVA, (3,9) A_LAVA+F_WATER -- which is why the format keeps two bytes and why the one-material-per-sector shortcut had to go. The two candidates row 1008 refused stay refused for the right reason: +0xF7 as an absolute keyx record offset (247) is the padding gap, and the wldx tail is the region table; the block lives at record offset 0x1E9 + 0xF7. Wired: Common.KEY_ENV/KEY_LIQ9/KEY_LIQ10, World.liquid_id(gx,gy,nibble), Liquid.material_id now reads the file, SectorView emits up to two liquid surfaces per sector (packed arrays are value types, so two named accumulators rather than a map). Verified through the production builder: sector (2,51) draws 3209 A_LAVA quads, (17,14) draws two surfaces B_WATER+A_LAVA at 72+30 quads, sea (47,67) 4096 B_WATER; liquid_check now also gates all 6050 records' ids in 0..13 and the sea's id at 0. The earlier 512-record loader is the map-format historian's lead for why the ENV block exists at all: the older format kept it out of line.

PARTIAL RETRACTION OF ROW 1008: its material table was one slot off, and its claim that row 669's names were shifted is WRONG -- row 669's names were right all along. The initialiser opens with TWO ADJACENT B_WATER blocks (pushes at 0x83a7bf5 and 0x83a7c58); row 1008 segmented one push per block and slid everything after slot 0 down by one. The truth is pinned by the frame counts: each block stores its count to record +0xC8, the values are 0x32 everywhere except 0x14 at records 6 and 7, and the pak's only 20-frame sets are C_LAVA and A_SCHWEFEL -- which land on 6 and 7 only under the corrected order B_WATER,B_WATER,C_WATER,D_WATER,A_LAVA,B_LAVA,C_LAVA,A_SCHWEFEL,D_LAVA,E_WATER,F_WATER,G_WATER,E_LAVA,B_WATER. Under it the +0xCC reflective set {0,1,2,3,10,11} is all waters bar E_WATER(9) and B_WATER(13), which is row 669's own parenthetical verbatim. liquid_check now pins 20 frames to indices 6 and 7 exactly, the assertion that would have caught this. NEW MEASUREMENTS from the same pass: (1) CADENCE -- the draw picks frame = ((ms >> 1) & 0x3FF) * count / 1024, so every set loops in a fixed 2048 ms regardless of length, ~24.4 fps for 50 frames, ~9.8 for 20; there is no per-record delay field, only the count. (2) ALPHA -- record +0xD0 is a SIGNED alpha multiplier (-12 on B/C/D/G_WATER and rec13, -24 on F_WATER, -255 on every lava, schwefel and E_WATER) applied to the cell's signed corner bytes +0x10..13 and clamped to 0..255; on liquid cells those bytes hold DEPTH (open sea -20, shallows rising to 0, verified empirically on three sectors), so negative-times-negative reads opaque over deep water and fades to nothing at the shoreline. The liquid surface itself is drawn FLAT: the depth shapes the bed, and the port feeding it into the surface heights had sunk the water into its own bowl. (3) +0xD4 is set on every lava plus schwefel -- hot, unconsumed by the port. Wired: corrected table, 2048 ms shader cycle, per-vertex depth alpha with TRANSPARENCY, flat surface; coast sector (46,38) renders water fading into its sandy banks. STILL OPEN: the reflection pass -- geometry read (mirrored ambient-modulated quad gated on +0xCC, intensity -8*corner-depth times ambient>>24) but its BLEND STATE goes through sub_83B41F2 render-state calls that are untraced, and a wrong blend looks worse than the pass's absence.

Outdoor walkability (row 990) stays OPEN after a bounded binary session; what it earned is leads, not the rule. NAMED PATHFINDING CLASSES EXIST in the Linux binary's RTTI: cPath, cPathAstar, cPathFloodfill (typeinfo names at 0x8728608/0x872860f/0x872861c) -- but no vtable byte-references the typeinfo objects, so the classes must be reached through their methods, not their tables; finding cPathAstar's neighbour-step test is the direct route to the movement rule and remains the best next move. RUNTIME CELL ACCESSORS IDENTIFIED: sub_80ED194(world, pos) returns the cell at a position and sub_80ED1F2(world, pos, layer) the cell on a specific layer; both are consumed by sub_8162606, the link-creature-into-world function, which tests cell[0x1F] & 3 -- low-nibble bits 0-1 -- to decide structure membership, and by sub_811577A, which switches on the full low nibble and treats class 9 with the +0x1E structure bit specially (room/visibility assignment, not movement). So the +0x1F low nibble is a CLASS retail does consult at runtime, just not (yet found) for walk-blocking. The keyx environment block has more live fields than the two liquid ids: sub_80D6CD6 returns env+0xD7 to ~40 gameplay callers and sub_80D6CFE another byte to three. NOT firing here: the &3 or low-nibble tests as walkability predictors -- row 990 already measured the low nibble against the region-grid navmesh and it does not beat the base rate. Untested and promising: outdoors nothing per-cell may block at all, with collision coming entirely from static-object FOOTPRINT chains plus liquid plus the region grids -- footprint coverage was never in row 990's predictor list, and Armalion's unported second branch (*(DWORD*)cell & 4 -> static chain lookup) points the same way.

Retail's click-to-walk player speed is 1.4-1.6 cells/s, measured twice from the game itself; the port's Movement.CELLS_PER_TICK placeholder of 4.0 cells/s ran the hero ~2.7x too fast and is now 1.5. METHOD, after three failed approaches taught the constraints: load the harness save through the menu walker, click-walk the hero along a single iso axis over open grass, capture the framebuffer every 500 ms via the autopilot shim's SACRED_SHOT, and phase-correlate consecutive frames -- the camera tracks the player, so its accumulated scroll IS the walk. Two independent runs of the same route netted (277,139) and (275,138) screen px, a pure 2:1 iso-axis ratio = 5.77 cells at the 48 px/cell x-step, over ~4.1 s of visible motion. Zoom pinned from the frames themselves by sprite height (~133 px = the nominal-zoom humanoid), not assumed. WHAT FAILED AND WHY, so nobody repeats it: (a) SACRED_WATCH's row-812 heap offset 0x2a3b70 is NOT the player position under this load route -- the pond-side screenshots stayed pixel-identical while the watched pair jumped 111 cells, so it read the click DESTINATION; the heap layout is not reproducible across runs (row 808 said so) and any absolute offset must be re-derived per process life. (b) Whole-second phase correlation shows the camera, not the hero: the camera follows with a catch-up dead-zone, producing zero-motion windows and burst windows -- only TOTAL displacement over a bracketed walk is trustworthy, never per-window rates. (c) Clicks at the screen bottom land on the taskbar and clicks into trees or across the pond path nowhere; the working route was open grass up-left of the Valor's-Fortress-save pond at (250,130). Residual uncertainty about +-0.15 cells/s from the 500 ms bracketing of the walk interval, and the walked path's small bend means net-under-counts path length slightly; a tighter number wants an in-process position re-scan (SACRED_SELFTEST's differential filter) in the same run as the walk.

TWO FINDINGS FROM THE FIRST REAL TWO-ENGINE COMPARISON (tools/drive/session.sh, port vs retail at the Seraphim new-game spawn, 29.3 percent pixel delta). FIRST, THE DAYS-OLD 'THIN HERO' WAS A DEPTH CROSS-SECTION, NOT GEOMETRY: the rig is true 3D and placed at its cell the Seraphim's body spans world z 268.8..310.1 -- 826 DEPTH_STEPs -- while her own floor quad sits at z=287.4, through her waist; with the depth test on, every pixel of her behind that plane loses and what survives is a thin dark sliver. Row 1006's narrow-trunk measurements were measurements OF THIS ARTEFACT. Fix is one line in PlayerView._style: no_depth_test=true -- a character is a UNIT, ordered wholly by the transparent queue's sort (node position + the sorting_offset update() already maintains), exactly the regime the object sprites live in; terrain is opaque and drawn first so she stands on it, walls sort against her baseline so they still occlude her. She renders as a full textured body in-world for the first time in days. SECOND, RETRACTION OF ROW 1007'S FACING FIX: the to_camera axis belongs at -Z, the ORIGINAL sign, and the morning's +Z 'fix' turned every character the wrong way. The camera-axis argument (camera at z=+1000 unrotated, towards-viewer = +Z) and the toe-in-front-of-ankle anatomy argument are internally consistent AND both wrong about the pixels: rendering the dressed body at each yaw, the FACE (red lips, necklace -- unmistakable, where the bare figure's forward-hanging pigtails read as a face from behind and fooled three probe reads this morning) appears at the yaw the -Z axis produces, on the same frame retail shows its front. The composed Toe0-Foot vector on these rigs points BEHIND the visual front, so every conclusion built on it -- row 1007's A/B, the morning facing_check anchor -- was 180 degrees off while being internally reproducible. facing_check's anchor now pins the RENDER-calibrated convention (composed toe-forward z < 0 towards the viewer) with the calibration story in the comment. In-game verification through the production drive harness: hero faces the player at spawn, matching retail. PROCESS LESSON, the sharpest form of sample-before-asserting yet: a bone-math A/B that never renders can be reproducible, mutation-tested, corroborated by two binaries -- and still measure the wrong convention; for anything the player SEES, the pixel is the only admissible ground truth.

Retail's taskbar draws ONE skill and ONE spell slot at the Seraphim's spawn, not five a side, and the ornamental rails carry the slots rather than spanning the screen. The count is readable straight off a frame through the placement formula this port already transcribed: x = 394 + 66*(i - n) puts the leftmost skill slot at 328 in retail's capture, and 394 - 66n = 328 gives n = 1; the spell side agrees independently, since x = 640 + 66*i would put a second spell slot at 706 and retail draws bare wall there. The rails follow from the same count -- each butts the console (397 left edge, 627 right) and tiles outward one piece per slot, which puts the right rail's end at 627 + 104 = 731 against retail's measured 732. The port had been drawing five empty 63x63 rings a side from x 64 to 904 and tiling rails from x 32 and x 890, i.e. eight spurious sprites and ten spurious rail tiles laid across open terrain, together 13% of the whole two-engine frame delta. Separately the day/night dial was rendering at its texture's own 128x128 rather than the declared 56: a TextureRect's minimum-size recalculation is deferred, so assigning size before add_child (and, measured, after it too) is clamped straight back up, and the dial painted a night-sky annulus across the entire console. Baking the size into the image is what makes it stick. Also removed: gfx id 82, a 33x33 button this port placed at (898,686), where retail's spawn frame draws bare cobblestones.

The object painter order was reading the wrong end of every sprite. static.pak stores a placement's TOP-LEFT corner, and sector_view sorted on that stored y, so a 389-pixel chapel pillar was ordered as though it stood a whole sprite-height further back than it does and everything nearer than its ROOFLINE painted over its stonework -- the ivy-across-the-pillar the two-engine compare had been showing for days. The fix is to sort at the sprite's foot (stored y minus sprite height, read from mixed.pak's 16-byte header via a new size_of() so a sector can be ordered without decoding its art twice), and it is not a new convention: the per-vertex pz has always been (-p.y + size.y), the baseline, so the geometry already carried the right depth and only the submission order overruled it. The height cannot be added unconditionally. A WIDE sprite is not one object standing at one spot but a structure spanning many ground cells, and the chapel's 460x889 interior shell reaches further south than the furniture standing inside it, so at its foot it sorted in front of its own contents and painted out the wine rack. Gating on sprite width fixes that; STRUCTURE_W was swept and 192-256 is a real minimum (17.53% at no height, 14.24% at 192 and 256, 16.85% at 400, 21.42% with no gate at all). The obvious alternative -- give the height only to sprites far taller than wide -- was measured and REFUTED at every ratio from 1.5 to 4.0. Still open: a candle standing on a wine rack's shelf is covered by the rack, because a single painter key cannot order a sprite that contains other sprites; retail draws those in authored order and that order has not been recovered.

mixed.pak's header dx/dy at +8 is NOT a placement hotspot, and applying it was the single largest error left in the port's frame: removing it took the whole-frame delta against retail's own spawn capture from 23.97% to 14.24% in one line. Measured across the corpus, dx/dy is exactly the NEGATION of the sprite's own minimum tile dst corner -- Bench 2 carries anchor (0,-7) and its tiles begin at dst y 7, Bench 1 carries (0,-36) beginning at 36, MINI_BLUE_4 carries (-4,0) beginning at x 4, and every sprite whose tiles already start at the corner carries (0,0). So adding it to the placement CANCELS the offset the dst rects already encode, re-seating each sprite on its bounding box instead of on the frame it was authored in. The tiles' dst rects are complete on their own: they go down at the stored position and nowhere else. What made this survive so long is that every KLOSTER_KAPELLE structure piece has a zero anchor, so the chapel's walls, floor and pillars lined up perfectly while the benches sat 7 pixels high and the small props each drifted a few -- the error was invisible exactly where it was zero, and the benches were the only isolated high-contrast sprites on open floor where it could be seen. It also masked a real signal: the STRUCTURE_W sweep taken before this fix showed a flat plateau and no minimum, and the same sweep afterwards has a clear one. What dx/dy IS for remains unrecovered; nothing needs it to place a sprite.

The Seraphim spawn scene now differs from retail by 13.55% of pixels (tools/drive/session.sh, same script and millisecond, any-nonzero-difference metric), down from 29.28% at the start of the session and stable across 0/2000/4000 ms. Open floor away from any object matches at a mean absolute error of 0.00, i.e. the terrain, its overlays and the camera are exact where nothing is drawn over them, so what remains is enumerable rather than diffuse. By measured share of the frame: the taskbar's remaining interface (the two FILLED art slots, the console's rune ring and the day/night dial's shape) about 1pp, whose art is not in GUI_MAIN_01..06 -- template-matching retail's own 63x63 slot against all six sheets returns nothing under an error of 56, where the pieces that ARE there match under 1.0; the cobblestone terrain at the screen's bottom corners about 2pp, a different tile ARRANGEMENT rather than a shift or a shade, and not the floor.pak overlay stack, since raising OVERLAY_MAX from 8 to 32 changes nothing; the priest NPC retail spawns at the benches with a ?! bubble, about 1.2pp, which --npcs does not supply (it builds five thieves at radius 5 and none of them are in frame); and the hero's own pixels about 0.9pp, unmoved by dressing -- START_SET 6 and the bare rig score within 0.01pp of each other, so the outfit is not what differs. Two pieces of art were recovered by pixel-matching retail's frame against the decoded GUI sheets rather than from the gfx table: the portrait frame is GUI_MAIN_02's whole 95x107 corner block at (932,15), exact to the pixel including the clipping at the screen edge, and the potion belt's four unfilled slots are one shared empty flask at GUI_MAIN_05 (195,65) rather than four different coloured potions.

The largest single remaining difference in the start scene -- roughly 2% of the frame, the cobblestone ground at the screen's bottom corners -- is localised to the floor.pak OVERLAY layer, and it is a tile-selection problem rather than a placement, depth or shading one. Three measurements bracket it. Nulling floor_pak repaints 91.7% of that corner while --noobjects moves only 5.3% of it, so those pixels are overlay tiles and not base terrain and not object sprites. Raising OVERLAY_MAX from 8 to 32 changes the frame not at all, so no cell's overlay chain is being truncated. And disabling the overlay layer outright leaves the whole-frame delta unchanged at 13.59%, which is the informative one: the port is not failing to draw overlays there, it is drawing overlays that are as wrong as drawing none. A best-fit scalar over the region makes the error worse rather than better, so it is not a shade or a light either -- retail's cobbles are larger and more continuous where the port's are broken up by grass showing between them, which is a different tile per cell. Everything around it is exact: open floor away from any object matches retail at a mean absolute error of 0.00, so the terrain machinery, its overlay compositing and the camera are all correct where the selection happens to agree.

Three hypotheses for the corner-cobble overlay difference (row 1019) are measured and REFUTED, recorded so the next attempt starts past them. FIRST, the chain-walk restriction is not it. _tile_stack follows world/floor.pak's chain only while the next link equals self+1 and stops otherwise, which would silently truncate any chain that jumps; following an arbitrary in-range link instead changes the frame not at all, so no chain in this sector has a non-consecutive link and nothing is being truncated. SECOND, the composite ORDER is not it, and the current order is right: reversing the overlay pairs while leaving the ground tile first takes the corner from 74.4% of pixels differing to 92.2% and its mean absolute error from 34.2 to 43.4, so the chain's own order is the drawing order. THIRD, it is not a placement offset, which is what it looks like -- the port and retail draw visibly the same cobble texture with a large hexagonal stone sitting in different places, and eyeballing that reads as half a tile of vertical shift. An edge-correlation search over plus or minus 40 pixels in both axes returns dx=0, dy=0 as the best alignment with a correlation of only 0.45, i.e. no shift improves it and the two are simply not the same arrangement. For contrast the same measure returns 0.9965 sixty pixels away in the lower middle of the same sector. Both corners sit in sector 50,39 along with the region that matches at MAE 0.00, so it is not a sector-boundary or streaming-margin effect either. What is left is the per-cell overlay tile SELECTION: the port reads a different tile id for those cells than retail draws, everything downstream of the id being correct.

The taskbar's two filled art slots are not in GUI_MAIN_01..06 because each combat art carries its OWN texture. texture.pak holds 440 GUI_* entries that are not GUI_MAIN_*, named per art in German -- GUI_MOVE_ATTACKE, GUI_MOVES_KRIEGSSCHREI, GUI_SPELL_REIKI, GUI_SPELLS_HOELLENFEUER and so on, split across MOVE/MOVES/SPELL/SPELLS prefixes. Every one is a 256x256 texture with the art occupying only the TOP-LEFT corner, about 64x64, and the remaining seven eighths fully transparent, so anything that scales the whole texture into a 63x63 slot is comparing against mostly nothing. The slot as retail draws it is a COMPOSITE of at least three layers rather than a blit: the icon itself is a dark greyscale disc (GUI_MOVE_ATTACKE is crossed swords on a plain dark ground), while retail's spell slot shows those same swords in BLUE over a GREEN orb inside a gold ring. So a backing colour and a frame are applied over the icon, and the backing colour is presumably the art's school. That composite is why identification by pixel match fails from both directions, and both failures are worth recording: matching retail's 63x63 slot against the six GUI_MAIN sheets bottoms out at an error of 56 where genuine finds score under 1.0, and correlating icon SHAPE against the slot's inner disc across all 440 candidates tops out at 0.40 with implausible winners and no separation between them. Recovering these needs the compositing rule -- where the backing colour comes from and which ring art frames it -- not a better search.

CORRECTION TO ROWS 1019-1020: the corner-cobble mismatch is NOT a per-cell overlay tile-selection error. A live retail OpenGL trace, correlated by exact screen-space diamond centres and upload MD5 against the retail archives, shows retail consumes exactly the same WldxEntry +0x0c chains as the port, in the same order, with the same art ids, mask ids and texture.pak images at mapped cells (46,18), (47,18) and (48,18). The first failing family boundary ISO854/texture 6341 to ISO855/texture 6342 is real authored content in both engines; deleting it, substituting 6341, or shifting its atlas slot all worsen the global frame. The trace also pins both samplers to GL_LINEAR/GL_REPEAT and the masked combine to SRC_ALPHA/ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA. Port-only controls against the existing retail PNG refute exact numeric retail UVs, 92x47/100x49 and traced 96.4x48.4 overlay footprints, art-alpha blending for unmasked overlays, and a 1.0041667 global projection scale; every experiment was removed and the engine tree restored clean. The remaining mismatch is downstream of identical draw inputs, most likely a fixed-function-versus-Vulkan raster/sampling semantic or an untraced framebuffer state. Do not modify floor chain selection to chase these pixels.

VERIFIED: the copied Windows GOG 2.28 tree crashed on every Ancaria -> Seraphim -> Start Game transition because WORLD/SECTORS.WLDX and SECTORS.KEYX retained the retail media's ReadOnly attribute and granted ordinary Users read/execute only. Sacred requests a writable file mapping; the denied open left sector +0x6c null, and duplicated cell accessors converted that null base plus a valid offset into low invalid pointers (observed 0x10400 and 0xfb40). The official GOG-installed copies were writable controls. Clearing ReadOnly and granting built-in Users Modify on only those two copied files made explicit ReadWrite opens succeed. With the exact untouched Sacred.exe SHA256 DB9B86A44C8C1CC8C5ED9E3F427121AB8B4ED62760861E58995F10AF9D971E74, QXL, dgVoodoo2 2.87.3, nomovie and 1024x768 RDP, the fixed path reached the visible Seraphim start scene and tutorial, stayed responsive beyond 52 seconds, and produced no Application Error or WER event.

MEASURED: the Windows GOG 2.28 (eng) tree at builds/windows-disc/eng/extracted/app and the live Linux LGP install/ ship byte-identical world data. World/Floor.PAK sha256 7b0fabcbf3810b5a2bb3374ceb0ec40731a360e298af57170d5f416ec3e21744 and World/Triggers.PAK sha256 b4c51f80fe1bc0d114e1fc392d0c02bbbc809570e6c385db2e9150d06d47b8e3 match on both sides; Static.PAK, sectors.wldx and sectors.keyx match by size (78889320 / 63854322 / 4646656), as does every PAK/ entry except sound.pak (374.3M win vs 434.5M lin) and loading1.bmp. Consequence for method: the two retail oracles are two independent renderers over one set of bytes, so any pixel difference between them is code and any agreement is canonical content. This is the precondition for using the Windows VM oracle to arbitrate row 1022's open item, where retail and port consume identical draw inputs and the residual corner-cobble delta was attributed to fixed-function-versus-Vulkan raster/sampling semantics: Windows renders the same data through dgVoodoo2 DirectDraw/D3D, a second fixed-function backend, so Windows agreeing with Linux there makes the port the outlier and Windows disagreeing makes those pixels backend-dependent and not worth driving to zero. No claim is made yet about the rendered frames; only the input bytes were compared.

The curve's full contract is now read: it clamps a5 to [0,0.99], forms k=-ln(1-a5)/ln(a4+1), takes r=a2/a3 (or 10000 when |a3|<=0.001), computes f=1-1/(r+1)^k, writes f through the optional out-param a6 and RETURNS a2*f. That settles why to-hit discarded the return at 0x81fc701: to-hit passes &[ebp-0x1f0] as a6 and rolls against the fraction, damage passes NULL and keeps the product. Per channel dmg[i] = a2[i]*(1-1/(a2[i]/a3[i]+1)^k)*(100-resist[i])/100, with a2 raw damage, a3 the target's armour, 100 at 0x86e6b98 and 0.01 at 0x86e6b9c.
