The port's combat now transcribes RETAIL instead of the 2001 prerelease, and the last inferential step in the to-hit read is measured rather than assumed. WHICH BRANCH IS THE HIT, settled: fcomp sets C0 when st(0) < operand, so `jne 0x81fc99d` at 0x81fc73e is taken on roll < chance, and 0x81fc99d is where the damage step continues. Breakpointing the comparison and the jump target together gives 11 of 11 rolls below chance reaching 0x81fc99d and 7 of 7 at or above it not reaching it, with chance = 0.424837 throughout = 19.5/(19.5+26.4) to six places. So roll < chance HITS and the comparison is strict; a miss leaves through a fall-through that builds a std::string. A trap worth recording: between that fall-through and 0x81fc99d sits a block at 0x81fc945-0x81fc99d that scales all four damages by (x + 10*c)*0.01 for the difficulty constant c, which LOOKS like the miss path taking a damage bonus and is not -- it ran zero times in the session, so it has another predecessor. WHAT CHANGED IN THE PORT: world/combat.gd carried clamp(200*AT/(AT+PA) * ALVL/(ALVL+DLVL), 5, 95) from the prerelease binaries, which retail does not use -- no level term in accuracy, no 5/95 clamp. Replaced by the shared curve sub_815D44C as curve_fraction(), hit_chance() = curve_fraction(AT, PA, 1.0, 0.5), resolve() rolling rand()%1001 * 0.001 over 1001 discrete outcomes rather than 101, plus level_term(), damage_channel() and damage() for the four channels. encounter.gd's strike() now runs its blow through the real damage formula with armour and resist as zero, which is retail's own no-armour branch rather than an invented number, and is marked ponytail because nothing decodes armour onto an actor until there is an inventory; rounding rather than truncating to int hp is flagged as the neutral choice since retail keeps damage in float and its hp arithmetic is unrecovered. combat_check.gd was rewritten around LIVE FIXTURES -- the retail binary's own printed inputs and outputs (chance 0.424837; four k=1 damage pairs; two k=2 pairs at forced lvlterm 1.5) -- so it checks the implementation against the subject rather than against its own algebra, and it now asserts the ABSENCE of the clamp and the ONE-SIDEDNESS of the level term, both of which a plausible rewrite would restore. Gate state unchanged at 41/41 checks green, parity 20 files / 0 violations; the MVP fight reads 47.7% where the prerelease formula docked the level-1 hero for the Ghoul's level 2.

HIT POINTS HAVE AN ADDRESS. Found by dumping the defender's struct at the damage breakpoint across a whole fight and asking which field falls, rather than by hunting a table: creature +0x4C8 runs 119 111 101 93 80 69 62 50 40 27 17 6 over twelve blows, +0x4CC sits at 119 and never moves, and +0x4D0 tracks +0x4C8 for eleven blows and then diverges 6 against 7. So +0x4CC is MAXIMUM hit points, and there are TWO current-like values rather than one and a mirror -- the single divergence is the only reason we know that, and which of them is authoritative is unsettled (the level-up rescale reads +0x4D0). They are one array: every accessor indexes [creature + idx*4 + 0x4C8]. The shared accessor is sub_819AE44, add(this, delta, idx): it rejects idx > 2 so there are THREE pools, floors at 0, and ceilings at +0x4CC UNINDEXED so all three clamp to the same maximum. Its three callers are potion and regeneration sites and it fired ZERO times across a fight, so DAMAGE DOES NOT REACH HIT POINTS THROUGH IT and the instruction that does is still unlocated. MAX HP IS LOADED, NOT DERIVED: CalcResults never writes it; the bulk copy at 0x80EF361-0x80EF3B5 moves +0x4B0..+0x4CC field by field out of a stack buffer into the creature, so the standing claim that HP is in no table read so far is better stated as HP is a stored record field whose table we have not identified. THE FRACTION EXISTS at 0x8188FB3 and is a level-up routine rather than a gauge: it takes current/max, calls CalcResults(creature+0x3A8), then multiplies the NEW max by the OLD fraction and truncates -- a stat change preserves your percentage of health -- and it independently re-confirms a1 = &creature[0x3A8] from an unrelated call site. ProzHP IS DEAD: it parses into the float array at 0x8B89B48 exactly as ProzAW does, and that address occurs once in the whole binary, the write; nothing reads it, so it is one of the 28 parsed-and-unused keys and no HP difficulty scaler should be modelled on it. SEPARATELY THE PORTRAIT BAR IS NOW MEASURED rather than eyeballed: its art is GUI_MAIN_02 rect (76,125,72,7), the FRAMED GREEN beaded bar, drawn at (942,124), ten beads five pixels wide on a seven pixel pitch, pixel-matched at mean per-channel error 0.44 where the threshold for this IS the art is about 1.0; the runners-up corroborate rather than compete, being the same y offset by exactly 7, 14 and 21 pixels, which is the bead pitch. The sheet carries six bar variants, not three -- yellow, green and red in unframed and framed forms -- plus gold and blue omega-segment bars. The portrait ring is CONFIRMED rather than contradicted: retail draws a RED ring and the 95x107 block at the sheet's own origin, the one the port already draws, is that red ring, with the grey one beside it at (95,0); matching the ring rect directly returns error 64 and must be ignored because that rect contains the live portrait render, exactly the case sheet_match's own header warns is answered confidently and wrongly. STILL OPEN: which quantity the bar reads. Three colours for one slot is the shape of a bar that recolours as it empties, which would make it health, but that is a reading and not a measurement; the settling experiment is one session.sh capture run over the staged combat save counting beads across a fight, and one attempt timed out before the retail side captured.

THE GREEN BEADED BAR UNDER THE PORTRAIT IS NOT HEALTH, AND THE GAUGE WAS NEVER A BAR. Captured by running retail from the staged combat save under gdb with SACRED_SHOT set, so the breakpoint trace and the frames come from ONE process and cannot disagree about which run they describe -- autopilot's glReadPixels hook writes /tmp/sacred-<ms>.ppm regardless of the debugger, which is what made the earlier session.sh timeout unnecessary (the port half runs first and ate the budget; look.sh drives retail alone). Identification is retail's own: the creature record's type id at *(a1+4)+0x10 reads 1 for the defender, a playable class, and 313 for the attacker, and the AT/PA getters already gate hero-ness on that field being <= 0x10. So the creature beaten from 119/119 down to 5/119 across twelve blows IS THE HERO and the monster at 42/42 never loses a point. Across the same run's frames the bar reads 72 of 72 beads lit in EVERY ONE. A gauge does not stay full while its owner is nearly killed, so the bar is excluded; what it does read is unknown. THE HEALTH GAUGE IS THE PORTRAIT RING: measured inside the ring annulus over the same run the red falls 454, 311, 168, 0 while grey rises to replace it, against 839 red in a healthy frame, and the red is an ARC ANCHORED AT ABOUT +32 DEGREES FROM BOTTOM-CENTRE whose far end sweeps away as health falls -- only the far end moves. Visual proof at analysis/evidence/hp-gauge-2026-08-20/ring-full-vs-empty.png: a full red annulus at high health against bare grey at 5 hp. THIS EXPLAINS THE STANDING PUZZLE. cUI_Taskbar2 was correctly enumerated as referencing no orb art and computing no fraction, because the gauge is not in the taskbar at all; it belongs to the portrait window, and its art is the pair row 1015 already identified -- GUI_MAIN_02 (0,0,95,107) is the FULL state and (95,0,95,107) the EMPTY one. The port already draws the red block at (932,15); what it lacks is the grey composited over it by fraction, not a new asset. A NEGATIVE RESULT WORTH KEEPING: pinning +0x4C8 to 60 at every blow and watching the ring keep draining LOOKS like proof the gauge reads +0x4D0 and is not -- printing the slot before overwriting shows the pin is gone by the next blow (set 60, reads back 109, 79, 78, 76), so the write is undone and the ring's behaviour says nothing about which slot it reads. The two slots do transiently differ with +0x4C8 the lower before they re-converge, which reads like +0x4C8 authoritative and +0x4D0 a display value easing toward it, but that is a reading and not a measurement. Mana remains entirely unlocated.

THE GREEN BEADED BAR UNDER THE PORTRAIT IS THE EXPERIENCE GAUGE, AND ROW 1039 READ IT UPSIDE DOWN. Correction first: row 1039 reported the bar as 72 of 72 beads lit in every frame. It never was. Those beads are the EMPTY TRACK, a muted green about (136,170,136) that a naive g>r+12 mask counts as lit, and the bar was reading ZERO in every frame of every run recorded so far. Row 1039's conclusion that the bar is not health is untouched and in fact strengthened -- a gauge pinned at zero obviously is not tracking a health value that fell 119 to 5 -- but its evidence was described backwards and the phrasing is withdrawn. WHAT IT READS, established causally rather than by elimination alone. Four quantities were varied under gdb with SACRED_SHOT frames from the same process and moved the bar not at all: the hero's own health driven 119 to 5; walking, with an inter-frame RMSE of 13530 proving the hero really moved; eight right-click combat-art uses, issued through autopilot's wheel verb which calls emit_button_n with an arbitrary button number so wheel 3 1 is a right click; and the target monster's health forced down to 8 of 42, which excludes the obvious reading that the bar is the selected target's health. Then the hero was made to KILL: clicks driven onto the hostile at its measured screen position with any struck monster forced to 1 hp at the damage breakpoint so the next blow finishes it. The first bead turned from the track's (119,153,119) to a vivid (85,255,0), and further kills lit further beads, 0 then 1 then 3. Proof image analysis/evidence/hp-gauge-2026-08-20/xp-bar-0-vs-3-beads.png. A ten-segment gauge under the portrait that starts empty and advances on a kill is the experience bar toward the next level; strictly what is measured is advances when the hero kills, and three beads from two forced kills means the increment is not one-per-kill, which is what an experience value does and a kill counter does not. THE GAUGE IS TWO ELEMENTS, NOT ONE, which is exactly why it looked static and why sheet_match returned the track as the art: empty track is element 67 at GUI_MAIN_02 (74,123)-(146,132), mean colour (104,117,85), and the fill is element 68 at (0,119)-(73,125), vivid (51,170,0), drawn at (942,124) as ten beads five pixels wide on a seven pixel pitch filling left to right. The siblings pair the same way -- 65 and 69 are the yellow and red tracks, 66 and 70 their fills -- so the sheet holds THREE COMPLETE GAUGES rather than six loose bars, which supersedes row 1038's reading of six variants. NOT LOCATED: the experience value itself. Dumping the hero creature's +0x420 through +0x620 across a kill shows only two noise fields moving, so the quantity lives off the creature struct and the port can draw the track but cannot fill it yet. Also recorded as a dead end: the gfx element table at 0x880DC68 has only five xrefs, all in the loader sub_8501A40 and the reloader sub_84FDDF4, so the draw path never touches it directly and who draws element 67 is not reachable by xref; and the promising-looking cluster writing 0x2a and 0x5f into an id array at 0x851599b is a PASSWORD MASK building asterisks and an underscore cursor, not element ids.

THE LIFE GAUGE'S FILL IS SYMMETRIC AND HORIZONTAL, AND ROW 1039 DESCRIBED IT AS AN OFF-CENTRE ARC. Correction first: row 1039 called the red 'an arc anchored at about +32 degrees from bottom-centre whose far end sweeps away, only the far end moves'. Both halves are wrong. Classifying every band pixel of retail's own frame as nearer the red art (GUI_MAIN_02 0,0,95,107) or the grey one (95,0,95,107) puts the boundary at row 54 on the LEFT and row 54 on the RIGHT -- horizontal, mirrored about bottom-centre, both ends moving together. The +32 degrees came from eyeballing an annulus and an annulus read by eye always looks like it starts somewhere. The band itself is now measured rather than assumed: diffing the two blocks gives 3814 differing pixels against 236 identical, so they are one frame painted twice and the differing set IS the gauge, and its vertical extent is rows 1..106 rather than the block's 0..107 -- a waterline run over the block is one pixel wrong at each end. WHICH FILL LAW IT IS CANNOT BE SETTLED BY THIS DATA AND IS RECORDED AS UNDETERMINED. Red area is very nearly linear in the hit-point fraction and both candidates reproduce the measured series 0.541 0.371 0.200 0.000 (against hp 0.529 0.345 0.210 0.042) to within 0.033: arc-proportional gives 0.525 0.339 0.190 0.033, height-proportional gives 0.520 0.366 0.237 0.009. They are inseparable because the band is near-uniform per angle -- 526 719 649 642 725 553 pixels over six 30-degree bins -- which makes arc length and height nearly the same function, and because a SYMMETRIC sweep puts both endpoints at equal height so the two laws draw the same boundary shape and differ only in where it sits. THE PORT TAKES THE HEIGHT SLICE because a slice is two rects and a sweep is a shader, marked ponytail with that ceiling named. Verified against retail's frame rather than against itself: at the best-fitting fraction (0.50, boundary row 53) the port agrees with retail on 99.3 percent of band pixels below the waterline (1069/1077), 81.4 percent above it and 81.0 percent in the leafwork column x>=72, where the art is semi-transparent over the live portrait bust. The residual is scattered single pixels with no shape, which is what noise looks like and not what a wrong model looks like. At full health the port draws NO grey at all -- not an optimisation but a parity requirement, since a zero-height grey rect under the red would blend the red ring's soft edge against grey instead of against the world and move pixels in a frame the capture runbooks md5. view/hud.gd gains set_health(frac) defaulting to full, hud_check gains a gate asserting the two slices tile the band exactly once at 1.0 0.75 0.50 0.25 and 0.0 with no overlap and no gap, and the stale header claiming the two 95x107 blocks belong to the mercenary window is retracted in the file that carried it. STILL MISSING IS THE NUMBER, NOT THE GAUGE: world/encounter.gd tracks only the hostile's hit points, and inventing a hero maximum would be inventing balance data while the table that loads creature +0x4CC is unidentified. MANA remains entirely unlocated -- no art, no field, no window.

SACRED HAS NO MANA, AND EVERY INTERFACE ELEMENT HAS RETAIL'S OWN NAME IN THE BINARY. The second half is the bigger result and it makes the first half cheap. A packed NUL-separated blob of 1452 strings at file offset 0x6CF9FD names the gfx element table, with gfx id = blob index - 5. NOTHING POINTS INTO IT -- no pointer to any of its strings exists anywhere in the image and no instruction takes one as an immediate -- so it is walked, not indexed, which is exactly why every xref search for it came back empty. The anchor is self-identifying: blob index 6 is UI_INVALID and gfx id 1 is the one entry whose sheet-name field literally reads INVALID; three shape checks agree independently (UI_HORSE_VHP_FULL is the only tall-thin rect at 15x71, UI_HORSE_HHP_FULL/_EMPTY are the two 71x14 ones, UI_CHR_HEALTH_01/_02 are the 95x107 pair), and all 1446 entries in the named range carry their own id field equal to the derived id. Coverage is ids 1..1444 against a table of 1886, so GUI_HERO_* is unnamed and that is not an error. Tool: tools/formats/uinames.py with a self-check. WHAT IT SETTLES AT ONCE: ids 42/43 are UI_CHR_HEALTH_01/_02, so the portrait ring is named HEALTH by retail and row 1039's identification stops being a pixel argument; 65-70 are UI_BAR_YELLOW/GREEN/RED_EMPTY and _FULL, carrying no semantics, so the green bar's experience role stays an empirical result; 76-81 are the HORSE's vertical and horizontal health and its horseshoe; 103/104/175 are UI_ACTION, UI_ACTION_BRIGHT and UI_ACTION_GRAYED; and 176-181 are UI_POTION_EMPTY/RED/BLUE/GREEN/PURPLE/YELLOW, so ui-taskbar.md's own table calling 177-181 the combat-art slots was WRONG. AND IT CORRECTS ROW 1041 BY ONE PIXEL: UI_CHR_HEALTH_02 is at x 96, not 95. Aligning the two blocks at 95 shifts them against each other and invents a differing pixel at every edge, which inflated the measured band from 2580 to 3814 px, dragged the leafwork into it, and dropped agreement with retail's frame from 97.3 to 87.5 percent. Corrected, the band spans rows 10..102 and columns 0..84 only -- the finial and leafwork are identical in both blocks, so they are frame and not gauge -- and the arc-versus-height fit tightens to a mean error of 0.026 for BOTH laws, which leaves them still inseparable. engine/view/hud.gd and its gate are fixed. THERE IS NO MANA GAUGE BECAUSE THERE IS NO MANA. Searching all 1446 names for MANA, _MP_, ENERG, STAMIN or AUSDAUER returns only UI_PORTRAIT_MP/_MP_H/_MP_E, and MP there is MULTIPLAYER -- a 127x189 frame sitting between UI_NET_* and UI_HORSEMERC. Four independent lines agree: retail's own attribute list (global.res 1401-1406) is Strength, Endurance, Dexterity, PHYSICAL REGENERATION, MENTAL REGENERATION, Charisma, and the whole 23123-entry text tree has no Mana stat label; slots 1459/1460 are Regeneration Spells and Regeneration Special Move and 6970 reads 'Accelerates the regeneration of spells'; TYPE_OBJECT_POTION_MANA_MINOR/MAJOR/FULL (5060-5062) are DEAD types whose description function sub_815DDA2 returns 0 for every one while the live coloured potions 5137-5172 all get text, the live blue one being a Potion of Concentration; and the creature+0x4C8 triple is entirely hit points, since sub_819AE44 ceilings all three indices against the FIXED +0x4CC and the healer sub_85667FC writes get(1) into BOTH index 0 and index 2 on a full heal. The resource is PER-ART REGENERATION and it shows exactly where a mana bar would have been, on the combat-art slots: UI_ACTION_GRAYED while an art regenerates against UI_ACTION/UI_ACTION_BRIGHT when ready, and a full UI_SPELL_nn_EMPTY/_LOAD/_FULL set for 105 arts -- a _LOAD state per art, a timer per art, not a pool shared between them. STILL OPEN: what fraction drives _LOAD and where the per-art timer lives in the creature. The mechanic is settled, its field is not.

THE COMBAT-ART SLOT IS THE SAME WATERLINE AS THE HEALTH RING, AND _LOAD MEANS LOADED. sub_85E676A is the slot renderer. Per slot it takes three element indices and one fraction f, then splits the control at split = (h-1)*(1-f): element[0] on TOP over rows 0..split, element[1] on the BOTTOM over split..h, and if f >= 1.0 AND the slot is the selected one it draws element[2] whole instead. The UV is stepped by split/256 + 1/512 -- texel-to-UV with the usual half-texel -- applied to the source rect's v0, which makes it a SLICE of the art rather than a scale of it. So _LOAD is not 'loading': it is LOADED, and it fills the slot from the bottom as the art recharges, while _EMPTY is the drained remainder above the line and _FULL is a separate brighter art shown only when the slot is both ready and selected. THIS ALSO ANSWERS THE OLD 'a filled art slot is a composite, not a blit' QUESTION: it is not a composite of icon plus backing plus frame at all, but one of three whole arts named per combat art in the element table, chosen and sliced -- the greyscale GUI_MOVE_ATTACKE that looked like an un-tinted icon is the EMPTY state. THE FRACTION IS PER-ART REGENERATION, IN A PER-CREATURE LIST. Two lists hang off creature+936 and the slot's kind (sub_833EBBE returns 2, 3 or 4) picks one: kind 2/3 reads the list at +250, stride 22 bytes, f = 1 - remaining/total from the record's +0x12 and +0x0A floats, with the art id at +0x04 which is how sub_8219C44 finds the entry; kind 4 (spells, ids >= 512) reads the list at +262, stride 38 bytes, f = min(elapsed/total, 1) from +0x22 and +0x1A. So the timer is per art, not a pool and not one clock shared between arts -- which is the field row 1042 recorded as still missing. Two overrides sit on top: an art that is unusable with the weapon in hand (checked via sub_819BA46) has all three elements forced to element[0], so the slot shows EMPTY at every fraction, which is the greyed-out slot; and if the hero has a linked creature (sub_81A3AD0: flag 0x2 at +20 and a cCreature at +0x1EC, the mount) the triple is replaced wholesale and f comes from creature+0x4E0 over creature+0x4E4 instead -- a second timer at creature scope rather than art scope. AND ROW 1042'S NAME OFFSET IS WRONG ABOVE ID 351. It gave gfx id = blob index - 5 flat; that holds to id 351 and fails above, because two elements somewhere in 352..442 carry no name, so from id 443 on the offset is -3. Retail's own data caught it: the combat-art table at 0x8793D00 stride 120 carries at +48/+52/+56 the three element indices each art draws with, and those must be an EMPTY/LOAD/FULL triple -- at -5 they straddle triple boundaries, at -3 all 52 that resolve land clean. The low end is pinned the other way, since id 351 is UI_PORTRAIT_MP at 127x189 and the -3 reading puts a 60x25 arrow there. uinames.py now returns None for 352..442 rather than guessing and its self-check asserts both the refusal and the 52 clean triples. NOTHING ROW 1042 CONCLUDED DEPENDS ON THIS: every element it identified (42/43, 65-70, 76-81, 103/104/175, 176-181, 351) is at or below the drift, and the mana result is a search over the NAME LIST, which is complete whatever the offsets are. STILL OPEN: which art populates each of the two lists, and what +0x4E0/+0x4E4 count while mounted.

THE 22-BYTE PER-ART RECORD IS MAPPED AND THE RECOVERY TIMER'S FORMULA IS RECOVERED. Record layout, from the accessors around it: +0x04 u16 art id (how sub_8219C44 finds an entry), +0x06 u8 permanent level from runes, +0x07 u8 temporary level from items, +0x08 u16 flags with bit 0 = known and the HIGH BYTE holding the bound taskbar slot stored as slot-270 (sub_821865A writes it, sub_82185BE reads it back adding 270), +0x0A f32 total regeneration time, +0x12 f32 remaining. sub_8218774 is retail's own is-this-art-ready test and it reads remaining <= 0.01, NOT == 0 -- worth transcribing exactly, since a float countdown decremented by a frame delta will not land on zero. WHERE THE TOTAL IS WRITTEN: gaining or levelling an art runs sub_8219FCE, which bumps the level byte and calls sub_820E04C for a full creature recompute. What it does around that call is the interesting part: it saves the old total, recomputes, and if the total GREW it adds the difference to remaining -- so levelling an art lengthens its regeneration and pushes the countdown out by exactly that difference rather than rescaling it, and a partly-recharged art keeps the seconds it had already served instead of jumping back to the same fraction. NOT READ: the formula inside sub_820E04C. It is 22 KB and recomputes the whole creature, so how the regeneration total depends on Mental and Physical Regeneration is still unrecovered, and that is now the remaining gap in this area. +0x4E0 / +0x4E4 IS THE ATTACK RECOVERY TIMER, not a mount clock. Row 1043 left the pair unknown. They are written in exactly one place, sub_816C244 at 0x817205f, together and from one value: t = sub_81A8636(item, creature) goes into creature+0x4E4 (total) and creature+0x4E0 (countdown, started full) and into the combat block at creature+0x3A8 +0x138/+0x13C -- and that block is the one row 1036 identified as the damage pipeline's a1, which is what identifies the pair as Recovery Rate / Combat Recovery (global.res 1413/1414). sub_81A8636 transcribes whole: regen = 20.0 when there is no item, otherwise base / (1 + 0.015 * modifier(22)), where base is +40 of the record reached through the item's property 13 and modifier(22) is sub_821A71C(creature+936, 22), which scans EIGHT modifier slots -- a kind byte at +36+i with the value fetched by sub_821A6CC -- and returns the one whose kind is 22. Kind 21 is what the healer's price uses, so those eight slots are a general per-creature modifier table rather than a regeneration-specific one. 0.015 per point, hyperbolic rather than linear, the same shape as every other Sacred curve: the modifier divides rather than subtracts, so it can never take the time below zero. The mounted branch of the slot renderer reuses this pair because a mounted hero's slots show the mount's attack rather than her own combat arts.

THE COMBAT-ART REGENERATION TOTAL IS A STRAIGHT LINE IN THE ART'S LEVEL, AND NO CREATURE ATTRIBUTE IS IN IT. Correction first: row 1044 named sub_820E04C as the writer of the per-art total. That was an over-read and the function says so -- all 354 of its float stores land in a derived-stat block at offsets 0x5A..0xF2 on the combat block, and not one touches the art record's +0x0A. It recomputes the creature; a callee does the arts. THE WRITER IS sub_82047D4 and it transcribes whole. For every entry in the art list it sets record+0x0E to 1.0f, reads perm = +0x06 (permanent level from runes) and tmp = +0x07 (temporary level from items), computes total = curve(def, perm) and both = curve(def, perm+tmp), and if both > total adds (both-total)*0.5 -- so TEMPORARY LEVELS COUNT HALF -- then stores the result to +0x0A. THE CURVE IS LINEAR with the two coefficients stored per art: a combat art (sub_8306C6A, table 0x8793D00 stride 120) uses base at +64 f32 and per-level at +68 f32, giving level*step + base; a spell (sub_830740E) uses base at +62 u16 and per-level at +64 u16, same shape. So regeneration RISES linearly as an art is levelled -- the cost of a stronger art is that it comes back more slowly -- and a temporary level buys only half the increase a permanent one does. NO ATTRIBUTE ENTERS, AND THAT RELOCATES THE QUESTION. sub_8306D8A and sub_83077BE take (definition, level) and nothing else; the creature is not a parameter, so Mental and Physical Regeneration CANNOT shorten the total. What they must scale is the COUNTDOWN. sub_81F0DA6 is the tick: for every art whose kind matches it does remaining += delta and clamps to [0, total], with delta supplied by the CALLER. One caller is already legible -- an item effect of kind 10 grants instant progress of -(magnitude * 4000 * k), negative because it reduces the remaining -- and a flag at +320 bit 3 / bit 2 multiplies the delta by 0.8 for one art kind, i.e. a buff that regenerates one school 20 percent faster. STILL UNREAD: the per-frame delta itself, which is where the two Regeneration attributes have to enter. That is now the whole remaining question in this area. AND A UNIFICATION WORTH RECORDING: the object holding these lists is creature+0x3A8, the SAME block row 1036 identified as sub_81FAC30's a1 -- creature+936 and creature+0x3A8 are one address written two ways, once as a float index and once as a byte offset. So a single structure carries the damage pipeline's inputs, the art list at +250 stride 22, the spell list at +262 stride 38, the eight modifier slots at +36, and the recovery pair at +0x138/+0x13C.

THE PER-FRAME REGENERATION DELTA IS FOUND, AND IT IS WHERE MENTAL AND PHYSICAL REGENERATION ENTER. The countdown is ticked in sub_81F118A and is two instructions: if the art's kind (+0x00) is 1, or its id (+0x04) is 1019, then remaining -= dt * art[+0x0E] * block[+0xEE], otherwise remaining -= dt * art[+0x0E] * block[+0xF2]. TWO CREATURE-LEVEL RATES PICKED BY THE ART'S KIND -- the shape a mana pool never had and Sacred never needed. art[+0x0E] is the per-art multiplier that sub_82047D4 resets to 1.0f on every recompute, i.e. the hook an effect can bend without touching the total. AND sub_820E04C BUILDS THOSE TWO RATES, which is what it was doing all along. Three stages: it accumulates bonuses into them (a switch over modifier kinds adds to both under case 11, 'to all regeneration', or to one; item property cases 813 and 814 add value*0.01 to +0xEE and +0xF2 respectively); it calls sub_82047D4 at 0x821248c to recompute the art totals; and then immediately scales each rate by its attribute -- block[+0xEE] *= 1 + block[+0x18]*0.01 and block[+0xF2] *= 1 + block[+0x16]*0.01, with 0.01 read from the image as flt_86E7454. So an attribute point is ONE PERCENT faster regeneration, multiplicative on the accumulated rate, which can never reach zero or flip sign -- the same divide-don't-subtract discipline as every other Sacred curve. WHICH ATTRIBUTE IS WHICH, BY TWO INDEPENDENT CHECKS THAT AGREE. +0x16 and +0x18 are adjacent u16s, and retail's own attribute order (global.res 1401-1406: Strength, Endurance, Dexterity, PHYSICAL REGENERATION, MENTAL REGENERATION, Charisma) puts Physical at +0x16 and Mental at +0x18 for a contiguous block of six starting at +0x10. The tick says the same from the other side: kind 1 is SPELLS (sub_81ADA76 adds an art with kind 1 when it resolves through the spell table and kind 2 through the combat-art table), and kind 1 reads +0xEE, the rate scaled by +0x18. So +0xEE / +0x18 / Mental drives spells and matches label 1459 'Regeneration Spells', while +0xF2 / +0x16 / Physical drives combat arts and matches 1460 'Regeneration Special Move'. THE WHOLE CHAIN END TO END: total = base + level*step per art, linear and attribute-free, plus half the temporary level's extra; rate = accumulated bonuses * (1 + attribute*0.01) per creature and per kind; remaining = clamp(remaining - dt*art_mult*rate, 0, total); fraction = 1 - remaining/total, which is what the slot draws as its waterline. A buff at block+320 multiplies the delta by 0.8 for one kind before it lands, i.e. 20 percent faster for one school. This closes the regeneration model that row 1042 opened when it established there is no mana.

COMBAT-ART REGENERATION IS NOW IN THE PORT, AND creature.pak CONFIRMED WHICH ATTRIBUTE DRIVES WHICH KIND. world/regen.gd transcribes the whole chain from rows 1043-1046: total = base + level*step per art (linear, attribute-free, plus HALF the temporary level's extra), rate = bonus * (1 + attribute/100) per creature and per kind, remaining = clamp(remaining - dt*mult*rate, 0, total), fraction = 1 - remaining/total. INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION OF ROW 1046's ATTRIBUTE IDENTIFICATION, from the port's own data rather than from the disassembly: formats/hero.gd already names creature.pak's six attribute columns STK, RES, GES, REPHY, REMAG, CHARISMA -- REPHY and REMAG are indices 3 and 4, adjacent and physical-first, exactly matching the +0x16 / +0x18 pair the tick reads. Row 1046 argued that from the global.res label order and from the kind routing; creature.pak's own column names now say it a third way. encounter.gd computes the hero's two rates from the template it already reads: Regen.rates(1.0, REPHY, REMAG), reported in status_line as regen_art and regen_spell. The accumulated bonus is left at the literal 1.0 and marked ponytail -- that aggregate is what sub_820E04C builds out of equipment, and the port equips nothing yet, so when it does the literal is the only thing that changes. TWO DETAILS TRANSCRIBED RATHER THAN CHOSEN, both of which a reimplementation gets wrong by default: the ready test is remaining <= 0.01 and NOT == 0.0, because a float clock decremented by a frame delta never lands on zero and an equality would leave every art permanently one tick short of usable; and the attribute is MULTIPLICATIVE at one percent a point, so no attribute value can drive the rate to zero or run the clock backwards. checks/regen_check.gd gates RELATIONS rather than literals, on the argument hud_check already makes -- a transcribed constant only proves someone typed it twice. It asserts that levelling LENGTHENS regeneration rather than shortening it, that four temporary levels are worth exactly two permanent ones, that a falling curve ignores the temporary branch (retail guards it with if(both > total)), that the two kinds do not cross their attributes, that the tick clamps at BOTH ends so a long frame cannot overshoot into a negative clock, that a full 10-second recharge at rate 1 lands exactly ready, and that the encounter status line formats for an empty dictionary as well as a populated one. It runs the rates over all eight shipped templates and requires both attributes to read back non-zero. All gates pass: regen_check OK, combat_check OK, hud_check OK, parity/verify layer 21 files 0 violations. NOT WIRED: no art is attached to a clock yet, because the per-art base and step coefficients live in the retail ELF's combat-art table at 0x8793D00 (stride 120, +64/+68) and the port reads no table from the executable. The math is transcribed and gated; the coefficients are the next step.

THE COMBAT-ART REGENERATION COEFFICIENTS ARE IN THE EXECUTABLE, AND THE PORT NOW READS THEM. An art's clock is total = base + level*step (row 1045) and those two authored numbers are in NO PAK -- not creature.pak, not balance.bin, not global.res. They are a static array compiled into the binary at 0x8793D00, stride 120, records 1..0x5E, which is exactly the range sub_8306C6A scans. Fields: +0x00 i16 art id, +0x30 i32[3] the EMPTY/LOAD/FULL element ids, +0x40 f32 base, +0x44 f32 step. MEASURED OVER ALL 94 RECORDS: base spans 3.0..40.0, step spans 0.0..45.0, every element triple is three consecutive ids, and NO art regenerates faster as it levels -- which matches sub_82047D4's if(both > total) guard expecting the curve to rise. Record 0 is a zero slot and retail skips it, record 95 is zeroed and 96 is garbage, so the bounds are retail's and not a guess. A CONVINCING WRONG ANSWER, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT REPEATED: an art id is NOT a global.res text id. Resolving art 1000 through the resource tree returns 'Buy item?', 1001 returns 'Sell item?' and 1060 returns the Gladiator class blurb -- the name hash of the decimal string collides with a UI string. Those are collisions, not names, and they read as a perfectly plausible naming until you notice the arts are all shop text. THE PORT READS IT AT RUN TIME AND COPIES NOTHING. engine/formats/combat_arts.gd is the first thing the port reads out of the EXECUTABLE rather than a data file; it follows balance.gd's precedent of carrying the OFFSETS while retail keeps the values, so no retail balance data enters the repository. It translates the virtual address through the ELF program headers rather than seeking, since the file is not mapped. IT VALIDATES A SIGNATURE RATHER THAN TRUSTING THE ADDRESS, because the failure mode here is not a crash: a wrong offset returns floats that look exactly like balance data. The signature is art 1000 at base 5 / step 3, the first four ids 1000/1001/1002/1009, every element triple consecutive, and no negative step; a different build fails `found` with a reason instead. GATED END TO END in checks/regen_check.gd: 94 arts read, every one with a positive finite non-decreasing clock and a three-element triple; CombatArts.total asserted to AGREE with Regen.total rather than merely coexist with it; art 1000 landing on retail's own 5.0 s at level 0 and 32.0 s at level 9 (5 + 3*9); and a full recharge driven through the port's own tick at a hero-derived rate until Regen.ready holds, which takes 3.84 s of simulated time. All gates pass and parity/verify reports 21 files, 0 violations. This closes the last gap in the regeneration model: the math was transcribed in row 1047, the coefficients are now read from retail rather than invented, and an art in the port has a real clock.

THE HERO TEMPLATES CARRY THEIR COMBAT ARTS AS THE LIVE IN-MEMORY STRUCT, AND THE PORT NOW GRANTS THEM. The CA count at +0x4CB was known; the LIST was not. It follows immediately at +0x4CD as `count` records of 22 bytes -- the SAME struct retail keeps at the combat block's +250 (row 1044), written out field for field. So a template is not a compact description of a starting art, it is a snapshot of the art already installed. Layout confirmed against the in-memory one: +0x00 u32 kind (1 spell, 2 combat art), +0x04 u16 art id, +0x06 u8 permanent level, +0x07 u8 temporary level, +0x08 u16 flags with bit 0 = known, +0x0A f32 total regeneration in seconds, +0x0E f32 the per-art multiplier, +0x12 f32 remaining. IN ALL NINETEEN RECORDS the multiplier is exactly 1.0 and the remaining is exactly 0.0 -- a new hero's arts are ready, which is what row 1045 predicted the multiplier would be since sub_82047D4 resets it to 1.0f on every recompute. The eight templates carry 19 arts between them: two each, except two classes with three and four. THIRTEEN OF THE NINETEEN AGREE WITH THE COEFFICIENT TABLE TO THE LAST BIT (base + level*step, row 1048). Of the remainder, six are SPELLS whose curve lives in a different record the table does not cover, and five read as the table's value divided by EXACTLY 1.12. THE 1.12 IS PER ART, NOT PER HERO, AND IS UNEXPLAINED. hero07 carries two arts that match the table and two that are off by it; hero00's two are both off; hero06 has one of each. So it is not an attribute, a class or a difficulty -- any of those would move every art on a character together. It is recorded rather than smoothed over: the port uses the SAVED number, and the gate asserts the ratio is exactly 1.12 wherever table and save disagree, so a misread record fails instead of passing as another instance of this. WIRED: formats/hero.gd gains combat_arts_list(); world/encounter.gd reads it into hero_arts and gains regenerate(dt), art_ready(id), use_art(id) and art_fractions(), with the CALLER owning the frame (R10.1) so a replay handing back the same deltas reproduces the same clocks. status_line reports the art count and the live fractions. GATED: checks/regen_check.gd asserts every class starts with at least one art, that the count matches the list length, that kind is 1 or 2, that every art has a positive clock, ships mult 1.0, starts READY and sits at level >= 1; that the table-vs-saved split is the shipped mix; and it runs the full use -> tick -> ready cycle on hero01's real arts at the rates her own attributes produce, requiring the recharge to take more than one frame -- a clock that finishes instantly is a clock that is not being applied. All gates pass, parity/verify 21 files 0 violations.

THE COMBAT-ART RECORD NAMES ITS OWN ICON, WHICH CLOSES AN OLDER SEARCH, AND CARRIES A SECOND COEFFICIENT PAIR THAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT APPLIED. The 120-byte record at 0x8793D00 gave up regeneration in row 1048; reading the rest: +0x00 i16 art id, +0x04 and +0x08 two per-art id series (text resources, not read), +0x0C char[24] THE ART'S OWN ICON TEXTURE NAME, +0x30 i32[3] the EMPTY/LOAD/FULL element triple, +0x3C i32 school, +0x40/+0x44 f32 regeneration base and per level, +0x50/+0x54 f32 a SECOND base/step pair. +0x0C CLOSES THE 'a filled art slot is a composite, not a blit' QUESTION in ui-taskbar.md. That section hunted texture.pak by shape correlation across 440 candidates, topped out at 0.40 with implausible winners, and concluded identification by search was exhausted. It was never a search problem: the table names the texture for each art directly -- GUI_MOVE_ATTACKE.TGA, GUI_MOVE_HARDHIT.TGA, GUI_MOVE_RUNDUM.TGA, gui_moves_attacke_demon. THE SECOND PAIR READS LIKE A DAMAGE MULTIPLIER AND IS NOT APPLIED. For the attack moves the shape and the ordering are exactly right: GUI_MOVE_HARDHIT is 1.80 + 0.20 a level against GUI_MOVE_ATTACKE's 0.75 + 0.05 and GUI_MOVE_RUNDUM's 0.80 + 0.10 -- a heavy swing landing at 1.8x where a quick one lands at 0.75x. But the SAME FIELD on art 1022, GUI_MOVE_CHANGELING_DAY, reads 24.00 + 6.00, which is a duration in seconds and not a multiplier at all. So the field is POLYMORPHIC and its reading is not recovered. CombatArts.effect() exposes it because it is measured; NOTHING multiplies damage by it, because deciding which arts multiply would be inventing balance and the wrong guess would be invisible -- every number involved is plausible. THE USE IS WIRED: encounter.strike(rng, art_id) spends an art, refuses one that is not ready (retail gates the same way at sub_8218774) and returns art and refused alongside the roll; main.gd's headless fight picks the first ready art each swing and advances the clocks between swings. A MEASURED CONSEQUENCE RECORDED RATHER THAN TUNED AWAY: the loop's per-swing time is retail's own no-weapon recovery default of 20.0 (sub_81A8636), and at the Seraphim's own rate that serves about 24 s of clock against her 15 s art -- so the art is ready again every single swing and the cooldown never bites in this loop. The first version of the log printed only the post-recovery fraction and therefore showed ready=[1.0,1.0] on every line, hiding the mechanic completely; it now prints the fraction BEFORE any time passes as well, which reads spent=[0.0,1.0] then after=[1.0,1.0]. The gate, not the log, is what proves the refusal: checks/regen_check.gd spends an art, ticks half its clock and requires it to still be unusable. All gates pass and parity/verify reports 21 files, 0 violations. STILL OPEN: where sub_81FAC30 takes an art into the damage it computes -- row 1036 already noted that what the weapon-slot flag selects appears nowhere in it.

--fight WAS A BATCH FLAG THAT NEVER TERMINATED, AND THAT MISLED ME ABOUT ITS COST. main.gd's --fight=N resolved the encounter, printed its swing, status and questbook lines, and then carried on being the game indefinitely -- only --autoplay and the parity/compare paths called get_tree().quit(). So every headless --fight run had to be killed by an outer timeout, which reports exit 143 (SIGTERM) and tells you nothing about whether the run finished. I READ THAT WRONG TWICE AND BOTH READINGS ARE CORRECTED HERE. First I recorded that a full app run 'exceeds the budget (world streaming)' and moved verification into the gate instead; the fight in fact completes in 1.9 SECONDS. Second, one run's wrapper reported EXIT=0 which I attributed to godot -- it was the shell's status from a trailing grep in the same command, and godot had been SIGTERM'd there too. The tell that it was idling rather than stuck was in the log all along: the tail showed swap-apply visible=13,14,15,16, new work being produced right up to the kill, where a genuine hang shows a static tail. FIXED: get_tree().quit(0) after the questbook lines. It is DEFERRED to the end of the frame, so the rest of the start-up path still runs and the exit stays on the same code path as a normal launch rather than tearing down a half-built tree. --fight=0 is untouched -- the flag is off, nothing prints, the app runs as before, verified by a 12-second run that correctly times out at 124. MEASURED: --fight=5 now takes 1.9 s and exits 0, against a run that previously ended only when an outer timeout killed it. No live runbook depended on the old behaviour -- the only other references to the flag are stale main.gd backups in the throwaway workspace. All gates pass and parity/verify reports 21 files, 0 violations.

The new list is ranked by EFFORT then by UNBLOCKING and every row cites what shows the gap is real: 1 runtime clip switching (high effort, largest visible difference, entirely unblocked); 2 the hero as a creature with hit points (blocked on the max-HP derivation, likely inside CalcResults); 3 equipment actually equipped, which is ONE gap and not three -- Combat.damage's zero armour, Regen's bonus of 1.0 and sub_81A8636's 20.0 fallback are all the same missing input; 4 what an art does to damage; 5 the experience value. The largest visible difference between the port and Sacred was that the hero played one clip forever: PlayerView.animate bound a resting clip once and nothing ever changed it, so a character that walked across a meadow did it in an idle loop. PlayerView.play_action now switches a body to its clip for a named ACTION and main.gd drives it once per frame from the only movement signal the sim actually has -- whether the cell moved -- because world/actor_state.gd's own header says click-to-move never writes `heading` and `facing` is HELD and therefore says which way she is turned rather than whether she is going. It drives WALK and IDLE only: both WALK and RUN clips exist on every class body, but the port has a single measured walk speed (row 1013), so there is no threshold to switch RUN on and inventing one would be tuning dressed as a port. Two bugs were caught by the gate rather than by reading, and the first is the instructive one: play_action originally routed every member of Rigs.REST_ACTIONS through rest_clip(), which reads like a harmless shortcut and is not, because WALK is in that list only as rest_clip's own FALLBACK for a body with no idle -- so play_action("WALK") returned the IDLE clip and answered true, and a hero who cannot walk reported herself as walking. Only "IDLE" ladders now. The second is the finding: SERAPHIM.GRN, the body a retail start actually spawns, resolves NO WALK clip at all, so this feature is inert for the default hero until that is fixed. probes/action_gap_probe.gd scored every action's best clip against her mesh WITHOUT the threshold, and it is not a near miss -- her scores fall in two clean groups with nothing between them, 0.891..0.915 for IDLE, FIDLE, DYING, ATTACK and SPECIAL against 0.255..0.273 for WALK, RUN, CAST, DEFEND, HIT, TALK and ACTIVATE, and the low group matches only 55 of her 72 mesh bones where the high group matches 68..71. SERA_WALK_1H.GRN is hers by name and scores 0.255, so the clips are split across two skeletons and MIN_SCORE at 0.5 sits correctly between them; by contrast GLADIATOR.GRN's own clips all land 0.78..0.82 including WALK, which is why every other class body switches. checks/hero_anim_check.gd gates the switch on the first class body that HAS a walk (DAEMONIA) and prints the ones that do not, so it fails on switching rather than on a defect in Rigs' matching, and it asserts on the clip index and anim_length rather than on play_action's return value -- returning true while playing the same clip is exactly the bug it had to be able to fail on.

Row 1053 left the default hero unable to walk and called the cause 'two skeletons' without naming them. There are two, they are both the Seraphim, and the difference is her ARMS. Measured mesh-against-mesh with no clip in the way (probes/sera_meshdiff_probe.gd), SERAPHIM.GRN and SERAWINGS02.GRN share 68 bone names and agree on only 21 of them: forearm 9.5545 against 8.4362 (-11.7%), hand 9.4793 against 8.2219 (-13.3%), Finger01 1.0991 against 1.4876 (+35%), a scatter of other bones at 2.8%, and a Root sitting at the origin in one and 58.59 units away in the other -- every one of those at an angle of exactly 0.00 degrees, so the joints point the same way and only the lengths moved. That is a re-proportioned arm, not a different creature. The clip corpus splits on the same line and the two families are exactly complementary: SERAPHIM.GRN matches IDLE, FIDLE and DYING at 0.89..0.91 and WALK, RUN, TALK, HIT, DEFEND, ACTIVATE and CAST at 0.255..0.273, while SERAWINGS02, SERAHELMET02, SERABOOTS01 and SERAHAIR01 -- her own armour -- match precisely the reverse set at 0.77..0.89. So the port draws the body from one rig revision and would hang the armour off the other. Two hypotheses were killed on the way and both are worth keeping: a uniform SCALE is refuted, because dividing out the least-squares best fit makes agreement WORSE (0.255 -> 0.036) and the per-bone length ratios spread 0.9718..1.0083 instead of clustering -- the 0.9718 median that suggested it was a percentile of that spread, not a constant; and a different BIND POSE is refuted too, because direction agreement is ~0.89 for every pair tested, matched and mismatched alike, including the Gladiator control, so direction carries none of the signal and length carries all of it. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PORT IS THAT THE MEASUREMENT DOES NOT MATTER: view/model_view.gd sets BIND_POSITION_TRACKS false and drops every translation track, so a clip contributes rotations only and the mesh keeps its own bone lengths. A clip authored against 8.4-unit forearms plays correctly on 9.5-unit ones. Sacred.Rigs is therefore gating playback on the one quantity that playback discards, and MIN_SCORE at 0.5 is correctly separating two real regimes while both of them are the same character. Lowering it is still the wrong fix -- it would admit other characters. The candidate fix, unmeasured and not implemented: geometry already proves ONE clip per mesh confidently, so take that clip's name prefix and admit the rest of the prefix, which learns the character-to-prefix map rather than assuming it and is exactly what row 963's UPI1_WALK_BH/UPIRATE_01 counterexample forbids assuming a priori.

Row 1054 proposed admitting a mesh's clips by the name prefix of the one clip geometry already proved, and left it unmeasured. Measured now over the 127 meshes Rigs has resolved (probes/prefix_probe.gd, prefix_cover_probe.gd), reading the existing user://rigmap.tsv rather than rescoring anything. THE BLAST RADIUS IS SMALL: 121 of the 127 gain nothing at all, and the six that gain are SERAPHIM +8 actions (ACTIVATE, CAST, DEFEND, HIT, RUN, STAB, TALK, WALK -- the entire missing set), THIEF2_MAL and THIEF2_FEM +3 each, GLADIATOR +1 (DEFEND), NOBLE_FEM +1 (ATTACK). THE ADMITTED CLIPS ARE USABLE, and this is the criterion that matters rather than the geometric score: view/model_view.gd sets BIND_POSITION_TRACKS false, so a clip contributes rotations only and binds by bone NAME, which makes name coverage of the deforming skeleton the question. Every single newly-admitted clip names 100% of its mesh's Bip01 chain -- 53/53 for the Seraphim, 58/58 Gladiator, 54/54 THIEF2_MAL, 58/58 THIEF2_FEM -- with NOBLE_FEM the one exception at 54/55. Whole-mesh coverage is lower (0.764..0.972) and the shortfall is entirely non-deforming: Dummy01..Dummy22 attachment points, Root, Angel_ponytail_L and weapon bones, which stay at rest and are meant to. THE SAFETY OBJECTION DIES ON ITS OWN DATA. 26 of 85 claimed prefixes are claimed by more than one mesh, and most are variants that should share (MINOTAUR/MINOTAUR_METAL, SKEL_WARRIOR/_01/_02, UPIRATE_01..04, eight FUERSTENGARDE). The three that read as genuine cross-character collisions -- BART shared by TROLL and BAUMBART, SHAR by MAGICIAN and DRYAD_SCOUT, SOLD by SOLDIER and DPIRATE_01 -- turn out to be INERT: both members of each pair gain nothing, because every action in the shared prefix is already resolved geometrically for both, so the rule would hand over no clip that is not already accepted. That is an empirical answer to a question a name-based argument about whether a Troll and a Baumbart are the same creature cannot settle. One artefact was found and fixed rather than reported: prefix_probe's first run bucketed 29 clips whose names begin with an underscore under the empty prefix, which handed CROW.GRN three actions off a pool it shares with two OGREs; excluding the empty prefix, CROW gains nothing. An earlier bug in the same probe is worth recording because it produced clean-looking findings: appending to a PackedInt32Array read back out of a Variant-typed Dictionary mutates a COPY, so every bucket stayed empty and the probe reported prefix_clips=0 for all 127 meshes and collisions=0 for all 85 prefixes -- a perfect null result caused entirely by a value-type copy. CAVEAT ON SCOPE, stated rather than left implied: 127 meshes is the population the port actually builds, not the pak's full mesh count, so the collision census is over the bodies that matter and not over everything.

Rows 1054-1055 found the cause and measured the fix; this is it wired and gated. Sacred.Rigs._admit_by_prefix takes the name prefix of the one clip geometry already proved for a mesh above MIN_SCORE and fills the actions geometry left empty. The licence for a name rule is narrow and worth restating: row 963 established that a clip's CHARACTER cannot be read from its name (UPI1_WALK_BH.GRN belongs to UPIRATE_01.GRN), which forbids ASSUMING a prefix and does not forbid LEARNING one. The justification is that Rigs was gating playback on a quantity playback discards -- view/model_view.gd sets BIND_POSITION_TRACKS false, so a clip contributes rotations only, bound by bone NAME, and the rest positions the geometric score compares are thrown away before anything plays. Four constraints are in the code rather than only in the argument: a geometric pick is never overridden and only empty actions are filled; the empty prefix is refused, because clips whose names begin with an underscore pool into it and it handed CROW.GRN three actions off two OGREs; MIN_MATCHED still applies, so a clip naming too few of this mesh's bones is refused rather than animating a fragment of it; and the rule is name-only, costing no clip decode, since candidates are found by string test on entry names and only those have their bone names read. CACHE_VERSION went 2 -> 3 because a prefix-admitted row is indistinguishable from a geometric one in the file and a v2 reader would trust it silently. BOTH GATES PASS ON A COLD RECOMPUTE. checks/hero_anim_check.gd now reports no_walk=[] where it reported [SERAPHIM.GRN], every one of the seven class bodies keeps splay 0% and a bind residual under 0.005 rad, and the Seraphim's REST pick is byte-identical at clip 3037 / IDLE / 0.915 -- the rule added her missing actions without touching the one geometry had already answered. checks/rigs_check.gd is the gate that could have caught the real risk and did not fire: 121 of 124 meshes resolved at 97.6%, scores 0.844..1.000, and its permutation control still separates cleanly at real >= 0.844 against permuted <= 0.489, under MIN_SCORE. Recorded because it cost real time twice: `pgrep -f <pattern>` matches the shell command line that is itself running pgrep, so a wait loop built on it never terminates and reports a finished process as still running -- two checks were read as hung when both had already passed, and `pgrep -x godot` is the form that answers the question. Separately, all seven probes written for rows 1053-1055 extend SceneTree and omitted the quit() the rest of probes/ ends with, so each printed its results and then ran forever; one was still competing for CPU an hour later, during the very check it made look slow.

Gap #2 (the hero as a creature) was recorded in game-wiring.md and row 1052 as 'blocked on the max-HP derivation -- likely inside CalcResults, which builds every other derived stat'. That lead is REFUTED and cost one query to kill: scanning all 5263 instructions of sub_820E04C (cCreatureHero::CalcResults, 0x820E04C..0x821369A) for any operand referencing creature+0x4C8, +0x4CC or +0x4D0 -- the hit-point triple row 1042 established is all hit points -- returns zero matches for all three offsets. That is consistent with row 1045, which found all 354 of its float stores landing in the derived-stat block at 0x5A..0xF2 and nowhere else, and it means the plausible-sounding inference 'CalcResults builds every derived stat, so it builds max HP' was never checked against that same disassembly. Max hit points are written somewhere else and the writer is still unidentified; the next instrument is a binary-wide operand scan for +0x4C8 stores rather than another read of CalcResults, and row 1048's note that the table loading +0x4CC is unidentified is still the open end. Recorded as a negative result specifically so the next session does not re-read a 22 KB function on a lead that has already been eliminated.

Gap #2's blocker was 'the max-HP derivation, location unknown'. The LOCATION is now settled and named by behaviour rather than by guess. creature+0x4C8 is a three-int array with its own accessors -- sub_819AE0E get(obj,i), sub_819AE2A set(obj,v,i), sub_819AE44 modify(obj,delta,i), each bounds-checking i <= 2 -- and sub_819AE44 is the damage/heal path: it floors at 0 (`if delta >= 0 or -delta < hp[i]` else 0) and then ceilings EVERY index against *(obj+1228), which is 0x4CC, i.e. element 1 of the same array. So element 1 IS the maximum, and elements 0 and 2 are two pools clamped to it; that also explains row 1042's observation that a full heal writes get(1) into both 0 and 2. sub_81A14DE confirms the ceiling independently on element 2 (`if get(2)+n < get(1) then set(2, get(2)+n) else set(2, get(1))` plus an event). The class is confirmed as cCreature by an explicit __dynamic_cast to `typeinfo for cCreature` in both functions, which matters because the first candidate was wrong in exactly the way an offset match invites: sub_80EF028 writes 1224 and 1228 back to back and looked like the initialiser, but it is the SECTORS.PAK loader filling a 0x5AC-byte sector object from a 512-byte record, and the two offsets are sector fields that happen to share the numbers. sub_818A60C is the resurrection path and gives the order of operations the port needs: apply the experience penalty (`-XP/20` by default, `-XP/10`, `/7`, `/5`, `/2` by difficulty in dword_8906CD0), then sub_821AE84, then CalcResults, then set(1)->element 2 and set(1)->element 0, a full heal to maximum. ROW 1057 IS CORRECTED IN ITS REASONING THOUGH NOT ITS RESULT. CalcResults is invoked as sub_820E04C(creature+936, 0, 1) -- 936 is 0x3A8, the combat block -- so everything it writes is BLOCK-relative and a creature-relative scan for [reg+4CCh] could never have found max HP even if it did write it; the offset to look for from inside that function is block+0x124. Searched: zero occurrences of `+124h]` anywhere in 0x820E04C..0x821369A, so the conclusion stands on the right evidence now. What CalcResults does write, sampled from its first 200 movs, is the attribute copies (+0x4A..+0x56 into +0x10..+0x1A) and the zeroing of the derived block at +0x66..+0xF2 with 1.0f seeded into +0xE6/+0xEA/+0xC6..+0xD2 and +0xEE/+0xF2, the last pair being the two regeneration rates row 1046 identified. STILL OPEN: which function computes the max-HP VALUE and writes it through set(obj, v, 1). A lead for gap #5 fell out on the way -- the death penalty reads *(creature+1006), i.e. +0x3EE, which is inside the combat block at block+0x46 and is the strongest candidate yet for the experience value that row 1048 could not find by dumping +0x420..+0x620.

The port had no way to read its own runtime state: framerate, window size, camera cell, sim tick and sector residency were all print-once startup lines or nothing at all, so any question about a live frame meant adding a print and rebuilding. godot-port/debug_overlay.gd is a CanvasLayer that answers them on one text block -- fps and process/physics milliseconds, window and viewport size, camera cell + sector + zoom step + ortho size, the cell under the mouse, sim tick/rate/dropped/actor count, the focus actor's cell, hp and facing, resident and queued sectors with settled-vs-streaming, draw calls/primitives/objects/nodes, static and video memory, engine version. F3 toggles it and it starts HIDDEN, so every existing capture runbook and md5 gate photographs exactly the frame it did before; --overlay starts it shown for a --shot=/--drive run that never sees a keystroke. It sits at the project root rather than in view/ for the same reason iso_camera.gd does -- it owns a _process, which parity/verify.gd's LAYER_RULES forbids there (layer gate re-run: files=21 violations=0). Text is rebuilt at 4 Hz rather than per frame. Every line reaches through a live engine API that can be renamed or moved without any visible failure, so checks/overlay_check.gd builds the real overlay against a real camera, sim and registry and asserts on its rendered text; verified end-to-end by an xvfb --overlay --shot= capture showing all nine lines populated in the streamed world. Full suite after the change: PASS=43 FAIL=0.

REGISTERED, NOT MEASURED. Retail draws a drop shadow under the hero and the port draws none. The fact was written down exactly once, in a code comment: view/player_view.gd:96, where it is noted as a nuisance contaminating the bottom of the silhouette during character-scale calibration. AGENTS.md STATUS 2026-08-17 (evening) decomposed the then-29.3% two-engine delta and made its FIRST bucket 'object-sprite shading + retail's drop shadows under every object and character (halo blobs in the diff, the port draws none)'. That bucket does not appear in row 1018's enumeration of the 13.55% measured the same night, no row since has closed it, and the word shadow appears in none of open-questions.md, world-sectors.md or game-wiring.md. It is now an Open entry in game-wiring.md, gap 6 in that document's current gap list, and a row in the open-questions index. WHAT IS FACT: the port emits no shadow pass; the only other occurrence of the word in the engine is shaders/object.gdshader:78, which is about Sacred's 4-bit alpha gradient and not a shadow pass. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED: (1) its pixel cost, never measured in any frame -- it is a CANDIDATE for the roughly 8.4pp of row 1018's 13.55% that the four named items (taskbar 1pp, cobbles 2pp, priest 1.2pp, hero 0.9pp) do not account for, and a candidate is not a finding; (2) whether the 'under every object' half is a separate pass at all, since object.gdshader:78 records that Sacred's sprites carry shadows, glass and smoke at partial alpha, so a static object's shadow may already be baked into its art and already drawn, leaving the hero's as the only one proven missing; (3) how retail draws the character's -- projected quad, sprite or blob -- which is untraced. The cheap first step is a measurement and not an implementation: crop the hero's footing in the existing retail/port pair and take the delta before anyone writes a shadow pass.

Row 1061 registered drop shadows as a gap and listed three things it deliberately did not claim: how retail draws the character's shadow, whether the 'under every object' half is a separate pass at all, and its pixel cost. TWO OF THE THREE ARE NOW SETTLED, and the evidence is our own binary rather than the lead that pointed at it. The chain was: a VK post from the Sacred NL author, whose site sacred-nl.necropol.sumy.ua is DNS-dead, recovered from Wayback as settingsNL.cfg, which carries a key named FORCE_BLACK_SHADOW. Grepping install/sacred for it returns that key AND six neighbours that no document in research/, engine/ or AGENTS.md has ever named: cGranny::renderShadow(), cGranny::renderShadowFake(), SHADOWDOT.TGA, SHADOW_TREE00.TGA, NOSHADOW and FLAGS:NOSHADOW. So retail has a named shadow render path in the Granny layer with a second cheaper mode beside it, the character shadow is a TEXTURE and not geometry, objects have their own shadow art which answers the 'separate pass' question YES, the pass is selective through a per-object opt-out flag, and a Settings.cfg key selects the mode. STILL NOT ESTABLISHED and deliberately not claimed: the pixel cost, still unmeasured in any frame, so this remains a CANDIDATE for the roughly 8.4pp of row 1018's 13.55% that its four named items do not account for; what renderShadow computes and how renderShadowFake differs; what NOSHADOW is set on; and which mode FORCE_BLACK_SHADOW forces. Seven string names are a map, not a mechanism. The next two steps are both cheap and neither is an implementation: crop the hero's footing in the existing retail/port pair and take the delta, then decode SHADOWDOT.TGA and look at it.

A completeness audit of the VK corpus found one real bug and three gaps, and the bug is the kind worth writing down: wall.getComments was called ONCE per post with count=100 and no offset loop, while the wall and the topic boards both paginated correctly, so every discussion past 100 comments was silently truncated -- and those are the busiest threads, which are the ones worth having. Seven posts were affected, including the pinned OverLookers post with 321 comments. thread_items_count also caps at 10, so nested replies past ten were dropped with no signal. Both are fixed: comments now page like the wall does, and a thread whose count exceeds its returned items gets its own call keyed on the parent comment. The refetch was made cheap rather than global by seeding the new state key from data already held -- each post's raw JSON carries comments.count, so comparing it against stored rows marked 10371 posts complete and refetched only 101, recovering 793 comments. All seven truncated posts now store exactly what the API reports. ARTICLES ARE MINEABLE AND NOW MINED, 91 of them, though not through the API: articles.get answers 'Unknown method passed' and no attachment among 12913 carries type article, so the only handle is the /@slug urls the posts themselves link. The desktop host is useless -- vk.ru answers 'your browser is outdated' and the SPA never renders server-side -- but m.vk.ru returns the article as ordinary HTML to a plain browser user-agent. Most are Raven Rock fiction chapters or MetaL's class build guides; the one of operational value is a 44 KB dgVoodoo guide, which matters because the Windows oracle depends on dgVoodoo2 2.87.3. NO SIXTH GROUP WAS FOUND, with a caveat about how that was established: groups.search REFUSES a service key with error 15 Access denied, so VK could not be asked directly and this is an absence of evidence from the corpus rather than a confirmed exhaustive list. The corpus's own cross-references yielded only VK path-words and one unrelated 131-member public. LEFT UNMINED BY DECISION, not by oversight: 9292 album photos and 362 videos. The initial survey reported photos as zero because photos.getAll returns 0 for these groups while photos.getAlbums does not, which is worth remembering before trusting a zero from that API. Corpus now 88914 items and 12913 attachments.

CORRECTION FIRST, because I asserted the opposite twice. Rows 1062 and the summaries around them claimed SetObjState was absent from this project's opcode table and was 'a live candidate for one of the 21 unnamed'. THAT IS WRONG. SetObjState is opcode 2, table B index 3, and has been named since the keyword tables were read on 2026-08-16. The grep that produced the false claim searched the PROSE of script-bytecode.md, which lists only a selection of names, while the full binding lives in generated/script-opcode-names.tsv -- a file the document references and which DID NOT EXIST on disk, though .gitignore explicitly un-ignores it. Regenerated and committed; the tool reports 121 entries, 120 of 141 opcodes named, 7 of 7 independent controls agreeing. A document that points at a generated file nobody generated is how a settled fact gets re-opened by mistake. WHAT IS ACTUALLY NEW is behaviour rather than a name, which is what the doc's own Open section asks for when it says A NAME IS NOT A BEHAVIOUR. sacred_orig carries a contiguous run of strcmp sites testing, in this order, lock (081c109e), Fix (081c10e4), ToInv (081c112a), unlock (081c1170), open (081c11b6), close (081c11fc), then enemy (081c1242), follow: (081c1288), hireling: (081c13ef), Damage: (081c1556). The strings sit adjacent in .rodata at 0x6a2b05 through 0x6a2b3b. Two ordered blocks, object states then NPC states, matching opcode 2 SetObjState then opcode 3 SetNPCState. THE BINDING IS INFERRED FROM ADJACENCY AND IS NOT PROVEN: no 4-byte value anywhere in the file lands inside 081c0d00-081c1700, so the region is inline code inside one large function reached by relative call, and the dispatch from opcode number to it was not found. INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION of the object side, from unrelated strings: cTrigger::setState (), cTrigger::resetState (), the log formats Trigger[%d] locked and Trigger[%d] unlocked, and the refusal cTrigger::setState () trigger is locked, at 0x6b7410 through 0x6b7464 -- so lock state is real and it is a property of the TRIGGER, not of the door. PROVENANCE AND ITS LIMIT: the lead came from a 2023 Russian modding thread recovered by tools/vk, describing a quest door held by a trigger and freed by setobjstate with unlock. The parameter is real and the trigger mechanism is real. Not established, and not claimed: the door and trigger id mechanics, the two object lists, and the name-collision bug the thread blames.
