ATTEMPTED AND NOT ACHIEVED, with the cost written down so it is not paid twice. Row 1067 said wiki pages and the Files sections were blocked rather than absent and that a user key would unblock them. A user key was obtained and IT DOES NOT. The VK ID flow itself works end to end and is now implemented in tools/vk/auth.py: OAuth 2.1 with PKCE pinned to RFC 7636's published vector, a two-phase paste login because a remote redirect cannot be caught locally, and a TLS callback catcher for the localhost case. Three registration facts cost a round trip each and are recorded so they are not rediscovered: a mini_app cannot use id.vk.ru/authorize at all and fails with a blank page or 'oshibka zagruzki' regardless of scope, which was confirmed by eliminating scope as the variable; VK refuses a plain http redirect at app-registration time with 'obyazatelen protokol https'; and it refuses localhost as a base domain, so the redirect has to be a real https domain, though it need not serve anything since the browser's address bar carries the code. THE WALL IS THE TOKEN CLASS, NOT THE APP. The token issued is genuine -- users.get returns Durov, wall.get on the operator's own wall returns their 156 posts, and VK ID's user_info names the account -- but pages.*, docs.*, groups.* and account.* all answer error 1051, method is unavailable with current profile type. The decisive test is that 1051 also fires for the operator's OWN documents and OWN group list, so it is not a permission on those communities; the whole method family is barred to this class of token. The cause shows in the grant: scope 'vkid.personal_info groups' was requested and 'vkid.personal_info' was returned. VK ID does not grant the classic social scopes at all, and the two flows that used to were disabled on 25 June 2024. EVERY OTHER ROUTE WAS ALREADY CLOSED in row 1067: service key gives error 28, m.vk.ru serves a login wall for page-<id> though it serves articles as plain HTML, a stored doc url fetched directly returns HTTP 418, and Wayback holds zero snapshots of vk.com/page-<gid>* or docs-<gid>*. So 613-plus wiki pages and the Files sections of five communities are recorded as UNREACHABLE by any supported route rather than as pending work. mine.py keeps --wiki and --docs because both are correct and would run against a token carrying those scopes; nothing obtainable today does.

The 2.2 GB disc added on 2026-08-24 is identified without extracting a byte, and my own MAP.md entry describing it was WRONG. It is not InstallShield: Setup.exe is MZP (Delphi PE32), the payload was built with Smart Install Maker v5.04, and the .cab files carry neither MSCF nor ISc( magic -- they are headerless split volumes at about 7.999 bits per byte. unshield is irrelevant and both cabextract and 7z fail. The installer stores its file table as plaintext strings, so a 379-path manifest was recovered with no extraction at all and is in tmp/sacred-plus/. It is 'Sacred Plus Internacional 1.8', a 2023 FAN REPACK by the Sacred Raven Rock team, whose VK group and mail address are embedded in it. Two structural proofs it is Plus and not Gold or Underworld: the manifest holds ZERO *03.pak files and ZERO LoadingUW*.bmp, both of which Gold ships in install/pak and in the extracted eng tree. WHY IT IS WORTH HAVING: the manifest lists World/static.pak, World/floor.pak, World/triggers.pak, World/sectors.keyx and World/sectors.wldx -- a SECOND, INDEPENDENTLY AUTHORED WORLD IN THE SAME FORMAT. Every world claim this project makes rests on one dataset, so this is the control that distinguishes a property of the FORMAT from a coincidence of our copy: whether WldxEntry +0x04 and +0x0c really are direct indices whose maximum equals count minus one, whether the 32-byte record holds, whether the corner order W N E S survives a different map. It also ships twelve language global.res files against retail's pair. CAUTION, and it is the canonical-first rule: the tree is modded. It carries lua5.1.dll, lua51.dll, caf.dll and a launcher.exe that appear in no retail tree, so its Sacred.exe is almost certainly patched and none of its Sacred.exe, bin/*.bin or PAK/* may ever stand as a retail oracle. Only World/ is interesting and even that gets diffed against retail before any claim. NOT ESTABLISHED: Sacred.exe's hash, because the config ZIP holding the payload offset table is ZipCrypto-encrypted and nothing is extractable offline; installing under Wine into a scratch prefix is the route, and Wine is present.

The 154 wiki pages and 91 articles are read out. They are overwhelmingly build guides, lore, quest walkthroughs and inter-community drama; exactly one wiki page of twenty largest is technical. NOTHING was found on the questions that matter most: floor.pak overlay tile selection, the authored draw order for building parts, wldx or keyx structure, and collision or pathfinding all return nothing. A scoping error is corrected here before it propagates: an agent reported that trigger returns zero hits across the whole corpus, and that is true only of the wiki and article kinds -- prefix-matched it returns 15 hits across posts, comments and topic comments, which is where row 1066's lead came from. THE VALUE IS CONCENTRATED IN TWO SACRED NL CHANGELOGS, v.17 and v.18, written by a binary-patching mod author who describes what he changed and therefore implies what retail does. Bearing on the drop-shadow gap of rows 1061 and 1063: he states retail has SUN shadows only and that they DO NOT MOVE, since his mod adds moon shadows and motion; and he adds a console command sw specifically for 'static shadows of 2D objects', implying a 2D shadow path distinct from the 3D one. Against the binary that is PARTLY corroborated and must not be overstated: install/sacred_orig names only cGranny::renderShadow and cGranny::renderShadowFake, two modes but both in the Granny layer, and no separate 2D function name exists -- what does exist is the ART for one, SHADOW_TREE00.TGA beside SHADOWDOT.TGA, and trees in Sacred are sprite objects. So a 2D shadow path is suggested by texture names and by a modder's console command, and is not proven by any symbol. Other testable claims: tiles and overlays are a real engine-level split, since his Ctrl+Shift+Y draws only those; object screen coordinates are computed such that at fractional zoom the seams between objects AND against the background shimmer; sector 2562 is Shirs-Pen and sectors carry a per-save visited flag, which is consistent with our 6050-record keyx but not more than consistent; .444 files are background textures whose loose-file override does not work, implying a different load path from object textures; and there is a named retail walkability hole, walking out through a wall in the Abandoned Mansion, which is a free collision parity case. Ctrl+F shows FPS and character coordinates in retail, which is a coordinate oracle the drive harness could read. Every one of these is a modder's claim and none is a citation.

The 74 files pulled out of VK are triaged, and the result that matters was sitting in our own install the whole time. GAME<nn>.PAK IS NOT A PAK CONTAINER. It is a save: magic AMS, version word 0x40, with exactly the allocation table and payload framing pax-saves.md already documents for hero saves -- 12-byte {DataType, Offset, UnpackedSize} entries at 0x100 and a 0xBAADC0DE + size + 24-byte frame ahead of standard zlib. It shares the .pak EXTENSION and nothing else. Measured over the nine independent GAME*.PAK in the corpus: 27 compressed sections and 27 of 27 inflate to exactly their declared UnpackedSize. EIGHTEEN SECTION TYPES appear -- 0x80 0x81 0x82 0x83 0x8B 0x8D 0x92 0x93 0x94 0x95 0x99 0x9A 0x9B 0x9C 0x9D 0xA0 0xA1 0xA2 -- and NOT ONE of them is documented, because pax-saves.md covers only the hero namespace 0xC3 through 0xCE. The two namespaces do not overlap, so DataType alone says which kind of save you are holding. AND IT WAS NEVER A VK FINDING: retail's own install/save/game01.pak is AMS 0x40 and carries the same eighteen types; the VK files only corroborate it nine times over. It went unnoticed because the document said 'hero saves' and nobody opened the file whose extension said pak. A ROBUSTNESS BUG WAS REAL AND IS FIXED: tools/formats/pak.py accepted a savegame as magic='AMS' v27 entries=64 layout=blob and printed plausible output -- it even decoded the save's own title string, 'Autosave - Sergeant Treville in Valor's Fortress', which is exactly what made it convincing rather than obviously wrong. It now refuses the AMS/AMH family and points at pax-saves.md; the real containers still probe correctly. STILL OPEN and deliberately not claimed: what any of the eighteen sections CONTAIN. The framing is read and the decompression is proved, not one section's semantics is established, and 0xA0 at 1.5 to 7.8 MB and 0xA2 at 0.1 to 7.3 MB are the two worth opening first. ALSO IN THE SET, unverified and listed for later: SacredFilesRes.zip carries genuine TXT-to-res format documentation plus 1289 symbolic global.res key names, checkable against global-res.md; sacredtools 3.3 carries a CHM documenting every Settings.cfg key, and Settings.cfg is documented NOWHERE in research/formats today though the VK copies alone show seven keys we do not carry; granny.dll1 is the real RAD Granny.dll of 2003-11-27, a direct oracle for granny-grn.md but proprietary and private-use only; and a 16 MB Funktionskonzept zu SACRED 2 authored by Franz Stradal in 2005 is a first-party Ascaron internal design document, which is a publishing-policy question before it is a research one.

THE FORUM CLAIM THAT STARTED THE VK EXERCISE IS ANSWERED. An English post credited the OverLookers team with altering Sacred's spawn triggers, method never published. They did not touch the engine: every behavioural change is recompiled script bytecode. ReBorn HD 4.6 is Inno Setup 6.1.0 and its payload extracts; it ships SRB\, a complete loose copy of retail's bin/ script tree. Matching every retail bin/**/*.bin against that set BY SIZE AND HASH rather than by name -- the installer names files by location index, so a name mapping would beg the question -- splits cleanly: startcode.bin 20 matched and 20 differ, funkcode.bin 11 matched and 10 differ, balance.bin and sets.bin differ, while questcode.bin, questpoolcode.bin and vectoren.bin are 20 of 20 BYTE-IDENTICAL and world.bin, world2.bin, wpmod.bin, treppe.bin, merc.bin, wea.bin, rust.bin, multistart.bin and static10_18.bin are identical too. So spawn behaviour in Sacred is DATA, and it is data in StartCode and FunkCode. A CORRECTION TO THE TIDY VERSION, because I checked it myself: defpos.bin is ALMOST untouched, not untouched -- 14 of 15 identical and ONE DIFFERS, which makes that one file the most interesting of the fifteen. Method caveat recorded in the document: size-bucket matching can pair two same-sized files that are not counterparts, so the per-row counts are approximate, though the pattern is far larger than that error term. WHY IT IS THE HIGHEST-YIELD EXPERIMENT AVAILABLE: this is a LABELLED before-and-after pair of the same bytecode where the author has told us what he changed, which is the one thing that can turn script-bytecode.md's own 'A NAME IS NOT A BEHAVIOUR' into a behaviour, for exactly the opcodes that differ. Both halves are already on disk. SEPARATELY, FOUR STRINGS ARE NOW OPENED that are in install/sacred_orig right now and that no document here mentions -- they came as mod leads and were then confirmed first-hand in our own binary: cWorld::remapTrigger_load(%s), which means the engine loads an EXTERNAL TRIGGER REMAP FILE and names a second half of our decoded-but-unwired triggers.pak; capture\world_spawn.txt and capture\world_spawn_num.txt, a BUILT-IN DEVELOPER DUMP of the spawn map to text, which if it can be triggered is retail's own ground truth for spawn placement; DungeonRespawn, which is Phase 7.1's subject; and TRIGGER_INSERT_SPAWNRENEW and TRIGGER_INSERT_ATTRACTOR, named trigger kinds. None is a finding yet -- four confirmed strings and no traced behaviour. CLEAN-ROOM: SacredReborn.exe and pureHD.exe are derivative copies of retail sacred.exe and SRB\*.bin are modified Ascaron assets; the observation of WHICH files differ is a fact and is safe, their contents are not ours to redistribute, and the extracted copies live only in tmp/. pureHD ships no sources on this disk despite its changelog saying they are open for v1.00 and v1.10, and it names two third-party libraries, Sacred API and Ecx Library, whose licences are unknown.

The retail-versus-ReBorn bytecode diff is run, and opcode 51 FillSector is where spawning lives. PAIRING FIRST, because it was the part that could have made the whole thing worthless: locNNN.bin is the installer's file list in directory order, each script folder a six-file group in alphabetical order, and more than sixty BYTE-IDENTICAL MD5 anchors to retail files fix every group's base index -- loc121 equals type_npc_daemonin/vectoren.bin exactly, verified independently. Every paired file is the same size as its retail counterpart and parses to the identical record count, and startcode.py consumed 100 percent of both sides with no parse failures. 20 startcode and 10 funkcode pairs. THE STRUCTURAL RESULT: no opcode count changed, no record was inserted or deleted, and no opcode appears in the mod that is absent from retail. Every edit is an in-place argument overwrite, which is why sizes are preserved exactly -- darkelve/startcode is 575839 bytes on both sides with different hashes. THE CHANGED SET: opcode 51 FillSector in 90 records, its 0x19 twelve-byte operand of three u32 moving in 290 slots, 163 down and 127 up, plus three slots of its 0x34 operand; opcode 67 SetVar in 40 records with all 40 decreased; opcode 8 CreateObj in 14 records. FillSector carries 90 of the 104 changed records, its name says it populates a sector, and the author's public claim is that he altered spawns -- so this is a BEHAVIOUR for a named opcode, which is exactly what script-bytecode.md's own Open section asks for when it says a name is not a behaviour, and it was reached from a labelled before-and-after rather than from a guess. The bidirectional movement of the 0x19 operand reads as re-tuning per-sector density or level bands rather than one global scale. The changes do NOT cluster per class: all eight playable-class folders carry the same five funkcode and two startcode changed records while the bulk sits in the shared netscript bodies at 21, 22 and 21, so one shared script body was edited and propagated into each class build. THREE LIMITS, RECORDED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED: SetVar's uniform downward move across all forty instances reads as a single global knob lowered, plausibly an interval or a cap, but that is inferred from direction alone and is not confirmed; CreateObj's fourteen records are probably NOT a structural edit because tag 0x3c is a VARIANT and a changed u32 re-frames everything after it, so a value edit misreads as a restructure; and the nine largest retail funkcode bodies, the non-addon ones at about 3.96 MB each, are ABSENT from the extraction and were never diffed. NO NAMING OPPORTUNITY: all three changed opcodes were already named by the keyword tables, and not one of the 21 unnamed opcodes participates in the diff, so the hoped-for route from this pair to naming an unknown instruction is closed. Nothing of the mod's bytecode is reproduced -- opcode numbers, tag numbers, counts and directions only.

BOTH LEADS FROM ROW 1072 ARE CHASED AND BOTH ARE CLOSED, one of them as my own error. CORRECTION FIRST: row 1072 and open-questions.md listed cWorld::remapTrigger_load as 'named in retail, written up nowhere'. THAT WAS WRONG -- formats/install-inventory.md line 144 already carried it: 'static10_18.bin, 41440, generated remap, magic map v0, 2574 x 16 B, consumed by cWorld::remapTrigger_load'. A grep that missed a prose document put it on the open list, and I propagated it. This is the same failure as the SetObjState claim in row 1066 -- searching one file and concluding about the corpus. WHAT THE CHASE ESTABLISHED ANYWAY, and it is a useful negative: remapTrigger_load is function 0x080f3d88 in sacred_orig, it opens the literal bin\static10_18.bin, reads a 256-byte header whose magic is map\0 with the record count at +4, then one fread of count*16 -- verified against the shipped file at 41440 bytes, count 2574, and (41440-256)/16 equalling 2574 exactly. Records are four u32; fields 0 and 1 are equal in early rows and fields 2 and 3 are 0xCCCCCCCC filler there and small integers in the tail, so {old_key, new_key, x, y} is inferred from magnitude with 2056>>6=32 and 2144>>6=33 matching sector coordinates. Its ONE caller is the savegame 'Triggers' block, reached from cEngine::save and cEngine::load, and the remap branch is taken only when stream_version <= 0x11 and the build id falls outside [0x2a30,0x2af7] and below 0x4650. So it is a trigger-ID renumbering table for savegames written by pre-release builds, and it is NOT the missing half of triggers.pak. A sibling function generates bin\static18.bin with magic SMP3 and 20-byte records, logging 'eta 20-30 minutes' -- a developer-side tool whose output does not ship. TARGET TWO IS DEAD CODE. The capture\world_spawn writer is 0x082d790c and it does dump exactly what we wanted: for each of regions 0 through 49 a line of level, creature name, and Sector X-Y, plus a 500-slot per-region creature census in world_spawn_num.txt, both fopen'd 'wt' relative to the working directory. But it has ZERO CALL SITES -- no call, no jmp, and no function-pointer table entry anywhere in .text; the single 4-byte address match in .data sits in unstructured garbage and is a coincidence. There is no Settings.cfg key, console command or keypress reaching it. Retained by the linker, unreachable at runtime in the shipped Linux build. NOT CHECKED: whether the Windows build reaches it, which is one grep if a stock Windows exe is ever obtained, and a live dump would still be retail's own ground truth for spawn placement.

THE MILESTONE METRIC IS NO LONGER STALE. It still has no gate and no agreed threshold, so 13.62% is a number without a verdict attached; see .planning/REQUIREMENTS.md, whose exit criterion states in terms that it has a target and no test.

CHASING TWO VK LEADS PRODUCED A THIRD FIND IN OUR OWN BINARY, and it is the one worth keeping. Retail's script loader prints an ordered fourteen-stage trace at 0x6a4a00-0x6a4d40: hero, openQuests, dialogText, mouseEvent, questKram, avl_trigger, base trigger, regionsnamen, ref2name, functionen, quest, questpool, questregions, ready. NOT ONE of those stage names appears anywhere in research/ before today. Three stages are followed immediately in the string table by a filename -- functionen by bin\sgf.bin, quest by bin\sgq.bin, questpool by bin\sgqp.bin -- and NONE OF THE THREE EXISTS IN THE INSTALL. The binary names exactly 24 .bin paths and these are the only ones with no file behind them besides Abin\static18.bin. They are bin\-relative, i.e. GLOBAL and class-independent, where every script file we actually read is per-class under bin/type_npc_<class>/ as FunkCode.bin, QuestCode.bin and QuestPoolCode.bin -- and the three stage names match those three files one for one. THE OBVIOUS READING IS NOT CLAIMED: what is proven is the adjacency in the string table, the bin\ prefix and the absence from disk. Whether they are ever written, read out of a savegame, or dead paths like capture\world_spawn in row 1074 is open. SECOND FACT FROM THE SAME REGION AND IT BEARS ON A READER WE HAVE: 'Funks Vector Korrektur (%d Durchlaeufe)' with counters for Changes, Overwrites and New members in Funks. FunkCode's symbol vector is corrected at load, in multiple passes, and entries can be changed, overwritten OR ADDED -- so vectoren.bin, which script-bytecode.md records as decoded at 5684 sectors and 0 orphans, is the INPUT to that pass and not its result. What the correction does is unestablished. Also there and previously only half-known: the quest trigger callbacks QIS_Trigger, QIS_OnEnter, QIS_OnExit, QIS_OnLose and QIS_OnSetUp, keyed by Sector and Region. Written up in script-bytecode.md and registered in open-questions.md.

TWO NEGATIVE RESULTS AND ONE PROCESS FAILURE, all recorded so nobody repeats them. MouseOver.bin from the VK set carries magic MOB\x01, which has the exact shape of the pak family's three-byte tag plus version byte -- ITM v5, TEX v3, MDL v3, SPF v1, OBJ v1, ACS v2, WLK v5 -- and it is NOT one of them. pak.py reads its entry count as 4093046339 and overruns the file. THE CHM IS OPENED AND THE HEADLINE IS A CLOSED OPEN ITEM, NOT A KEY LIST. Row 1071 deferred sacredtools 3.3 as 'a CHM documenting every Settings.cfg key'; that is half right. A PUBLISHED TOOL CARRIED A BUG THIS LOG REFUTED NINE MONTHS OF ROWS AGO, and it was found by a lookup that should have worked and did not. tools/formats/globalres.py's name_hash ran h = (h*0x71 + toupper(c)) % MOD in UNBOUNDED PYTHON ARITHMETIC. Row 954 established that retail's sub_80ACC3E is INT32: 0x71*h passes 2**32 from the fifth character on and wraps, and the modulo is x86 idiv whose remainder takes the DIVIDEND's sign, so h goes negative between iterations. The two agree for exactly four characters and diverge after. THE FAILURE MODE IS THE ONE THIS PROJECT KEEPS MEETING: every numeric id in the shipped files is three to five digits, so the tool's self-check -- by_id(9400) is 'Heavenly Magic', by_id(1100) is 'Attack Speed', both four characters -- was GREEN throughout while every symbolic name silently returned None. I hit it head-on: SacredFilesRes.zip's hash-0.txt scored 0 of 50, and I very nearly recorded that as 'these names are not in our global.res'. What stopped it was testing the tool against its own documentation -- global-res.md states UI_QUICKSAVE resolves to 'Quicksave' and INVENTAR_RES_PHYSICAL to 'Physical Resistance', and those returned None too. A documented claim failing to reproduce is what exposed the tool rather than the data. WITH THE INT32 WRAP: UI_QUICKSAVE, INVENTAR_RES_PHYSICAL, D1Dorf_01 ('Smith'), EWT_Schwert ('Sword') and DQ_BAUER_BEGRUESSUNG_LOG all resolve, and hash-0.txt goes 0 of 50 to 50 OF 50. FIXED in globalres.py with an _i32 helper, and the self-check now asserts FOUR SYMBOLIC NAMES, all longer than four characters, so the 64-bit form cannot pass again. AUDIT OF WHAT THE BUG TOUCHED TODAY: rows 1079 and 1080 verified 435 combat-art string ids through this tool; every one of them is at most four digits and buggy-versus-correct disagree on 0 of 435, so those results stand unchanged. Row 1080's other claim also survives but for a better reason than I gave: the InheadImage texIDs 14807 and neighbours are FIVE digits, exactly where the two hashes diverge, so my 'returns None' was luck -- re-tested under the correct hash they still return None, and that sheet is still unverified. THE PORT WAS NEVER WRONG: engine/formats/resources.gd carries the int32 form and documents why, and the 64-bit version in checks/resources_check.gd is a deliberately-kept control, labelled as such.

SacredFilesRes.zip is opened and row 1071's description of it needs one correction: it does NOT carry '1289 symbolic global.res key names'. 1289 is the BYTE SIZE of hash-0.txt, which holds FIFTY names. I misread a size as a count. The zip is three files -- a converter SacredFilesRes.exe, a Russian TXT-format.doc whose text is Word-fastsaved and yields only fragments, and that name list. THE EXECUTABLE IS THE USEFUL ONE. It names the res-to-txt conversion in three stages -- 'Stage 1. Hash order:', 'Stage 2. Tabulators:', 'Stage 3. Text lines:' -- and carries a ten-value entry-type enum nothing here had: CET_SECTION, CET_PARAM, CET_LISTNAME, CET_LISTDATA, CET_LIST_LIST, CET_LIST_WORD, CET_WORDNAME, CET_WORDDATA, CET_WORD_WORD, CET_WORD_LIST, plus six ERROR_ codes. STAGE 1 BEING 'HASH ORDER' IS AN INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION that the index is ordered by name hash and not by id or insertion -- reached here by reading the file, and by another author from another direction. THE LAST TECHNICAL DEFERRAL FROM ROW 1071 IS OPENED. granny.dll1 is RAD's Granny.dll, built 2003-11-27, copyright 1998-1999 RAD Game Tools, md5 c1ffdac411b506382f2acb7550b5ccf4, a 4-section PE32 with 101 named exports and no unnamed ones. ITS IDENTITY IS NOT IN DOUBT AND THE TEST IS TWO-SIDED. Windows Sacred.exe imports 54 of the 101, the subset it calls, and names Granny.dll in its import table. The Linux sacred this project runs carries ALL 101 plus 21 further Granny-prefixed names that are the error enum -- GrannyOK, GrannyInvalidCall, GrannyOutOfMemory, GrannyMismatchedVersions and the rest -- which is what a STATIC link looks like and explains why the Linux build has no Granny.dll import at all. NOT ONE EXPORT IS UNUSED BY BOTH BINARIES. So the DLL's export surface is exactly Sacred's Granny API. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A NAME LIST: granny-grn.md's Ground truth section describes tools/granny_oracle/ as calling the Granny 2.x runtime, and reading the code shows the chain is .GRN then grn2gr2.dll then .GR2 then granny2.dll -- a 2.x runtime answering questions about a 1.x file that a CONVERTER HAS ALREADY REWRITTEN. That conversion step is the one link in the ground-truth chain nobody has audited, and this DLL removes it: it reads .GRN natively because it is the library that shipped with the game. The two obvious first questions are already open in that document -- the EIGHT of 3421 animation clips that do not decode, and DUNKELELVE.GRN and MAGICIAN.GRN, the two of seven class body meshes that do not build. Both are recorded there as our decoder being short rather than the map being wrong, which is exactly the shape of question a vendor runtime settles. NOTHING HAS BEEN RUN. This row records that the oracle is in hand, not that it has answered anything; a harness needs Wine and a freestanding 32-bit PE stub of the kind granny_oracle/granny_probe.c already is. LICENCE, UNCHANGED AND BINDING: the DLL is proprietary RAD code, it stays in donotpublish/, it is never committed, and it may be read only by observing the OUTPUTS of its exported API -- the terms granny_oracle/README.md already sets, which is why no third-party binary lives in that directory. The version string in the file reads 1.2b and that is unconfirmed by anything but the string itself.

THE CONTROL THE HANDOFF ASKED FOR IS RUN AND IT SETTLES A BUILD-DEPENDENCE QUESTION. Sacred Plus Internacional 1.8 installs under Wine from builds/windows-disc/sacred-plus in a contained prefix -- Z: removed, D: pointed at tmp/ -- yielding 3.0 GB including a complete PRE-UNDERWORLD World/. It is 3982 sectors against retail's 6050, (3058432-256)/768 exactly, and every container matches retail's magic and version: WLK v5, WLD v5, OBJ v1 twice, TRG v1. pak.py reads all three paks unmodified. THE SHARP TEST IS THE floor.pak BIT SPLIT. world-sectors.md records that Armalion packs 16/16 and retail 17/15 and calls the split build-dependent; Sacred Plus is the third corpus and it makes the RULE visible. Its tiles.pak holds 47099 tiles. Under a 16/16 read the maximum low field is 47098 -- EXACTLY THE LAST TILE -- and no record exceeds the table; under 17/15 the maximum is 67071 and 1628732 records point past the end, which is impossible. Retail is the mirror image: 16/16 tops out at 65420 and leaves 24711 tiles unreachable, 17/15 reaches 90131, exactly ITS last tile. So the split is NOT an era or a version marker, it tracks the tile table crossing 2^16, which is what Underworld did when it grew the table from 47k to 90k. A reader must take the split from tiles.pak's COUNT; all three files are OBJ v1 with the same 16-byte record, so the version byte does not carry it. ACTIONABLE ON OUR SIDE: checks/floor_check.gd hardcodes LOW17 and TILE_COUNT 90132, correct for the install we target and wrong for any pre-Underworld data -- recorded as a pinned assumption, not changed. THE OTHER READINGS ALL HOLD ON THE NEW CORPUS: +0x08 is non-zero in 0 of 16310272 Sacred Plus cells, matching retail's 0 of 24780800, which with Armalion's 73 populated cells dates the dropped layer to before the shipped game; +0x1e never sets a bit above 2, values 0 to 7 only; +0x1f's high nibble uses all 16 classes; and all 3982 sectors inflate to their declared size with 0 failures. ONE OF MY OWN ERRORS ON THE WAY: the blob index triple is (flags, offset, size) and I first unpacked it as (offset, size, _), which read 0xCCCC uninitialised padding and returned max low = 52428 for BOTH worlds -- a suspiciously round number is what gave it away.

AN OPEN ITEM CLOSES, AND IT WAS OUR DECODER RATHER THAN THE DATA. granny-grn.md recorded five malformed names in texture.pak's 25535 entries and left them as a divergence. THE NAME FIELD IS 32 BYTES, NUL-PADDED, AND A NAME THAT IS EXACTLY 32 CHARACTERS CARRIES NO TERMINATOR. SHADOWDOT.TGA proves the layout: 13 characters, NULs to byte 32, then the u16 pair w=64 h=64. So a reader that scans for a NUL runs straight into the WIDTH field, and every stray byte in the old list is that width's low byte. AMAZONE_ARMOUR_KURZKHEMD_CELAL.T is followed by 256 x 256; GIGANT_SPIDER_HAIR_RED_DEMON.TGA by 64 x 16, whose 0x40 is the '@' that was read as part of the name; PHEX_SHE_THIEF_HELMET_LEATHER.TG by 64 x 64, same '@'; and INSTRUMENT_HARFE_128X128_ALPHA.T by 128 x 128, whose 0x80 is the '\x80' -- AND THAT ONE SELF-CONFIRMS, because the name says 128X128 and the bytes read 128 by 128. THE COUNT WAS ALSO WRONG. Scanning all 25535 entries: 25528 are NUL-terminated and SEVEN fill the field, not five. The three that were never flagged -- ELVE_SORVERESS_LEDERHARNISCH.TGA, HORSE_BRIDLE_LEATHER_METAL01.TGA and HORSE_BRIDLE_LEATHER_METAL02.TGA -- are exactly 32 characters WITH .TGA intact, so they read correctly by luck. The previously-listed fifth entry TEX followed by 0x03 0xbf C does NOT reproduce as a literal byte search and is unaccounted for; it is recorded as unreproduced rather than quietly dropped. WHAT SURVIVES OF THE ORIGINAL OBSERVATION: two of the four have a TRUNCATED extension, .T and .TG, because the full name would exceed 32 characters, and retail builds its key by appending .TGA to a stem -- so retail genuinely cannot reach those two. The other two were only ever a decoder artefact. THE LEAD CAME FROM THE RAVEN ROCK DLC, whose file names sent me to compare against texture.pak's index; the answer was in our own file the whole time.

THE OPEN QUESTION FROM ROW 1089 IS ANSWERED AND THE ANSWER IS NO, WHICH IS THE USEFUL DIRECTION. Raven Rock's DLC/ directory of 990 loose files looked like an engine load-order rule the port would have to reproduce. It is not one. srr.dll, 704563 bytes, built 2021-01-28, is a RUNTIME CODE PATCHER and its own data says so: 34 byte-pattern signature strings of the shape make_signature emits -- 8A 44 24 0F 8B D0, 8D BC CD 0C 71 09 00, 3D FF 1F 00 00 -- sitting beside PATCH PAYLOADS rather than more search patterns: 90 90 90 90 NOP sleds, 90 E9 AC 00 00 00 a jump, B8 44 00 00 00 90 a mov eax 0x44. It imports VirtualProtect, left the source filename winsig.c in the binary, carries EUpdatePatch::Open and EUpdatePatch::Read, and names the literal 2.29, the game version it targets. At 0x7b204 there is a table of directory-name slots -- seven DLC, eighteen hero, then forty more DLC -- one per patched call site. So the mod finds Sacred 2.29's file-open code by signature, makes it writable and rewrites it to consult a directory name from that table. RETAIL HAS NO SUCH PRECEDENCE AND THE PORT NEEDS NONE. Recorded as a negative deliberately: an override layer is a plausible thing for a 2004 engine to have, and reproducing one that does not exist would have been silent permanent divergence. WHAT IS IN THE DIRECTORY, measured against our own indexes: 606 of the 915 .tga are replacements of names already in texture.pak; ALL 68 .grn are already in models.pak; 31 of the remaining textures are present in the ARMALION 2001 PRERELEASE and not in retail; and 278 are in neither and are fan-made. THE 31 ARE THE CUT DAS SCHWARZE AUGE HERO LINE that global-res.md records -- AMAZONE_BODY, BORON_PRIEST_BODY, BORON_PRIESTESS_BODY, ELVE_SORCERESS_BODY, MAGICIAN_BODY -- the art Seraphim and Gladiator replaced, put back from the prerelease. ALSO NOTED WITHOUT CHASING: srr.dll carries season names in three languages, Winter/Spring/Summer/Autumn with German and French forms, a UI_WND_CONSOLE string and a %sys_dir% template vocabulary, so the mod does more than file redirection; none of that is traced.

READING THE 22 IN FULL, AND ONE HYPOTHESIS DIES ON THE WAY. Each of the 22 appears exactly 20 times, matching the 20 string-pool copies of row 1092, so there are 22 symbols and not 440. The set: scalars TYPE_BOOL, TYPE_BOOLEAN, TYPE_CHAR, TYPE_DWORD, TYPE_FLOAT, TYPE_INTEGER, TYPE_LONG, TYPE_STRING, TYPE_LPSTR, TYPE_LPWSTR, TYPE_NULL, TYPE_UNKNOWN; arrays TYPE_ARRAY_BOOLEAN, TYPE_ARRAY_DOUBLE, TYPE_ARRAY_INTEGER, TYPE_ARRAY_STRING; Win32 structs TYPE_POINT, TYPE_RECT, TYPE_WINDOWPLACEMENT; and TYPE_ARGUMENT, TYPE_FUNCTION, TYPE_HEXSEQUENCE. TWO ASYMMETRIES WORTH NOTING because they say the set is hand-written rather than generated: TYPE_ARRAY_DOUBLE exists with no scalar TYPE_DOUBLE, and TYPE_BOOL and TYPE_BOOLEAN both exist. WHAT IT IS: a typed config-persistence system. TYPE_WINDOWPLACEMENT, TYPE_POINT and TYPE_RECT are exactly what you serialise to remember a window, and the DLL carries UI_WND_CONSOLE beside them; with the seven %app_path%-style macros, the 34 lexer character classes and the XML comment tokens of row 1092 it is a config-file library, not a game feature. THE HYPOTHESIS THAT DIED: TYPE_HEXSEQUENCE sitting near 34 hex byte-pattern strings suggested the patch signatures were TYPED CONFIG VALUES loaded from a file. THEY ARE NOT. The only configuration filename anywhere in srr.dll is Sacred's own Settings.cfg, so the 34 signatures are COMPILED IN, and TYPE_HEXSEQUENCE is just another member of a generic type system. Stated because it was a good guess and the evidence refused it. ALSO MEASURED: srr.dll names only SEVEN Settings.cfg keys -- COMPAT_VIDEO, GFX32, LANGUAGE, NETWORK_SPEEDSETTINGS, SLOTINFO, WINDOW_HEIGHT, WINDOW_WIDTH -- and Raven Rock's shipped Settings.cfg carries 59 keys of which EVERY ONE is already in the 156-key union of row 1080, so it adds nothing. WINDOW_WIDTH and WINDOW_HEIGHT are read by TWO INDEPENDENT MODS, pHD.dll and srr.dll, which share no other code, so that pair is the community's de-facto name for a resolution override rather than one mod's invention; SLOTINFO is now attributed to srr.dll. The lowercase token pool is MSVC locale and math boilerplate -- country names, acos, ceil, fmod, frexp -- which is a third confirmation of the library reading.

THE PATCH SITES ARE DISASSEMBLED AND MY ROW 1091 READING WAS WRONG IN ITS CENTRAL CLAIM. Row 1091 said the 34 hex strings are 'code to find, the shape make_signature emits'. THEY ARE PAYLOADS, NOT PATTERNS. The whole patch table is one function, sub_100033EA, 0xa5b bytes, and it is a flat list of 80 writes with no scanning anywhere. sub_10002722, reached through the thunk that takes those strings, walks one with strtoul(s, &s, 16) and writes each parsed byte into the target. Every address is a HARDCODED CONSTANT rebased as hLibModule minus a stored default base plus K, which is exactly why the DLL is locked to one version and carries the literal 2.29. SIX WRITE PRIMITIVES, all thin wrappers over a byte-poker that IsBadWritePtr-checks and advances: fill with 0x90 for n bytes; fill with byte b for n bytes; parse-hex-and-write; write a string's bytes in place with no NUL; write 0xE8 followed by fn minus p minus 4, i.e. INSTALL A CALL DETOUR, then n NOPs; and write a WORD. THE SPLIT OF THE 80 IS THE FINDING. Thirteen are code patches in .text between VA 0x616593 and 0x75AD60 -- two detours to sub_100014DD and sub_10001492, one 126-byte NOP sled, two WORD writes derived from xRight and hDest, and four identical 68 01 00 00 00 sequences which is a push of 1. THE OTHER 67 ARE IN-PLACE STRING OVERWRITES IN THE DATA SECTION between VA 0x8E9A8E and 0xA1C880: 49 write DLC and 18 write hero over whatever three or four bytes were already there, and they land in FIXED-STRIDE RUNS -- eighteen at a 16-byte stride across 0xA1AF18 to 0xA1B028 and six at a 20-byte stride -- which is the shape of arrays of fixed-size string slots. SO THE MOD DOES NOT ADD A LOOKUP PATH, IT REWRITES SACRED'S OWN HARDCODED PATH STRINGS IN MEMORY. The conclusion of row 1091 survives and is strengthened: retail has no DLC/ precedence and the port needs none. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED AND I STOPPED RATHER THAN GUESS: which string each of the 67 addresses overwrites. That needs a 2.29 binary and WE HAVE NONE -- the Windows disc exe, gold228-rus, pureHD at 2.28 and the unfinished 2.30 are all other versions, and reading those addresses in the disc exe lands on unrelated data, motion names and German quest-editor keys. community/patch/Sacred_2_29_14_Patch holds Sacred22914.svp and a Patcher.exe that could build one, which is the route if anyone wants the per-site answer.

THE SITES ARE CHECKED AND THE ANSWER IS COMPLETE. The 2.29 binary needed was not something to build: it ships with the mod. srrp.exe is unpacked, base 0x400000, sections whose file pointer equals their RVA, and every one of the 67 string-patch targets falls inside .data's raw range. The Sacred22914.svp route was a dead end anyway -- its header names an expected source md5 eb00fb615bea2d53ced02b48522f4e73 and NONE of our four candidate binaries matches it. THE PATCHES REDIRECT EXACTLY THREE DIRECTORY PREFIXES. 42 sites write DLC over PAK\ -- MODELS.PAK, TEXTURE.PAK, SOUND.PAK, TILES.PAK, MIXED.PAK, MOTIONS.PAK, SNDPROFILES.PAK, ITEMS.PAK, WEAPON.PAK, Creature.pak, the Models.tmp and Texture.TMP lookups, SAVEGAME.BMP and LOADGAME.BMP. 7 write DLC over Bin\ -- Balance.bin, Wea.bin, World.bin, World2.bin, wpmod.bin, NetScript%s and Addon\NetScript. 18 write hero over Save or SAVE -- SAVE/GAME%.2d.PAK, SAVE\*.PAK, Save\Hero%.2d.pax, Save\Hero00.ptx through Hero05.ptx. Three and four characters over three- and four-character prefixes with no NUL, so the rest of each path survives: Bin\Balance.bin becomes DLC\Balance.bin. It matches the installed tree, which ships a DLC/ directory and an EMPTY hero/. THE REAL PRIZE IS IN RETAIL, NOT THE MOD. The 16-byte-stride run I measured in row 1095 resolves to Pak\Items00.pak through Pak\Items15.pak -- ALL SIXTEEN SPELLED OUT -- and those strings are in RETAIL'S OWN BINARY, including the Linux sacred this project runs, alongside PAK\ITEMS%.2d.PAK, .\PAK\MODELS%.2d.PAK, PAK\TEXTURE%.2d.PAK and a singular PAK\Mod1.pak. NOT ONE of those strings is documented anywhere in research/. SO items03.pak, models03.pak AND texture03.pak ARE SLOT 3 OF A SIXTEEN-SLOT NUMBERED OVERLAY ARRAY the engine already indexes, not a one-off promo naming; install-inventory.md called them 'a beer advertisement', which is right about the CONTENT and wrong about the MECHANISM, and is now corrected in place. Only slot 3 ships, and no file answers Mod1.pak in any install we hold. NOT ESTABLISHED: the load ORDER and override semantics between slots, and whether a higher slot masks a lower one or merely adds -- sixteen strings in a table are a capability, not a rule. THE LEAD CAME FROM THE MOD AND THE FINDING WAS IN OUR OWN BINARY, which is the third time today.

THE SLOT SEMANTICS ARE READ FROM RETAIL'S CODE AND THE RULE IS COMPLETE. sub_8139520 in install/sacred is TypeManager::loadItemTypes -- it names itself in its own warning string -- and sub_8139814 holds the loop. The disassembly at 0x8139e5b is unambiguous where the decompiler's rendering was not: ebx starts at 0, sprintf formats PAK\ITEMS%.2d.PAK with ebx, THEN ebx is incremented, THEN the loader is called with the incremented value, and the test is cmp ebx,0Fh jle. So ITEMS00 is loaded with ordinal 1 and ITEMS15 with ordinal 16, and EVERY numbered slot takes the add-on path; the base path with ordinal 0 belongs to PAK\ITEMS.PAK, loaded first by the two TypeManager callers sub_8134FA4 and sub_81355E2, which print loadItemTypes... for the base and loadItemTypesCustom... before the numbered loop. THE OVERRIDE RULE, per 128-byte record: with ordinal 0 the record lands at index i, its SEQUENTIAL POSITION in the file; with ordinal >= 1 it lands at an index READ FROM THE RECORD ITSELF at record offset 118. An add-on record therefore NAMES ITS OWN TARGET ID rather than taking a position, and it overwrites whatever is there. If the target already holds a populated record -- the byte at record offset 62 is set -- the engine prints 'TypeManager::loadItemTypes() - WARNING!!! Overwrite of base itemType [%d] because of add-on [%s]!' AND OVERWRITES ANYWAY. So higher slots mask lower ones and the rule is LAST LOADED WINS, ASCENDING. A missing file is skipped SILENTLY: the loader fopens, gets NULL and returns 0 with no message, which is why an install carrying only slot 3 boots normally. For ordinal >= 1 the loader also adds a per-slot delta accumulated over j from 0 to ordinal-1 out of a table, to two fields of the record at +24 and +118, which is an id-space shift per preceding slot. IT MATCHES THE RECOVERED DEBUG.LOG LINE FOR LINE -- loadItemTypes..., PAK\ITEMS.PAK V5 #32768, loadItemTypesCustom..., PAK\ITEMS03.PAK V5 #32768 -- and only slot 3 appears there because only slot 3 ships. STILL NOT ESTABLISHED and deliberately not generalised: MODELS%.2d and TEXTURE%.2d have their own loaders which were NOT traced, and nothing was found that loads PAK\Mod1.pak. Only the item path is read.

THE GAP REQUIREMENTS.md HAS CARRIED SINCE THE MILESTONE WAS SET IS CLOSED: the metric had a target and no test, and now has analysis/tools/parity/start_scene_gate.sh, which exits 0 or 1 like every other gate here. THREE HUMAN DECISIONS, asked rather than assumed, and recorded in the script's own header so a later reader argues with the decision and not the code. FIRST, SCOPE: the verdict comes from the WORLD band alone, 0,0,1024,600. The milestone is the Seraphim and her LOCATION; the taskbar is interface, it differs by 22.99% against the world's 11.00%, and a single whole-frame number would let UI art dominate the verdict and block world work. The taskbar and the full frame are still measured and printed every run. SECOND, RATCHET RATHER THAN TARGET: no threshold was invented. The gate stores the best value ever measured in start-scene-baseline.tsv and FAILS when a run is worse by more than TOL, currently 0.10pp. That catches regressions from the first run and needs no agreed number; naming an absolute target stays open and stays a human decision. THIRD, STRICTNESS: the verdict remains any-nonzero-channel because this project reproduces retail exactly rather than acceptably, and png_delta.py gained an OPT-IN --mae flag printing mean absolute error beside the percentage -- 11% differing at MAE 5 and 11% at MAE 40 are different problems and the percentage cannot tell them apart. The default single-field output is UNCHANGED because drive/session.sh parses it. Current readings: world 11.00% at MAE 5.05, taskbar 22.99% at MAE 12.91, full 13.62% at MAE 6.77 -- so the taskbar is worse on both axes at once. A FLAW WAS FOUND BY RUNNING IT AND IS FIXED. The first end-to-end run measured 10.95 and 13.59 against a baseline of 11.00 and 13.62 taken minutes earlier on the same build, and the gate dutifully ratcheted itself down onto that noise -- which is the same 0.07pp run-to-run difference row 1075 recorded as uncharacterised. A ratchet that updates on ANY improvement walks its own baseline down on luck and then fails honest runs. TOL is now applied on BOTH sides: an improvement must clear the same tolerance the gate forgives. Re-run, the 0.05pp gain is correctly absorbed and the baseline holds. All three branches are exercised: a baseline of 9.00 gives FAIL and exit 1, 12.00 gives PASS improved and rewrites the file, and the true value gives PASS. STATED AS DEBT IN THE SCRIPT: TOL 0.10 is set from two observations and not from a measured distribution.

CORRECTION FIRST, TO MY OWN ROW AN HOUR OLD. Row 1099 handed on a lead by calling the hero's cost a shading difference and saying the port draws her MARKEDLY DARKER than retail. That was an eyeball impression and the numbers refuse it: over the differing pixels the port is on average +8.09 BRIGHTER, brighter on 63.4% of them, and the per-channel ratios are 1.10 R, 1.06 G, 1.13 B -- a port that is uniformly brighter, not darker. WHAT THE CAPTURE ACTUALLY SHOWS IS DIFFERENT EQUIPMENT. Retail's Seraphim wears light blue armour with white boots, gold trim and a horned helm; the port's wears heavy dark segmented plate on shoulders, forearms and legs, dark boots, and carries a different weapon. THE PORT SAYS SO ITSELF AND NOBODY HAD CONNECTED IT TO THE METRIC: main.gd line 47 reads 'a full starting kit is not what a new retail character has. It is here so the composition path is exercised by the default run; a real inventory replaces it', and START_SET := 6 sits under it. A placeholder chosen to exercise a code path is the second largest identified contributor to the milestone delta. THE COST, measured with an EXACT silhouette rather than a guessed box -- the port driven twice, once normally and once with --hideplayer, so her pixels are the difference between two PORT frames: both engines drew her and the colours differ, 2114 px = 0.344pp of the world band; the port drew her where retail did not, 956 px = 0.156pp; retail drew her where the port did not, 1722 px = 0.280pp; total 4792 px = 0.780pp. Roughly 44% surface and 56% SILHOUETTE, so it is two problems and not one. The two silhouette rows rest on a threshold estimate of retail's own mask and carry method uncertainty; the total and the surface row do not. THE RESULT THAT SHOULD BE READ TWICE: hiding her entirely scores BETTER. The world band is 10.95% with her and 10.88% without, so the port's hero rendering is currently worth MINUS 0.07pp. Retail draws her either way, so the port's version does not remove the disagreement, it relocates it. ROW 1018'S 'UNMOVED BY DRESSING' DOES NOT EXONERATE THE OUTFIT: it recorded that START_SET 6 and the bare rig score within 0.01pp of each other and concluded the outfit is not what differs. Both are simply wrong in the same amount, which is what you expect when NEITHER is what retail starts her in. What retail actually equips a new Seraphim with is now an open question and is worth up to 0.34pp on its own.

THE QUESTION ROW 1100 OPENED IS ANSWERED AND THE ANSWER IS APPARENTLY NOTHING. cEngine::initGame names the step in its own trace, 'cEngine::cEngine() equipe' at 0x80b7692 in the Linux binary, immediately after initHero(e). It fills the new hero from TWO ARRAYS whose indexing is read off the code rather than guessed: dword_8B89740[class*20 + slot] is the WORN table, 8 classes by 20 slots with slots 0 to 18 used, and dword_8B899C0[class*8 + i] is the CARRIED table, 8 by 8. Each entry is an item id and AN ENTRY OF ZERO IS SKIPPED, so a zeroed table equips nothing. The class index is the hero id with 8 and 9 folded down by one. EXACTLY ONE FUNCTION WRITES EITHER ARRAY and it is a TEXT PARSER -- the same one that reads BalanceDmg, BalanceRes, regionkill and 390 other keys, i.e. the balance-text family. The two keys are equip and inventory, and the grammar falls out of the strchr('='), strchr(','), strtol sequence: equip=<CLASS>,<slot>,<itemid> and inventory=<CLASS>,<itemid>. The class token is matched with strncasecmp at 4 characters against a fixed list which is now recovered in full: SERA 0, GLAD 1, MAGE 2, DELF 3, WELF 4, VAMP 5, DWAR 6, DAEM 7. NO SHIPPED FILE CARRIES SUCH A LINE. Searched the whole retail install, bin/balance.bin itself, the Armalion prerelease, Sacred Plus, every community mod and tool, and the 88914-item VK corpus: ZERO occurrences of equip= anywhere, and balance.bin contains none of the strings equip, inventory or SERA. WHAT IS PROVEN is the layout, the grammar, the class map, the zero-skip and the absence of any input in every corpus we hold. WHAT IS NOT PROVEN, and is stated in the document rather than glossed: the parser is reached through a POINTER rather than a direct call so its call site was not traced, and a file we do not hold cannot be ruled out by searching the ones we do. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PORT IS SHARPER THAN THE ANSWER. engine/main.gd dresses her from sets.bin set 6, which install-inventory.md records as 'the seven Seraphim pieces' -- a MAGIC ITEM SET like Uriel's Legacy, not a starting kit -- and main.gd line 47 already says a full starting kit is not what a new retail character has. If retail is bare then the port's remaining 0.34pp surface gap is its BASE MESH OR TEXTURE and not its equipment, and row 1018's finding that the bare rig scores within 0.01pp of set 6 says the port's bare rig is wrong too. That is the next measurement and it needs a --nodress path the port does not currently have.

A --nodress FLAG WAS ADDED TO THE PORT AND THE MEASUREMENT SETTLES WHERE THE HERO'S COST LIVES. The guard sits INSIDE _dress_player rather than at its two call sites, so a third caller cannot be added that quietly ignores the flag, and it prints the same dress line with set=none so a run says what it did. Driven at the Seraphim start, 4000ms, against the same retail frame: DRESSED with START_SET 6 the world band is 10.95% at MAE 5.05 and the hero box 31.10%; BARE with --nodress it is 10.92% at MAE 5.02 and 29.94%; MESH HIDDEN with --hideplayer it is 10.88% at MAE 4.96 and 28.81%. SO UNDRESSING HER RECOVERS 0.03pp OF HER 0.78pp, about 4% of her cost, AND HIDING HER ENTIRELY IS STILL BETTER THAN EITHER. The two port renders are not identical to each other -- 2324 pixels differ between dressed and bare, 0.378% of the world band -- so the outfit is plainly on screen and simply does not move the score. THE CONCLUSION IS THAT THE PORT'S SERAPHIM IS WRONG IN A WAY EQUIPMENT CANNOT FIX. The remaining roughly 96% of her cost is the BASE RIG -- mesh, texture, pose or scale -- and that is where row 1100's 0.34pp surface gap actually lives. This also independently reproduces row 1018's result that START_SET 6 and the bare rig score within 0.01pp of each other, a finding I doubted an hour ago because the two outfits look nothing alike; they do look nothing alike, and it still does not matter to the metric. NOT CHANGED AND DELIBERATELY SO: START_SET remains the default. Row 1101's reading that retail equips nothing argues for making --nodress the default, but main.gd line 47 keeps set 6 so the composition path is exercised by the default run, and trading test coverage for 0.03pp is a human call and not a measurement.

Synced the project docs to the state rows 1075-1102 left them in. AGENTS.md and MAP.md both still led with the 13.55% of 2026-08-17 and neither mentioned that the metric has a gate; both now open on STATUS 2026-08-25 with the world/taskbar/full bands and the ratchet. game-wiring.md's Open section still asked what retail equips a new Seraphim with and still named the hero's footing crop as the cheap next step, both of which were answered the same day (rows 1099, 1101, 1102); folded in, including the three-configuration table that shows undressing recovers 0.03pp of her 0.78pp. open-questions.md gained a Decisions waiting on a human section, flagged as the one section not derived from any document's ## Open, holding the absolute delta target and the --nodress default. The method lesson is the fourth: auditing the index against the corpus with find . silently reached ONE file, because analysis/ is a symlink farm into the three repos and find does not follow symlinks without -L; the real count is 19 documents and 20 headings, exactly what the preamble claims. Same shape as the grep-one-file error of row 1066. Link scan of the research repo is clean apart from a printf %s in a generated file.

Investigated the base rig row 1102 named as the remaining hero defect. Using the port's exact silhouette (drawn minus --hideplayer) and retail's thresholded one in the same column: port dressed 3070 px, 146 tall, 43 wide, centroid x 512.4; retail 3837 px, 149 tall, centroid x 511.9. Height agrees to 2 percent so scale is not the defect, and a cross-correlation over dx -8..+8 and dy -6..+25 peaks at dx=0 dy=+5 improving IoU only from 0.441 to 0.460, so it is not a translation either. What is left is shape: IoU 0.46 means less than half the silhouette overlaps at best alignment. Retail's idle holds her arms out with a drawn sword, the port's holds them in. The bare rig scores WORSE than the dressed one (0.441 vs 0.460), a second independent reason equipment is not the lever. Separately and more important as a method result: two retail runs of the same route at the same millisecond differ by 1.31 percent of the world band, and a difference map puts effectively all of it on the hero, the NPC beside her and the quest marker, which animate. That noise floor is larger than the entire 0.78pp hero budget and nearly twenty times the 0.07pp port-side spread of row 1075, so no single-frame pose comparison can see past it and any pose work needs a multi-frame retail reference first.

Chasing the hero found something worth more than the hero. Retail's start frame carries a robed NPC with a quest marker beside the player that the port does not draw at all: 5639 px at MAE 56.8 = 0.918pp of the world band, against the hero's whole 0.780pp at MAE 17. The mechanism is in retail's own log: cInterpretSQW runs WorkFunktion Sector50039Init then Sector50039Enter as the player arrives, sector being the cell divided by 64. Those are ordinary FunkCode procedures reached by name through vectoren.bin, which holds 11414 Sector and 128 Region entry points. Sector50039Enter is 515 bytes: 6 CreateNPC, 4 CreateObj, 1 SpawnValues. CreateNPC arg 3 is a packed cell, one u64 read as lo=x hi=y, giving four NOVIZIN.GRN, a CHICKEN and a RABBIT plus four FX_FIRE_L objects - a cathedral courtyard authored per sector. None of the six is on screen: the camera is orthographic at size 768/2.0 so the world-to-pixel scale is exactly 2.0 and with HW=48 the visible half-width is 5.3 cells of x-y, while those six are 16 to 40 cells out. The same arithmetic clears --npcs of a defect it appeared to have, since its five startcode thieves at 20 cells and beyond are legitimately off-camera rather than silently missing. Inverting the projection from the on-screen figure's measured offset of -95.1,+98.0 px puts her at cell 3236.5,2512.5, and the rounded integers predict that offset back to within two pixels. She is placed by neither literal-coordinate path: a scan of all 23494 procedures finds no CreateNPC or CreateObj within 8 cells, and all 319 startcode NPC records carry a cell with the nearest at 20.4. Her source is open.

Row 1105 left open where the robed NPC beside the Seraphim comes from, having ruled out both literal-coordinate paths. She is created by QIS_OnEnter1, the OnEnter hook of quest 1, titled Tutorial, 311 bytes at offset 1702864 which the port's own Sacred.Vectoren resolves: SetVar PoolDLG, four QuestBook entries naming BOOK_HQstart_sera01 through 03 and SERA_WAS_TUN_TUTORIAL, then CreateNPC with args res:17095, 679, novizin1, auftrag10, 1, ECS_HEALING, then NPC_Goto res:17095 to cell 3237,2514, then QuestKompassObj res:17095 which is the ?! over her head, then SetVar atmos10 and SetVarBit 10. The reason no coordinate scan could find her is structural and worth more than the answer: this CreateNPC carries NO POSITION AT ALL. Its argument tags are 0x1 0x2 0x4 0x9 0x6b 0x67, naming a handle, a creature id, a script name, a task and a combat art, and the cell arrives one record later against the handle. Searching for a CreateNPC near a cell was looking for something the format does not put there. Creature 679 is NOVIZIN02.GRN, distinct from the sector script's four 677 NOVIZIN.GRN. The handle is stable across the corpus: QIS_OnEnter9, Das brennende Schwesternhaus, walks the same res:17095 on with NPC_Goto 3237,2519 then Teleport 3237,2520 then NPC_Goto 3237,2524 then SetNPCState auftrag09. CORRECTION to row 1105: the world-to-pixel scale is 1.0, not 2.0. I read iso_camera.gd's declared default zoom_index := 0 instead of the step main.gd:734 actually sets, which is 1. No conclusion changed, since every sector-script placement and every --npcs thief is off screen at either scale, but the cell row 1105 inferred for this figure was doubled. At the corrected scale cell 3237,2514 predicts a screen offset of exactly -96,+96 px against the measured -95.1,+98.0, and that two-pixel agreement is what fixes both the placement and the scale. The port already reads the hook and world/quest_log.gd can already run one; nothing fires quest 1's OnEnter on a new game.

Wired quest 1's OnEnter to fire on a new game, per row 1106. world/script.gd gained four opcodes (SetVar, CreateNPC, NPC_Goto, QuestKompassObj) and five argument tags, one of them a new VARIANT class that reads a u32 and decides its own shape: both forms occur in this single hook, since CreateNPC names its NPC with the string form and the NPC_Goto two records later gives that NPC an x,y,z triple, so a reader that fixes on one shape decodes half the hook as plausible nonsense. The refusal invariant was widened rather than weakened: run() now also refuses when the HOST cannot receive an opcode's effect, so a plain QuestLog gets the same all-or-nothing answer as an unimplemented opcode instead of writing four book lines and then crashing. New world/quest_cast.gd collects the cast as data and builds nothing, since world/ may not touch the scene tree; main.gd turns each placement into a rig and --noquests opts out. The hook executes all ten records and builds NOVIZIN02.GRN at cell 3237,2514, exactly where the script says. THE RESULT IS NOT YET A WIN AND THAT IS THE FINDING: the world band moves 10.95 to 11.11 against the same stored retail frame and the NPC window 0.918pp to 1.074pp, stable over two runs, so drawing her costs 0.16pp MORE than drawing nothing. Same shape as row 1100 for the hero: retail draws the figure either way, so a port figure in nearly the right place doubles the disagreement rather than removing it. What is right is the model, the cell and the horizontal placement, centroid x 416.9 against retail's 416.5, agreeing to under half a pixel, which is what confirms the projection and the handle matching. What is wrong, in cost order: she is drawn 10 to 19 percent too tall and about 12 px too high, she faces the camera where retail faces away, she has no drop shadow, and the ?! marker is deliberately not drawn. The height error is the important one because view/player_view.gd scales every rig by one global constant, 133/73, calibrated on the Seraphim alone from two landmarks in one frame that disagree by 6 percent, and its own doc already calls that a relative calibration rather than an absolute one. This is the first independent second-model test of that constant. Both height figures come from threshold masks of a white robe on pale stone, which is why the error is a range and not a number. Incidentally re-confirms row 1106's corrected 1:1 world-to-pixel scale from a different direction: player_view.gd's calibration block states ortho size 768 over a 768-px viewport. A hoisted Sacred.Rigs construction took the build from 8967 ms to 92 ms.

Asked to fix the character scale, I measured it instead and there is nothing to fix. Row 1107's claim that the port draws NOVIZIN02 10 to 19 percent too tall was measurement error: I compared the port's exact silhouette, obtained by differencing two port frames, against a retail mask obtained by thresholding retail against the port's hero-less world, and that retail mask had swallowed both the ?! quest marker above her head at rows 300 to 330 and her drop shadow below her at rows 465 to 495. Segmenting her instead on her own brightness inside her own column, a white robe on a mid-grey floor, which a marker outside the column cannot enter and a shadow darker than the floor cannot either, gives retail 122 px against the port's 125. That is 2.4 percent, comfortably inside the 6 percent by which the original two-landmark Seraphim calibration already disagrees with itself, so RETAIL_HUMANOID_PX over REF_HEIGHT equals 133 over 73 PASSES its first independent second-model test rather than failing it. A second hypothesis also died: drawing the same NPC at the hero's own cell as a one-off diagnostic lands her feet at exactly y 385, the hero's own foot row, and inside the hero's own x range, so there is no per-model rig-origin offset and the two models ground identically. What the remaining 27 px vertical disagreement with retail actually is, is ANIMATION PHASE. The same rig at the same scale measures y 330 to 454, 125 px tall, at cell 3237,2514 and y 234 to 385, 152 px tall, at cell 3236,2511, a 22 percent swing in drawn extent from nothing but the clip's phase, because main.gd seeks each NPC to fmod of a hash of its cell so that a capture is reproducible. Retail's figures animate too, row 1104 having measured 1.31 percent of the world band as run-to-run variance concentrated on exactly them, so a single frame cannot settle a pose question on either side. The method lesson is the third of its kind today after rows 1099 and 1100: a mask built by thresholding one image against another carries everything that differs between them, not the thing being measured, so segment the subject on its own properties instead. I also corrected myself mid-investigation on the x placement, which was right all along at centroid 416.9 against retail's 416.5.

Audited the port's state end to end. All 43 checks pass and parity/verify.gd reports 22 files with 0 layer violations, so the engine is green. Three inconsistencies found and fixed. First, seven sites decoded Granny bone and clip names with get_string_from_utf8 while the fourteen other string reads in formats/ used get_string_from_ascii; Sacred's strings are CP1252, so a byte such as 0xb4, an acute accent, made Godot emit a parse error and substitute U+FFFD, costing 35 log lines from rigs_check, 7 from bindagree_check and 669 in one drive session. The seven were symmetric with each other so bone matching never broke, which is why this is a legibility fix and why the group had to move together. Second, checks/README.md still said pax_check needed a third-party SACRED_CHARS corpus and exited 1 without one, which stopped being true when that check was rewritten to read the install's own templates/hero00.ptx through hero07.ptx; a README describing a gate as conditionally red hides a gate that has gone green. Third, _build_quest_cast carried an untyped items parameter where _dress_player next door types it Sacred.Items, three untyped loop variables, an inferred-Variant rigs, and four calls to placed() to print one line. THE MEASUREMENT WORTH KEEPING is the control the decode change needed. Two runs of the SAME build differ by 3710 px, which is 0.604pp of the world band and MORE than the 2848 px the decode change moved, so a pixelwise diff alone would have called a no-op a regression exactly as it nearly did. But both runs score 11.11 against the same retail frame, identical to 0.01pp, because the pixels that wobble are already inside the set that differs from retail. So the port has a 0.6pp pixel noise floor and a 0.01pp SCORE noise floor, six times below the gate's TOL of 0.10, which is what makes that tolerance sound. Retail's own floor is 1.31pp of pixels from row 1104. The rule that falls out: never compare two captures pixelwise and call the difference a regression, compare their scores.

Row 1108 left the start NPC's pose as the open item. Two defects, both fixed and measured against the same stored retail frame: world band 11.11 to 11.01, NPC window 1.077pp to 0.978pp, gate PASS against an 11.00 baseline. FIRST, THE CLIP. All three NPC builders in main.gd called Rigs.clip_for, the best geometric score, where view/player_view.gd has always called rest_clip for the hero. For a standing character clip_for is routinely wrong: NOVIZIN02.GRN gets PRSS_WALK_BH where rest_clip gives PRSS_IDLE_BH, THIEF2_MAL.GRN gets another character's WUE2_WALK_BH where rest_clip gives the prefix-matching TH2M_IDLE_BH, and SERAPHIM.GRN's own clip_for is SERA_SPECIAL_MULTI_2WAFFEN, a two-weapon special attack, which is why the hero path already used rest_clip. The start NPC was walking on the spot. rest_clip prefers IDLE then FIDLE then WALK and falls back to clip_for, so no mesh loses an animation. SECOND, THE PLACEMENT. cell_to_world maps an integer cell to its CORNER and that is right for the hero, who is spawned at a cell and whose feet land on retail's to the pixel, y 385 in both engines with x within 1. It is wrong for an NPC that WALKED here, because retail's NPC_Goto converges on the middle of the target cell. Her feet measure corner 456, centre 480, retail 483, so a half-cell offset closes 24 of the 27 px and the remaining 3 are slack between an exact port mask and a brightness-segmented retail one. The offset moves a figure 24 px down the screen and 0 px across and x was already correct, so a fit would have needed both axes to move. Her resting place is reproducible: three retail runs put her extent at exactly y 362 to 483 and x 402 to 425, while a fourth caught her at y 340 to 419, still walking at the four-second mark, which is itself the evidence that this is a destination and not a spawn point. Isolating the two took holding the animation phase at 0 across two cells, because main.gd seeks each NPC by a hash of its cell and pose therefore confounds with position. Drawing her still costs 0.06pp against omitting her, down from 0.16pp; what remains is her facing, which retail turns away from the camera and nothing in the hook specifies, the drop shadow the port draws for nobody, the undrawn ?! marker, and a rendering defect noticed in the crop but not yet investigated: the port's robe is semi-transparent, her legs and arms visible through it, where retail's is opaque.

Asked to fix the transparency I reported in row 1110, I tested it first and there is nothing to fix. The claim came from a 4x crop comparing retail's nun, who is turned AWAY from the camera, against the port's, who faces it: what I read as legs and arms visible through a translucent robe was the garment's own front, gold filigree included. Rendering the port's rig at yaw 180 shows a solid opaque figure with a face and no see-through anywhere. Two independent measurements agree. First, decoding every texture the two character models name gives a=255 on EVERY texel across ten skins, movizin_legs, novizin_head, novizin_body3, novizin_hands, novizin_arms, novizin_belt, Sera_head, Sera_arms, Sera_body and Sera_legs, with zero partial and zero transparent pixels, so there is no alpha to blend. Second, switching the material from TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA to TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA_DEPTH_PRE_PASS changes the rendered frame by ZERO pixels in the NPC window and 3 in the hero box, which is inside the port's own 0.01pp score noise from row 1109. That zero is itself the proof: a rig genuinely blending its own surfaces would change a great many pixels under a depth pre-pass. The material was therefore left exactly as it was, which is the ladder's answer to a fix that buys nothing. ONE REAL DEFECT WAS FOUND AND IT IS A COMMENT. player_view.gd asserted that DEPTH_DRAW_OPAQUE_ONLY 'still writes the depth buffer so opaque terrain occludes correctly', which is the opposite of what the mode does: it means only OPAQUE materials write depth, so a transparent rig material writes none. Terrain occludes a rig correctly because TERRAIN writes depth, not because the rig does. The comment is corrected and records the measurement, so the next reader does not re-derive it. Worth noting for the transcribe-retail rule: install/sacred links glAlphaFunc and glDepthMask, so retail used alpha TEST plus depth writes rather than sorted blending, and the depth pre-pass is the faithful model even though it is not currently worth its cost. This is the fourth reading error of the day after rows 1099, 1100 and 1108, and the third caused by comparing two images that differ in more than the one variable being judged.

A material draw group's `mesh` field is a 0-based index into the FormMesh list, and each FormMesh (0xCA5E0C03) node's int32 payload is the 1-BASED index of its Mesh node counted over ALL Mesh nodes in directory order -- the same reference the bone-list pairing already trusts, read for a second purpose. Measured over every entry carrying groups: on 1563 of 1565 the submesh it resolves to has exactly the triangle total its groups declare, and the two that disagree (SERABFG.GRN, EDLST_RUND_GESCHL_KLEIN.GRN) resolve to the same submesh a triangle-count rule picks and disagree only on the count, each declaring one triangle against a 114- and an 80-triangle mesh. The group order is a per-file permutation of the reader's submesh order with no single rule: GLADIATOR and DWARF are a 3-cycle, WALDELFE_DARK a transposition, SERAPHIM the identity.

view/model_view.gd reconciled group order to submesh order by TRIANGLE COUNT and refused the split whenever two submeshes shared a face count. Census over all 1567 buildable KIND_MESH entries: 143 refused on that ambiguity, and the twelve of those naming more than one texture rendered as flat untextured clay because one merged surface carries one material. Two were character bodies -- THIEF2_FEM.GRN (11 groups, 8 materials) and ELVE_SORCESS.GRN (7 groups, 7 materials) -- and both drew as featureless silhouettes. Replacing the count rule with the FormMesh reference textures both correctly; ELVE_SORCESS resolves all seven of her body-part skins (skirt, legs, shoes, body, head, arms, hands) through a material table whose indices run to 12 against 7 textures.

Four entries carry geometry no material group claims: ELVE_SORCESS.GRN (six whole 14-triangle submeshes) and 14 triangles each on GIGANT_SPIDER.GRN, CHEST4.GRN and DWARF_CHEST_02A.GRN. Whether retail draws them is OPEN -- a draw batch is what binds a texture, so unclaimed geometry has no stated material. Drawing it as clay was tried and refuted visually: ELVE_SORCESS grows a column of pale lumps down her spine. The port now draws such triangles only where the entry names exactly one texture, which leaves no ambiguity about which skin they take, and counts them otherwise as ModelView.ungrouped_triangles.

STRIKES the granny-grn.md claim that DUNKELELVE.GRN and MAGICIAN.GRN, two of the seven class body meshes, do not build at all. Re-tested directly 2026-08-26: both decode mesh_arrays and mesh_weights, and both render fully textured -- DUNKELELVE 1856 verts / 2115 tris / 82 bones / 8 of 8 surfaces textured, MAGICIAN 1316 / 1516 / 75 bones / 6 of 6. Also measured while checking the influence ceiling: 955 of 1567 buildable entries decode weights and 612 do not, but every sampled failure is an unskinned prop (shields, doors, swords), which is the format's own way of saying a mesh is rigid rather than a decode shortfall.

The material-group join change moved the start-scene world band from 11.00% to 11.06% (MAE 5.05 to 5.19), full frame 13.62 to 13.67. The gate PASSES -- 0.06pp is inside its 0.10 tolerance -- but it is above the port's own run-to-run score noise of 0.01pp measured in row 1109, so it is a real if small movement and is recorded as such rather than called noise. It is not caused by the dropped ungrouped triangles: drawing them back for single-texture entries left the number at 11.06 unchanged. The remaining cause is the split itself, which now gives start-scene objects their per-batch textures instead of one.

REFUTES my own report that DWARF.GRN renders collapsed and distorted. The claim came from two misreadings. First, the default figure yaw of 270 shows a very broad character edge-on, where a correct stocky dwarf reads as a formless blob; at yaw 0 he is plainly a dwarf with arms, legs, feet and a braided beard. Second, his skeleton view is a starburst of spokes from the waist, which I read as a broken parent chain -- they are eight 4-bone chains named Bone01, Bone05, Bone09, Bone13, Bone17, Bone21, Bone25, Bone29, i.e. authored beard-braid or cloth bones, and they account for 32 of his 117 bones against GLADIATOR's 68. The one genuinely odd link, Bip01 L/R Thigh parented to Bip01 Spine rather than Bip01 Pelvis, is shared by GLADIATOR and SERAPHIM, both of which render correctly, so it is how Sacred's rigs are authored and not a decode error. Confirmed against retail: the character-select screen draws the dwarf at large scale and his proportions, stance, hanging arms, short bent legs and hunched shoulders match the port's.

REFUTES my own report that GLADIATOR's torso and SERAPHIM's thighs carry dark blotchy patches the port draws wrongly. The regions are real: Sera_legs.tga's lower ~60 percent and a panel of Gladiator_body.tga are mottled dark brown against clean art elsewhere. They are AUTHORED and retail draws them identically. Three independent joins already pinned the chain -- retail's own GL uploads correlate 1.000 with our decode of both images, the batch-to-texture links match retail on 44 of 45 batches, and GLADIATOR's UV box matches retail's own glTexCoordPointer array including the six vertices outside the unit square. The direct test settles it: retail equips a new Seraphim with nothing (row 1101), so the start-scene capture shows her BARE, and retail's own frame draws her with the same dark brown thighs between a skin-toned midriff and white knee boots that the port's figure viewer draws. The regions look unfinished because they are the parts equipment covers -- retail's character-select Gladiator hides exactly that midriff and thigh band behind a belt and kilt.

THE ORACLE FOR CHARACTER DRESSING, captured directly. Retail's new-game Seraphim wears NO armour at all -- no helmet, no chest plate, no shoulder pieces, no gauntlets -- and carries TWO blades, both hanging point-DOWN at her sides, the long one in her RIGHT hand (viewer-left, she faces the camera). Retail's character-select screen shows the same body plus WINGS and the two blades, so wings are a character-select-only display. This CONTRADICTS the comment at main.gd:1123, which claims a retail new-game frame shows her wearing helmet, armour, belt, shoulder, gloves and boots and carrying the sword -- eight of set 6's nine members.
