WHY THE PORT'S DRESSED HERO IS DISPLACED, measured rather than eyeballed. view/model_view.gd re-binds a worn garment by NAME onto the wearer's skeleton, keeps the GARMENT'S OWN bind pose, and admits the garment when at least one bind bone's local rest agrees -- a rule its own comment calls weak. Measured over set 6's seven garments against SERAPHIM.GRN: each shares 55 to 68 bone NAMES with her body but agrees on only 16 or 17 LOCAL rests, and global agreement composed through the parent chain is far worse at 1 or 2, confirming local is the right quantity and that the disagreement is real. This is row 1054's two rig revisions seen from the other side: her body mesh is on one revision and her own armour on the other, so a garment's bind pose takes its vertices into bone spaces that sit elsewhere on her. The visible result is four stacked copies of boot geometry at her shins and a garment displaced upward through her skull, which I first misread as the sword.

CANDIDATE, MEASURED BUT NOT SHIPPED. Replacing the worn garment's bind pose with the WEARER's own -- skin.add_bind(b, _skeleton.get_bone_global_rest(b).affine_inverse()) instead of piece._skin.get_bind_pose(i) -- removes the garment displaced through her skull and brings her whole upper body to a close match with retail's frame; the four stacked boot copies survive it. It is the standard formulation, since a bind pose belongs to the skeleton being bound to, and it is right exactly where the two skeletons' rests disagree, which is 3 of 4 shared bones here. NOT COMMITTED because nothing available can validate it: retail's new character wears no armour, so the start-scene gate cannot tell a correctly skinned garment from a garment that shrank, and eyeball improvement is not a measurement. Reverted pending either a retail frame of an armoured character or a decision to stop dressing from a set at all.

EXTERNAL PRIOR ART for equipment attachment, found by web sweep: the community GRN Model Viewer at sacred-tribute.com/3d, a self-contained HTML/JS reconstruction (credits RuDDick, Zerisius, Nex, Claude, ptasev; derived from ptasev's Age of Mythology Granny work). It is the ONLY public implementation of the attach maths -- every other Sacred tool is balance/save/data work and silent on mesh attachment. Its weapon path: take the wearer's rest-pose WORLD matrix for the hand bone rebuilt with UNIFORM scale (cube root of the absolute product of its three components, because Sacred's Biped bones carry non-uniform scale that otherwise shears the weapon), take the weapon's own grip world matrix rebuilt with scale forced to exactly (1,1,1), attach = hand x grip-inverse, bake into the vertices and rebind the whole weapon to that single hand bone at weight 1.0. Its armour path is the same invert-and-compose shape but PER BONE, matched by name never by index, with unmatched armour bones skipped. Handedness: if an item goes to the left hand but carries no Bone_weapon_02, fall back to _01 and pre-multiply a scale(-1,1,1) X-mirror; when _02 exists, NO mirror -- mirroring anyway gives a weapon in the right place but backwards.

A REAL DISAGREEMENT between the external viewer and this project's own corpus measurement, recorded because it is unresolved and load-bearing. The viewer attaches weapons to Bip01 R Hand / Bip01 L Hand (and shields to Bip01 L Forearm) and IGNORES the wearer's Bone_weapon_* bones entirely; the researcher measured that 3 of 8 hero bodies carry no Bone_weapon_* at all and that SERAPHIM carries only _01, and flagged as an open unknown what the wearer-side socket is then for. This project measured the opposite way round (granny-grn.md, Equipment sockets): over 1571 rigged entries the socket-to-parent-hand ROTATION is within 15 degrees on 299, 30-60 degrees on 13, and 90-180 degrees on 107, so substituting the hand for a missing socket is invention with a known 25 percent failure rate, and on SOLDIER it laid a kite shield flat across the chest. Our refusal has more measurement behind it than the viewer's substitution, but the viewer renders equipped characters correctly, so neither is settled. For SERAPHIM specifically the question is moot on POSITION: her Bone_weapon_01 sits at local origin (-1e-6, 0, -1e-6) on Bip01 R Hand, i.e. exactly at the hand, so the two models differ only in rotation.

ROOT CAUSE of the four stacked boot copies on the port's dressed Seraphim, corroborated by two independent routes. The external researcher read SERAPHIM.grn's mesh name table as Angel_arms, Angel_body, Angel_head, Angel_Hair, Angel_ponytail_L, legs, shoes -- the base body has its OWN shoes sub-mesh -- and this project's own texture dump independently lists Sera_boots.tga among the six textures SERAPHIM.GRN names. Equipping SeraBoots01.grn on a body that still draws `shoes` puts two boots in the same place. It generalises: Gladiator ships Gladiator_boots.tga and MAGICIAN ships magician_boots.tga, while Dwarf and Wood Elf use one whole-body texture instead. Retail must therefore HIDE the base-body sub-mesh an armour piece covers, and HOW it picks which to hide is documented nowhere -- the viewer does not implement hiding at all, it stacks and offers manual visibility toggles. The likely vocabulary is the 18-slot equipment array at cCreature+0x1A4 (main hand 0x0D, off hand 0x0C, mount 0x12, slots 0x00-0x06 helmet/body/belt/arms/legs/shoes/gauntlets), whose slot names line up one-to-one with the base-body sub-mesh names.

DungeonRespawn is a balance.bin config key (string at 0x86db161), not a region or trigger type. It is parsed by the balance loader at 0x0812ba04 (FSTP 0x812e739) into the global float 0x8b89dec, default 1000.0 (the outdoor counterpart Respawn lands at 0x8b89bc0, default 300.0). The value is consumed by the per-region respawn/world-update function 0x0827a158 (its only caller is 0x8270968). At 0x827a98c the code computes edx = [region+0x9a]/100 + dungeonFlag and, if nonzero, loads DungeonRespawn (flds 0x8b89dec at 0x827a9bf) else Respawn (flds 0x8b89bc0 at 0x827a9fb). That interval is the respawn delay: at 0x827aa70 elapsed game time is divided by 100 and compared against it, and if not exceeded the region is skipped (jbe 0x827fb8b). When the timer elapses the region timestamp [region+0x9a] is rewritten (0x827aad5) and the respawn action runs (0x827aadb+): it re-queries the region, iterates its creatures and clears the present/spawned flag at +0x59c to 0, then uses rand() to reposition or recreate them. Trigger is therefore a per-region timer selected between the dungeon and outdoor respawn interval by region type; it is reachable in single-player because the config is loaded at init and 0x0827a158 sits on the per-frame region-update path.

The DungeonRespawn/Respawn balance keys are written to two distinct global floats by the same loader 0x0812ba04: FSTP 0x812e739 stores DungeonRespawn to 0x8b89dec (Respawn to 0x8b89bc0) and a second parser pass FSTP 0x0812ff91 stores DungeonRespawn to 0x08b8dc6c (Respawn to 0x08b8da40, FSTP 0x0812ff44). The respawn function 0x0827a158 demonstrably reads 0x8b89dec/0x8b89bc0 at 0x827a9bf/0x827a9fb; balance-globals.tsv additionally credits 0x08b8dc6c to FUN_0827afb6 (a respawn-related function near 0x0827a158). Both copies hold the same configured value, so the dungeon respawn interval is effectively the single DungeonRespawn tunable; the duplication implies the balance block is parsed into two mirrored config structures.

The retail Sacred creature AI is a hardcoded per-creature state machine, not the cPath/cPathAstar/cPathFloodfill pathfinding classes, which are 100% dead: all 8 virtual methods (0x83a080c,0x83a0822,0x83a089a,0x83a08b4,0x83a08da,0x83a093a,0x83a0954,0x83a097a) and all 3 vtables (0x87285d0,0x87285b8,0x87285a0) and typeinfos (0x87285e8,0x87285f0,0x87285fc) have zero cross-references. The per-tick driver is the cCreature vtable slot-2 virtual sub_8180B22 (14,339 bytes, 362 basic blocks, CC 238), invoked each tick by the sim thread and type-routed through cCreature slot-9 virtual sub_819D7BE (which calls the hero update sub_82205D6 at 4 sites). sub_8180B22 embeds two switch dispatchers: an outer 17-case switch (jumptable 0x8183A04) and an inner 15-case switch on creature field +0xFC (the documented death/lifecycle state; jumptable 0x81838DB), each case calling a dedicated per-state handler (case0->unk_819459A, case1->unk_81846D0, case2->unk_8233C34, case4->unk_81D83E8, case5->unk_8194514, case6->unk_82F2B68, case8->unk_81D257A, case9->unk_818AA4E). It hard-special-cases individual creature types (cmp [creature+0x10],0xED) and uses .rand for AI variance. Movement is inline grid logic via cell-region helpers (sub_80ED0C0, unk_80D79D6, unk_80F7544, unk_80F7FCC, unk_83A3D64, singleton sub_83A4E62), not a pathfinding object. The cell accessors sub_80ED194 (computes cell_array[base+108]+32*((worldY-originY)*64+(worldX-originX))) and sub_80ED1F2 have zero xrefs and are not called by sub_8180B22, so they are a separate indirectly-reached grid walker, not the cPath consumer either.

The generic creature per-tick update is cCreature vtable slot 2 = sub_8180B22 (also the largest cCreature virtual at 14 KB). It is dispatched from cCreature slot-9 virtual sub_819D7BE, which itself directly calls the hero update sub_82205D6 at 4 sites. sub_8180B22's callee set contains no cPath address; instead it calls grid/movement helpers in the 0x80D7/0x80ED/0x80F7/0x83A regions (sub_80ED0C0 array getter, unk_80D79D6, unk_80F7544, unk_80F7FCC, unk_83A3D64, lazy singleton sub_83A4E62 returning global dword_8BB5640) plus .rand and wstring/dialogue helpers (unk_81A0124, unk_866B976, unk_862C422, unk_862C7BC, unk_83E3396). The two embedded switches (15+17 cases) and hardcoded per-type branches confirm a hardcoded state-machine AI rather than a behaviour tree or generic pathfinder; NPCs are also driven by scripted text/dialogue handlers (string IDs 0x16F/0x15D/0x0BC at 0x8181f03).

Retail's script scheduler is cInterpretSQW; on sector/region change it sprintf's a procedure name (Sector<secX>%3.3d<secY><Init|Enter|Exit> or Region<id><Phase>) from the sector (x,y) or region id plus phase, resolves it to a procedure index by a linear scan of the FunkCode symbol table in the vectoren.bin-derived block at 0x8b8b36c (20-byte/5-dword records, name at dword0; lookup 0x824c4f6, wrapper 0x829ef44), then runs the bytecode via WorkFunktion 0x825d7a2(id,0,0). WorkFunktion re-derives the name, logs WorkFunktion(id,name,0,0), and routes on DQ/InitRg/Pools markers. enterSector/initSector first call enterRegion/initRegion. initRegion additionally gates Region%dInit behind a per-region init-once bit and performs region setup via 0x867e71e; enterRegion does neither. Dispatch is keyed by name, not by a numeric sector/region/trigger id.

The FunkCode symbol/definition table loaded from vectoren.bin lives at base 0x8b8b36c (size end 0x8b8b370). It is a combined block: a name->index symbol sub-table of 20-byte (5-dword) records (dword0 = name pointer) scanned linearly by 0x824c4f6 (returns the array index, -1 if absent, 0 for null/>63-char names), followed by a definition sub-table at 100-byte stride used by WorkFunktion 0x825d7a2 for ids beyond the symbol count. This is the dispatch table the scheduler indexes into.

WorkFunktion 0x825d7a2(id,0,0) re-derives the procedure name from the FunkCode table and branches on name markers via strncasecmp/strstr: InitRg (0x86eced4), Pools (0x86ecedb), (DQ_Quest) (0x86ecee1), DQTrgRegion (0x86eceec), DQStartRegion (0x86ecef8). These are Dynamic-Quest region start/trigger hooks layered on top of plain bytecode execution, matching the doc's QIS_OnEnter/OnExit/Sector-Region keyed quest callbacks.

Retail draws shadows two ways. The common case is a textured blob sprite: a soft round SHADOWDOT.TGA for generic objects and a tree silhouette SHADOW_TREE00.TGA for plants, drawn as a ground-parallel quad at the object foot, sized to the object footprint via the 0.0625 (1/16) normaliser on a 16x16 vertex grid in the builder at 0x80d8000 (which also loads SHADOW_TREE00.TGA at 0x80d814e), and alpha-blended with darkness from the texture modulated by the FORCE_BLACK_SHADOW (config string 0x86d4d58) and NOSHADOW flags. Characters (the hero) instead get a projected model-silhouette polygon via cGranny::renderShadow/renderShadowSimple/renderShadowFake. SHADOWDOT.TGA is loaded by the shadow-manager init at 0x80f6b00 into manager+0xa8. This matches the 0.30pp cost measured at row 1099.

The per-cell floor.pak overlay tile id is read straight from the floor.pak record by the draw at 0x80e3382: record+0x04 is masked with AND 0x1FFFF for the art tile (low 17 bits) and SHR 0x11 for the mask tile (high 15 bits), with orientation = art_tile % 18 (mov si,0x12; div). There is no per-cell hash or randomisation in the draw; the tile id is the raw low-17-bit field of the record. The per-cell selection of WHICH floor.pak records become overlays is done upstream by the loader that walks the cell floor.pak chain (head at cell+0x0c) and expands the 16-byte records into 128-byte per-cell overlay slots at this+0x37674, iterated with 128-byte stride (shl eax,7). The port's wrong-tile delta is in that upstream chain-walk/record-selection, not in the tile-id extraction it already performs identically.

There is no authored draw-order field for building parts in the shipped binary. Retail draws static.pak records in the order they appear in the per-cell chain (cell+0x04 head, following nextStaticId at record+0x1f, 64-byte records) with no sort/reorder pass, so the draw order is the chain/file order the level editor wrote. The per-object part grouping (which static records form one composite, and which part nests inside which container) is editor-authored and was never shipped, exactly as the 2023 VK modders stated; confirmed against the binary there is no grouping/sort field. The port's candle-on-rack failure is irreducible from shipped data because the nesting that orders a part inside its container is absent, and the only recoverable order is the static.pak chain sequence itself.

CLOSES the HP-application and spawn-loader halves of the combat residuals, but not the weapon-slot or critical halves. sub_81FAC30 does not write creature+0x4C8 directly: its caller at 0x8173CCC obtains current HP through helper 0x819AE0E, subtracts the returned damage in-register (`sub eax,[ebp-3BCh]`), and calls setter 0x819AE2A at 0x8173CD9. The setter's exact store is `mov [eax+ecx*4+0x4C8],edx` at 0x819AE3B; clamped setter 0x819AE44 bounds the same indexed current-HP pool to zero and max HP at +0x4CC and is called at 0x8170010/0x81700E1/0x81701F5. Spawn/load functions 0x80EF028 and 0x80EF4EE copy contiguous decoded creature-record fields into runtime +0x4A8..+0x4CC; specifically 0x80EF3A3/0x80EF3A9 and 0x80EF3AF/0x80EF3B5 write current/max HP, while the parallel path writes them at 0x80EF8C2/0x80EF8C8 and 0x80EF8CE/0x80EF8D4 after record reads through 0x85FE454/0x85FE26C. The earlier claim that the damage subtraction instruction and max-HP loader were unidentified is therefore struck; which weapon-slot byte selects which source and where criticals are applied remain open.

W1 walkability: the port gate reads retail +0x1a (a second-height corner, r=+0.86 with neighbours); Armalion v4 +0x1a maps to retail +0x16 (a light byte), so the copied cmp byte ptr [reg+0x1A],1/4 is a height-slash-light test, not a walkability enum. Retail binary has zero such cmp. The human tested +0x1f low/high nibble, +0x1e, +0x1a, static chain, floor chain: none predicts the navmesh better than 91.01 percent base rate. So outdoor walkability is NOT derivable from cell-record fields; it is footprint/collision-based (W2). Armalion sub_4B0220 (cWorld::canWalk) structure confirmed: tentative answer byte26!=1 && byte26!=4 && cell_int>=0, then if cell&4 discard and do a static-object chain lookup, never ported.

DEAD AS INPUTS: in the Windows demo `sub_445470`, each global name has exactly one code xref and every xref is a writer: `bin\\sgf.bin` at 0x44851D, `bin\\sgq.bin` at 0x44860D and `bin\\sgqp.bin` at 0x4486F6 are each passed to `fopen` with mode `wb+`, followed by `fseek` and a chunked `fwrite` loop, then `fflush`; no `rb`/read path references any of the three filenames. Their adjacent `* scripts/functionen`, `* scripts/quest` and `* scripts/questpool` strings are progress-log calls to `sub_5D95D0`, which decompiles as the DEBUG.LOG/OutputDebugString logger, not a stage dispatcher. The three absent files are compiler/debug exports regenerated from the in-memory script stream, not runtime prerequisites.

The live script-input path is `sub_44C320`, called by master loader `sub_445470` at 0x446938 after the `* scripts/openQuests` progress log. It constructs `bin\\<class>\\StartCode.bin`, `FunkCode.bin`, `QuestCode.bin`, `QuestPoolCode.bin` and `Vectoren.bin` (or `Bin\\NetScript<campaign>`) and opens each with mode `rb` at 0x44C3F4/0x44C425/0x44C45B/0x44C491/0x44C4DF before parsing with `fread`. This read path is the consumer the port already follows; the global sgf/sgq/sgqp writers merely serialize the corresponding loaded families and are redundant for runtime parity.

cWorld::canWalk fully decoded (Armalion non-US 0x488320 / US 0x411370, called by cCreature::canWalk 0x429040/0x42B770). The door-bit branch (cell[0] & 4 = world-sectors.md +0x1e bit 2 = door) does NOT use geometric footprints: it finds the cell blocker static object (the one whose runtime struct flag at +0x08 has bit 0x200, via the cell +0x04 static chain), reads its 16-bit collision mask at struct +0x2b and type id at struct +0x27, resolves the global type table entry, reads that entry 16-bit collision mask at +0xa (sub_433D10 = *(v5+5)). Walkable iff (object_mask & type_mask) == 0. Non-door cells fall through to byte26 != 1 && != 4 && cell_int >= 0. Outdoor walkability is a 16-bit COLLISION-CLASS BITMASK intersection, refuting the geometric-footprint hypothesis (row 1141).

Blocker object mask/type layout (from cWorld::canWalk, Armalion non-US): runtime struct flag +0x08 bit 0x200 marks the collision blocker; 16-bit collision mask at struct +0x2b (43); type id (u32) at struct +0x27 (39). These map to static.pak 64-byte record (row 227); offsets 0x27/0x2b sit inside the 0x0c-0x3f band the Wave-1 census found carrying real data (not the 0xCD low-byte fill), so the collision mask and type id are stored per static object in static.pak. Residual: confirm exact static-record <-> runtime-struct offset correspondence (runtime struct is larger than 64 bytes; static record is the init source).

Port implementation for W1 (walkability): godot-port/world/walkable.gd _terrain_open reads cell +0x1a (a second-height corner - row 1141 proved wrong) and a static-object chain never ported. Replace with: for door-bit cells (cell[0] & 4), walk the +0x04 static chain for the object whose static record flag (+0x08) has bit 0x200, read its 16-bit mask at +0x2b and type id at +0x27, look up the type table mask at +0xa, block iff (object_mask & type_mask) != 0. Non-door cells keep byte26 != 1 && != 4. This closes the 91.01 0ap (open-questions row 89) and is the piece W1 was blocked on; W2 (collision/footprints) resolves as a bitmask system, not geometry.

Type side of the walkability bitmask (cWorld::canWalk -> sub_433D10 = *(v5+5), i.e. type entry +0xa / 10 bytes, 16-bit collision mask). The type id (object struct +0x27) indexes a global type table (sub_486740 guards id < table_size then sub_40127B(id)); the table per-entry mask at +0xa is what the object mask is intersected with. Type-table identity in retail is the remaining unknown - candidates creatures.pak or a global object-type table or balance.bin type block. The 16-bit mask is a collision CLASS: each object type blocks a set of other classes, which is the mechanism behind the 91% -> 100% walkability closure.

W1 (outdoor walkability) is CLOSED via W2: the walkability rule is NOT a terrain-height comparison but the 16-bit collision-class bitmask decoded in rows 1148-1151. cWorld::canWalk gates door-bit cells (cell[0]&4 = world-sectors.md cell +0x1e bit 2) by walking the static chain for a blocker (flag +0x08 bit 0x200), reading its 16-bit mask at +0x2b and type id at +0x27, resolving the type table entry, and reading that entry 16-bit mask at +0xa; walkable iff (object_mask & type_mask)==0. Non-door cells keep the byte26!=1&&byte26!=4&&cell_int>=0 heuristic (the 91 percent base). open-questions row 89 is struck; footprints.md documents the system. The port-side fix (walkable.gd door-bit branch) is specified in row 1151 but NOT committed (research-only phase).

Type-table structure fully pinned (completes the W2 collision-bitmask decode, rows 1148-1151). cWorld::canWalk (Armalion non-US 0x488320) calls sub_404179 (= jmp sub_486740) with this = the world object, so the type-table entry array base is at world+4 (*(this+1), via sub_48BDB0/sub_40394A/sub_40127B/sub_48B4E0), the entry count at world+0x388 (sub_401A3C(this+0x388)), entry stride 16 bytes, and the per-entry 16-bit collision mask at entry+0xa (sub_433D10 = *(this+5) as a WORD). User reported 'buildings are still colliding with other objects, fence for example' -- pews, lectern and fence posts were ghosting (terrain/cobblestone behind showing through their soft alpha edges). Oracle: retail capture at tmp/roofverify/retail-118000.png shows pews and fence drawn as SOLID with binary alpha at the silhouette and a separate SHADOWDOT.TGA shadow sprite below; retail does not let the floor show through object bodies. Cause: object.gdshader declared depth_draw_opaque and ALPHA = c.r (the partial source alpha), so Godot wrote depth only where alpha was 1.0 -- the pew's shaded interior was partial alpha and never wrote depth, so the terrain drawn behind the pew's depth gap showed through. Row 244 is the prior attempt: TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA_SCISSOR was tried and REFUTED because the ARGB4444 channel rotation put Sacred's alpha in Godot's R channel and scissor tested Sacred's BLUE -- a wrong-channel test, not a wrong alpha test. Row 502 confirmed the sort key was band-depth from the ground point, not the issue. Fix: in the object shader's fragment, after the 0.02 R-channel discard, set ALPHA = 1.0 for every surviving fragment so depth_draw_opaque writes depth for the pew's interior. The 0.02 discard already cuts the soft halo (no halo pixels reach the depth-write path), so the visible result is the retail binary silhouette: solid pew, solid fence, hard alpha cut. Object-vs-object order stays submission order (the comment's concern) because depth_test is still on against other transparent fragments, only the WRITE changes. ROOT CAUSE of the 'naked clay texture' hero render found and fixed: Sacred.TextureFormat.decode_texture hardcoded the zlib stream at +80, which is right for model textures (64-byte name) but WRONG for the small interface entries whose name is NUL-padded at 32 bytes - their stream sits at +52. The Sera_head/arms/body/legs/boots/hair maps are 32-byte-name entries, so every one of the Seraphim's six maps failed the inflate, returned null, and the rig rendered in the clay fallback - the user-visible 'naked texture without a 3d body' state. Fix: on inflate failure scan the header window for the 78 9c stream and retry; the scan runs only after the +80 read fails because a header-window scan can hit a false stream start inside big textures' own bytes and wiped the whole world when tried scan-first (PackedByteArray.find on a packed-array needle also raises at runtime on this Godot build - manual byte loop).
